📚 Subject: Cloud Computing & Systems Topic: Virtualization & VMs Sheet No: 01

🖥️ Virtualization & Virtual Machines — Detailed Notes

Clean, Exam & Interview-Friendly Revision Notes

KEY TOPIC

1. Introduction to Virtualization

Virtualization is one of the most commonly used concepts in the IT industry, especially in:

✔ Cloud Computing
✔ AWS
✔ DevOps
✔ Data Centers
✔ Server Management
✔ Software Dev & Testing
Simple Definition:
Virtualization is the process of creating virtual versions of computing resources such as computers, servers, storage, or networks using software.

👉 Instead of purchasing a separate physical computer for every requirement, we can use one physical machine to create multiple Virtual Machines (VMs).

2. Understanding a Physical Computer

Let's first understand a normal laptop or desktop. A physical computer generally contains:

Hardware Components:
  • CPU → Processes instructions
  • RAM → Temporary memory
  • Hard Disk / SSD → Permanent storage
  • Network interface
  • Other hardware components
Operating System (OS):

Above the hardware, we install an OS:
• Windows   • Linux   • macOS

The operating system manages the hardware and provides an environment for applications to run.

Traditional Architecture (Without Virtualization)
Applications
↓ (runs on)
Operating System (Windows / Linux)
↓ (manages)
Hardware (CPU + RAM + Storage)
SCENARIO

3. Why Do We Need Virtualization?

Imagine you are a software engineer developing an application. You may need to test your application on different operating systems: Windows, Ubuntu, Red Hat Linux, and other Linux distributions.

Without Virtualization:

Computer 1 → Windows | Computer 2 → Ubuntu | Computer 3 → Red Hat | Computer 4 → Another OS

❌ Expensive
❌ Difficult to maintain
❌ Requires more physical space
❌ Requires more hardware
With Virtualization:

You can use one physical computer and create multiple virtual machines!

✔ 1 Physical Computer runs multiple OS
✔ Scalable, cost-effective & easy
✔ Instant start/stop & cleanup

Therefore, one physical machine can run multiple operating systems simultaneously.

Handwritten Lecture Notes Page 1 of 8
📚 Subject: Cloud Computing & Systems Topic: Hypervisor & Virtual Machines Sheet No: 02
CORE CONCEPT

4. What is a Hypervisor?

The virtualization layer that enables us to create and manage Virtual Machines is called a Hypervisor.

Definition:
A Hypervisor is software (or firmware/software layer) that creates, runs, and manages Virtual Machines. It allows multiple virtual machines to share the physical hardware resources of a computer.

Main Responsibilities of a Hypervisor:

• Create Virtual Machines
• Allocate CPU resources
• Allocate RAM
• Allocate storage
• Manage Virtual Machines
• Start / stop VMs
• Isolate VMs from each other
• Allow multiple OS on same physical PC

5. Example — Oracle VirtualBox

One common example of a hypervisor is: Oracle VirtualBox. It is commonly used for learning and testing virtualization on personal computers.

Setup Flow: Physical Computer ➔ Windows (Host) ➔ VirtualBox ➔ (VM 1: Ubuntu & VM 2: Linux)
No OS Replacement Needed!

You can run a Linux-based VM on your Windows computer without replacing Windows.

HOW IT WORKS

6. How Does a Hypervisor Work?

The key concept is: A hypervisor shares the physical hardware resources among multiple Virtual Machines.

Resource Allocation Example (Physical ➔ Virtual)
Physical Computer
RAM: 8 GB
Storage: 100 GB
➔ [ Hypervisor ] ➔
VM 1: 2 GB RAM | 20 GB Storage
VM 2: 2 GB RAM | 10 GB Storage

*The remaining resources can be used by the host system or allocated elsewhere.

⚠️ Important: The resources assigned to the VM ultimately come from the physical hardware. A VM doesn't magically create physical RAM or storage.

7. What is a Virtual Machine?

A Virtual Machine (VM) is a software-based representation of a physical computer. It behaves like an independent computer even though it runs on another machine.

• Virtual CPU (vCPU)
• Virtual RAM (vRAM)
• Virtual Hard Disk (vDisk)
• Virtual Network Interface (vNIC)
• Operating System & Applications

8. Why "Virtual" Machine?

A physical computer actually exists as physical silicon hardware.
A Virtual Machine is created using software.

Key Takeaway: A VM behaves like a computer, but it is created using software rather than being a separate physical machine.

9. Virtual Machine Example

Suppose your laptop runs Windows and you want to learn Linux. Instead of buying another laptop:

Your Laptop (Windows) ➔ Hypervisor ➔ [ Ubuntu VM ➔ Linux ]

Now you can use Ubuntu inside your Windows computer. You can also create another VM simultaneously!

TESTING BENEFIT

10. Virtualization and Software Testing

Virtualization is extremely useful for software developers and testers. Suppose an application needs testing across Windows, Ubuntu, and Linux:

One Physical Computer ➔ Hypervisor ➔ [ Windows VM | Ubuntu VM | Linux VM ]

The developer can seamlessly test the application in different environments.

✅ No need for multiple physical computers
✅ Easy to create testing environments
✅ Easy to delete / recreate VMs
✅ Reduces hardware costs
✅ Useful for continuous development and testing workflows
CRITICAL EXAM POINT

11. Isolation — An Important Feature

One of the most important benefits of virtualization is isolation. Each VM generally operates in its own isolated environment.

Example Scenario:
Suppose: VM1 → Testing environment | VM2 → Development environment.
If something goes wrong or you install something problematic inside VM1, it generally doesn't directly affect the OS or applications running inside VM2!

Isolation makes virtualization ideal for testing, development, security boundaries, and multi-tenant environments.

*Note: Isolation is strong, but it isn't an absolute guarantee against every possible failure or hardware vulnerability.

12. Host Operating System & Guest Operating System

In some virtualization setups, the physical computer already has an operating system installed:

Host OS:

The operating system installed directly on the physical computer.
Example: Windows (on your laptop).

Host OS = OS of the physical / main machine.
Guest OS:

The operating system installed inside the Virtual Machine.
Example: Ubuntu Linux (inside VM).

Guest OS = OS running inside a VM.

13. Types of Hypervisors

Type 1 (Bare Metal) & Type 2 (Hosted)
TYPE 2

14. Type 2 — Hosted Hypervisor

A Type 2 Hypervisor runs on top of an existing host operating system. It is installed just like normal application software.

Architecture Stack:
Virtual Machines (Guest OS + Apps)
↓
Hypervisor (e.g. VirtualBox)
↓
Host Operating System (Windows)
↓
Physical Hardware
Common Use Cases:
  • Learning & Academic practice
  • Local development & debugging
  • Testing multi-platform applications
  • Running Linux on Windows
  • Running Windows on Linux / macOS
  • Personal computers & laptops
Handwritten Lecture Notes Page 3 of 8
📚 Subject: Cloud Computing & Systems Topic: Type 1 Hypervisors & Full Stack Architecture Sheet No: 04
ENTERPRISE STANDARD

15. Type 1 — Bare Metal Hypervisor

A Type 1 Hypervisor runs directly on the physical hardware. There is no traditional host operating system sitting underneath it.

👉 This is why it is called a Bare Metal Hypervisor: because the hypervisor software is installed directly onto the raw physical server hardware.
COMMON CONFUSION

16. How Can Type 1 Work Without an Operating System?

A common beginner question! A Type 1 hypervisor doesn't require desktop Windows or Ubuntu. Instead, the hypervisor itself acts as a specialized operating layer with built-in low-level kernel drivers to:

✔ Access & schedule CPU
✔ Manage RAM memory directly
✔ Control physical storage disks
✔ Handle low-level networking

You can think of it as an ultra-lean specialized OS designed strictly for virtualization efficiency.

17. Examples of Type 1 Hypervisors

VMware ESXi

Widely used in enterprise enterprise data centers globally.

Microsoft Hyper-V

Core virtualization in Windows Server infrastructure.

Citrix Hypervisor

Optimized for server and desktop virtual infrastructure.

*Cloud providers (AWS, Azure, GCP) use custom bare-metal hypervisor architectures to efficiently provide multi-tenant compute resources.

Complete Architectural Comparison
25. Complete Architecture — Type 2 (Hosted)
Applications (Inside VM)
Guest OS (Ubuntu / Linux)
Virtual Hardware (vCPU | vRAM | vDisk | vNIC)
Hypervisor (e.g., Oracle VirtualBox)
Host OS (Windows / macOS)
Physical Hardware (CPU | RAM | SSD)
26. Complete Architecture — Type 1 (Bare Metal)
Applications
Guest OSs (Linux VM | Windows VM | Linux VM)
Virtual Hardware Layer
Type 1 Hypervisor (VMware ESXi, Hyper-V)
No Host OS Layer (Direct Hardware)
Physical Server Hardware (CPU | RAM | Storage)

📚 Subject: Cloud Computing & Systems Topic: Cloud Virtualization & Benefits Sheet No: 05
CLOUD FOUNDATION

18. Virtualization in Cloud Computing

Virtualization is the core foundational technology powering modern cloud providers like AWS, Azure & GCP.

Large Physical Server ➔ Hypervisor ➔ [ VM (User A) | VM (User B) | VM (User C) ]

A large physical server is partitioned into multiple isolated virtual computing environments without customers needing to buy servers.

19. Why Do Cloud Providers Use Virtualization?

1. Better Resource Utilization: Physical resources are shared across thousands of customers simultaneously.
2. Scalability: Users can instantly scale up CPU/RAM as app traffic surges.
3. Cost Efficiency: Pay-as-you-go instead of capital datacenter expenditure.
4. Strict Multi-Tenant Isolation: Users cannot view or interfere with other tenants' data.
5. Flexibility: VMs can be launched, resized, snapshotted, migrated, and destroyed in seconds.

20. Virtualization in Organizations

Large enterprises run private on-premise data centers. Instead of a dedicated box per role:

Application Server Database Server Dev Environment Testing Environment Internal Tools Monitoring System

Far more cost and power-efficient than purchasing 6 separate physical server boxes!

EXAM ESSENTIAL

21. Major Benefits of Virtualization

1. Cost Reduction 💰

Fewer physical machines needed. Drastically reduces: Hardware costs, Datacenter real estate space, Power consumption, Cooling bills, Maintenance staff.

2. Better Resource Utilization

Traditional servers average only 10-15% CPU load. Virtualization stacks workloads to achieve 70-80% hardware efficiency.

3. Scalability

Dynamic resource adjustments: 2 GB RAM ➔ 4 GB RAM ➔ 8 GB RAM in clicks without physical upgrades.

4. Flexibility

Run diverse environments concurrently: VM1 (Ubuntu), VM2 (Windows), VM3 (Dev), VM4 (Testing).

5. Isolation

Crashes or virus infections in one VM remain quarantined and do not bring down neighboring machines.

6. Easy Testing & 7. Management

Spin up sandbox VMs, test destructive code, revert with snapshots. Centralized dashboard control.

22. Virtualization vs Physical Machines

Feature Physical Machine Virtual Machine
Hardware Dedicated physical hardware Uses virtualized hardware layer
Creation Requires manual physical setup Can be created instantly through software
Cost Generally higher capex Generally lower per workload
OS Usually one primary OS Multiple VMs run different OSs simultaneously
Scalability Physical replacement/upgrade needed Resources can often be adjusted dynamically
Isolation Physical separation boundary Software-based logical isolation
Testing Less flexible & slower Very flexible (easy snap & restore)
Resource Sharing Limited / Single tenant High multi-workload sharing
FAVORITE INTERVIEW Q

23. Type 1 vs Type 2 Hypervisor

Feature Type 1 Hypervisor Type 2 Hypervisor
Other Name Bare Metal Hosted
Runs On Directly on bare hardware On top of Host Operating System
Host OS Required? No traditional host OS Yes (needs Windows/Linux/macOS)
Performance Generally better for servers (near-native) More overhead due to Host OS middle layer
Common Use Enterprise Data centers / Cloud / Servers Desktop / Personal Lab / Dev / Testing
Example VMware ESXi, Hyper-V, KVM Oracle VirtualBox, VMware Workstation
⚡ Easy Way to Remember:
Type 1: Hardware ➔ Hypervisor ➔ VM
Type 2: Hardware ➔ Host OS ➔ Hypervisor ➔ VM

24. Important Terminology Quick-Glance

Host Machine: The physical computer/server running virtualization.
Host OS: The OS installed on the physical machine in Type 2.
Hypervisor: Software layer creating & managing virtual machines.
Virtual Machine: Software-based computer running on physical box.
Guest OS: The OS installed and running inside the VM.
Virtual Resources: Virtualized vCPU, vRAM, vDisk & vNIC.

PRACTICAL SCENARIO

27. Real-World Example Walkthrough

Scenario: You have a laptop with 8 GB RAM + 100 GB SSD + Windows. You want to learn Linux.
• Without Virtualization: You would need to buy another physical computer.
• With Virtualization: You install a hypervisor on your existing Windows setup:

Laptop (8GB RAM, 100GB SSD, Windows) ➔ Hypervisor ➔ [ Ubuntu VM (2GB RAM, 20GB Disk) + Another VM (2GB RAM, 10GB Disk) ]

🎉 Now you can learn and test Linux without spending money on another laptop!

28. Virtualization vs Cloud Computing

These two concepts are intimately related but are not identical:

Virtualization:

A foundational technology that allows physical resources to be abstracted into virtual slices.

Cloud Computing:

A broader business & service model delivering on-demand computing over the network/Internet.

💡 Easy Analogy: Virtualization = How resources are sliced & isolated | Cloud = How resources are packaged & billed as a service!
⭐ EXAM SUMMARY

Key Concepts to Remember

1. Virtualization: Creating software versions of resources.
2. Virtual Machine: Software computer on physical hardware.
3. Hypervisor: Creates, allocates & manages VMs.
4. Host: Physical machine running virtualization.
5. Guest: The VM and its internal OS.
6. Type 1: HW ➔ Hypervisor ➔ VM
7. Type 2: HW ➔ Host OS ➔ Hypervisor ➔ VM
8. Isolation: VMs operate in separate sandboxes.
9. Sharing: Multiple VMs pool CPU, RAM, & storage.
🔥 ONE-LINE MEMORY TRICK

“Hypervisor divides physical resources ➔ creates VMs ➔ VMs run Guest OSs ➔ multiple workloads share one physical machine.”

🧠 Quick Revision — 30 Seconds Summary

• Virtualization allows multiple virtual computers on one physical machine.
• A VM contains virtual CPU, RAM, disk, network, and an operating system.
• A Hypervisor creates and controls these VMs (Type 1 Bare Metal vs Type 2 Hosted).
• Core benefits: Cost efficiency, Resource sharing, Isolation, Flexibility, Scalability, and Easier testing.
• Cloud giants like AWS rely on bare-metal virtualization to deliver multi-tenant compute globally.

🎯 Top Interview Questions & Exact Answers

Q1. What is virtualization?

Ans: A technology allowing us to create virtual versions of computing resources, such as servers or computers, using software.

Q2. What is a Virtual Machine?

Ans: A software-based computer that runs on physical infrastructure and has virtual CPU, RAM, storage, networking, and an OS.

Q3. What is a hypervisor?

Ans: Software or virtualization layer that creates, runs, and manages Virtual Machines.

Q4. Difference between Type 1 & Type 2?

Ans: Type 1 runs directly on bare hardware; Type 2 runs on top of a host operating system.

Q5. Give an example of Type 2 hypervisor.

Ans: Oracle VirtualBox.

Q6. Give an example of Type 1 hypervisor.

Ans: VMware ESXi.

Q7. Why is it useful in cloud computing?

Ans: Divides infrastructure into isolated environments for better resource utilization, flexibility, scalability, and cost efficiency.

Q8. Difference between Host OS & Guest OS?

Ans: Host OS runs directly on the physical computer; Guest OS runs inside the Virtual Machine.

☁️ Cloud Computing — Detailed Notes

Structured, Comprehensive, Exam & Interview-Ready Study Guide

CORE DEFINITION

1. What is Cloud Computing?

One-Line Definition:
Cloud computing is the on-demand delivery of IT resources over the Internet with pay-as-you-go pricing.

In simple words: Cloud computing means using computing resources over the Internet instead of owning and maintaining all the physical infrastructure yourself.

These resources can include:
✔ Servers / Compute
✔ Storage
✔ Databases
✔ Networking
✔ Software
✔ Containers
✔ Serverless computing
✔ Machine Learning services
✔ Monitoring
✔ Logging
✔ User management
✔ Security services

2. What Does "Cloud" Actually Mean?

When we say Cloud, we are generally referring to computing infrastructure and services that are provided remotely through a network, usually the Internet.

Instead of:
Your Company ➔ Own Physical Servers ➔ Own Storage ➔ Own Networking ➔ Own Maintenance
You can use:
Internet ➔ Cloud Provider ➔ Compute + Storage + Database + Networking + Security + etc.

You access these resources when required.

3. Cloud Computing Example

Think about services such as Google Drive / Google Photos.

You can upload:

• Photos
• Videos
• Documents
• Files
You don't need to purchase and maintain the physical storage infrastructure yourself. You simply access your data through the Internet. This is an example of using a cloud-based service.
PRICING

4. Pay-As-You-Go Pricing 💰

One of the most important concepts in cloud computing is: Pay only for the resources/services you use. Instead of purchasing a large physical server upfront, you rent resources.

Traditional Model:
Buy Server ➔ Large Initial Investment ➔ Maintain Hardware ➔ Pay Electricity ➔ Pay Cooling ➔ Pay Maintenance
Cloud Model:
Choose Required Service ➔ Use It ➔ Pay According to Usage

This is commonly called a pay-as-you-go or usage-based pricing model. Important: Exact pricing models vary by service; not every cloud service is billed in exactly the same way.

5. Cloud Service Providers (CSPs)

Companies that provide cloud computing services are called: Cloud Service Providers (CSPs).

Amazon Web Services (AWS) Microsoft Azure Google Cloud

These companies operate huge amounts of infrastructure in data centers around the world.

6. What Do Cloud Providers Actually Have?

Massive physical infrastructure containing: Physical servers, CPUs, RAM, Storage systems, Networking equipment, Data centers, Security infrastructure, Databases, Specialized hardware.

Cloud Provider ➔ Large Data Centers ➔ [ Compute (VMs) | Storage (Data) | Networking (Connectivity) ]
FOUNDATION

7. Role of Virtualization in Cloud Computing

Remember the previous topic: Virtualization. Cloud providers can use virtualization technologies to efficiently allocate physical resources to multiple customers.

Large Physical Server ➔ Hypervisor ➔ [ VM1 (Customer A) | VM2 (Customer B) | VM3 (Customer C) ]

Instead of giving an entire physical server to one customer, resources can be divided into virtual environments.

✔ Better resource utilization ✔ Scalability ✔ Flexibility ✔ Isolation ✔ Efficient infrastructure usage

📚 Subject: Cloud Computing & Systems Topic: Real-World Case, Hosting Challenges & Benefits Sheet No: 02
SCENARIO STUDY

8. Real-World Use Case — Starting an E-Commerce Website

Let's take a simple example: Suppose Raju wants to start an e-commerce business. He has developed an e-commerce website. Now he needs to deploy it and make it available to users.
At first, it sounds simple: "I just need to put my website online." But a production application has many requirements!

CRITICAL REALITY

9. Challenges of Hosting an Application Yourself

If Raju decides to build and host everything himself, he may need to handle:

1. Servers: Needs physical or virtual servers to run the application.
2. 24×7 Availability: Website should ideally remain available continuously without downtime.
3. Networking: Users from the Internet need to reach the application reliably.
4. Security: E-commerce handles sensitive data; security becomes extremely important.
5. Performance: Website should respond quickly even when many users access it simultaneously.
6. Backup: Important application data needs appropriate backup and disaster recovery mechanisms.
7. Scaling: Sudden surge of thousands or millions of users requires additional dynamic resources.
8. Monitoring: Continuous health, uptime, and performance metrics tracking are mandatory.
9. Maintenance: Patching OS, firmware, hardware, security updates, and administration.
10. Human Resources: Needs full-time engineers for servers, networks, databases, security, backup.

10. The Traditional Infrastructure Problem

Raju could purchase physical infrastructure, but it requires massive upfront capital:

Physical Servers + Storage + Networking + Data Center + Power + Cooling + Security + Maintenance + IT Staff

For a small business, this can be painfully expensive and complicated.

11. Cloud as an Alternative

Instead of purchasing and maintaining everything himself, Raju can use a cloud provider such as AWS or Azure. He rents the services:

Raju's Application ➔ Cloud Platform ➔ Compute + Storage + Database + Networking + Security + Monitoring

Allows him to focus on business and app code rather than building infrastructure from scratch.

INTUITIVE ANALOGY

12. Car Rental Analogy 🚗

A simple way to understand cloud computing is to compare it with renting a car for travel from Point A to Point B:

Option 1 — Buy a Car:
Buy Car ➔ Pay Large Amount ➔ Maintenance, Insurance, Fuel, Repairs, Parking.
(High initial cost, permanent overhead)
Option 2 — Rent a Car:
Need Car ➔ Rent Car ➔ Use It ➔ Pay According to Agreement.
(Zero upfront capital, pay as you need)

👉 Cloud computing follows the same idea: Instead of owning all the infrastructure, you use resources provided by a cloud provider.

13. Major Benefits of Cloud Computing

1. Lower Upfront Cost 💰: No expensive hardware purchases before starting.
2. Scalability 📈: Resources expand effortlessly as user traffic grows.
3. Flexibility: Select only the precise services and resources actually needed.
4. Faster Deployment ⚡: Provision servers in minutes, not months.
5. Global Availability 🌍: Infrastructure across geographic regions closer to users.
6. Reduced Infrastructure Management: Cloud provider manages underlying hardware.
Shared Responsibility Model: Customer and cloud provider share security roles (covered in depth in AWS).

14. Scalability in Cloud Computing

Suppose Raju's website traffic surges over time:

Initially:
100 users/day ➔ Later:
10,000 users/day ➔ Eventually:
1,00,000 users/day
Small Resources ➔ Growing Business ➔ More Compute + Storage + DB Capacity ➔ Large Application

Cloud platforms make it seamless to increase resources as demand grows. Major reason businesses adopt cloud!

CORE TAXONOMY

15. Cloud Service Models

Cloud services are commonly categorized into three major service models based on levels of responsibility:

1. IaaS
Infrastructure as a Service
2. PaaS
Platform as a Service
3. SaaS
Software as a Service

16. IaaS — Infrastructure as a Service

MOST FLEXIBLE

Full Form: Infrastructure as a Service. Provides fundamental computing infrastructure: Virtual machines, storage, networking, compute resources.

Simple Idea: Imagine renting a blank computer. You receive the basic infrastructure, but you are responsible for configuring much of the environment.

You Manage:

Applications, Operating System, Configuration, Data, Some Security.

Cloud Provider:

Physical Hardware, Data Center, Networking Infrastructure, Virtualization.

17. Ice Cream Parlour Analogy — IaaS 🍦:
Imagine you rent an empty shop. You get basic physical space, but you must arrange painting, furniture, refrigerator, ice cream machines, decoration, products, and equipment.
Result: Maximum flexibility, but more management responsibility!
18. IaaS — Key Characteristics:
✔ High flexibility & More control
✔ More configuration options
✔ Suitable for custom environments
❌ More management responsibility
Example Concept: Virtual server choosing CPU, RAM, SSD, OS (e.g. Amazon EC2).

19. PaaS — Platform as a Service

DEV FAVORITE

Full Form: Platform as a Service. Provides a ready-to-use platform/environment for developing and deploying applications without managing underlying OS and hardware.

You Mainly Manage:

Application code & Application Data.

Provider Manages More:

Runtime, OS, Infrastructure, Hardware, Networking.

20. Ice Cream Parlour Analogy — PaaS 🍦:
Instead of an empty shop, you receive a shop that already has furniture, refrigerator, ice cream machine, display counter, and basic setup. You mainly bring your ice cream/product to sell!
Remember: PaaS = Platform is already prepared; developers focus primarily on their applications.

21. SaaS — Software as a Service

READY TO USE

Full Form: Software as a Service. Provides a complete software application to the end user over the Internet. You don't install software, manage servers, manage OS, or maintain infrastructure. You simply access and use it.

22. Ice Cream Parlour Analogy — SaaS 🍦:
Instead of renting a shop, you get a fully operational ice cream vending machine! Everything is set up. Customer inserts money ➔ selects ice cream ➔ receives ice cream. Very little infrastructure management for the customer.
Remember: SaaS = Ready-to-use software delivered over the Internet.
23. SaaS Examples:

Common examples include cloud-based applications such as:

• Gmail
• Google Docs
• Microsoft 365
• Salesforce
• Dropbox

Accessed via browser/app rather than managing underlying servers.

24. IaaS vs PaaS vs SaaS

Feature IaaS PaaS SaaS
Full Form Infrastructure as a Service Platform as a Service Software as a Service
Control High Medium Low
Responsibility High Medium Low
Main Focus Infrastructure Application Development Using Software

And remember: IaaS = You manage more | PaaS = Provider manages more | SaaS = Provider manages almost everything you need to use the application.

25. Cloud Deployment Models: Public, Private & Hybrid

Categorized according to how infrastructure is deployed, isolated, and consumed.

PUBLIC

26. Public Cloud ☁️

Definition: Cloud resources provided by a cloud provider on infrastructure shared among multiple customers. Customers don't own physical datacenters. (AWS, Azure, GCP).

27. Public Transport Analogy 🚌:
Think of a public bus: Many passengers share the bus infrastructure. Similarly, customers share cloud infrastructure while their resources remain logically isolated.
✅ Cost-effective & Highly scalable
✅ Easy to provision | No datacenter ownership
PRIVATE

28. Private Cloud 🔐

Definition: Cloud environment dedicated entirely to a single organization. Operated on-premises or by a third-party provider for ultimate control.

29. Rental Car Analogy 🚗:
Renting a car exclusively for your family—not shared with others. Provides dedicated control & compliance.
✅ Greater control, customization & security
❌ More expensive, complex & heavy management
HYBRID

30. Hybrid Cloud 🔄 (Private + Public)

Private Cloud + Public Cloud = Hybrid Cloud
Definition: Combines private and public clouds so workloads/data move between both based on business needs.
31. Commute Analogy 🚗🚌: Point A ➔ Public Transport ➔ Point B ➔ Private Car ➔ Point C. Combining two transport methods!
32. Example of Hybrid Cloud:
• Private Cloud: Sensitive core database & compliance records.
• Public Cloud: Scalable web frontend & peak computational traffic.
33. Public vs Private vs Hybrid Cloud

Users Multiple customers One organization Mixed
Cost / Scalability Generally lower / Excellent Generally higher / Depends Depends / Excellent

Example AWS Enterprise private cloud Private + AWS

BEYOND VIRTUAL MACHINES

34. Other Cloud Services

A common misconception is: "Cloud means only Virtual Machines." ❌ This is incorrect! Cloud platforms provide an enormous ecosystem of specialized managed services:
Compute Services 🖥️:

Running applications: Virtual Machines, Containers, Serverless computing.

Storage Services 💾:

Files, images, videos, backups, and app data objects.

Database Services 🗄️:

Relational DBs, NoSQL DBs, and massive Data Warehouses.

Networking Services 🌐:

Virtual networks, routing, load balancing, DNS, firewalls & connectivity.

Container Services 📦:

Docker-based workloads, container orchestration & clusters.

Serverless Computing ⚡:

Run code without managing servers; provider handles infrastructure.

Machine Learning 🤖:

Model development, training, deployment, and vision/speech APIs.

Identity & Access (IAM) 🔐:

Controlling users, roles, granular permissions, and resource security.

Monitoring & Logging 📊:

Tracking apps, servers, metrics, performance, errors, logs & alerts.

EXAM ESSENTIAL

35. Major Advantages of Cloud Computing

💰 1. Cost Efficiency:

Reduced need for large upfront capital expenditure on hardware.

📈 2. Scalability:

Resources scale up or down dynamically to match app demand.

⚡ 3. Faster Deployment:

Provision complex enterprise environments in minutes.

🌍 4. Global Reach:

Deploy apps in regions worldwide close to end users.

🔧 5. Flexibility:

Pick and swap exact technologies needed for workloads.

🔒 6. Security Features:

Extensive enterprise-grade controls, encryption, and compliance.

💾 7. Backup & DR:

Automated snapshots, replication, and disaster recovery.

📊 8. Monitoring:

Built-in dashboards, alerting triggers, and analytics.

⭐ CRITICAL POINTS
• Cloud Computing: On-demand delivery of IT resources over Internet with usage-based / pay-as-you-go pricing.
• Cloud Service Provider: Company providing cloud services (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud).
• IaaS: Infrastructure is provided; customer manages more of the environment.
• PaaS: Platform/environment provided; developers focus on applications.
• SaaS: Complete software application delivered over the Internet.
• Public Cloud: Shared provider infrastructure serving multiple customers.
• Private Cloud: Cloud environment dedicated to one organization.
• Hybrid Cloud: Combination of public and private environments.
🧠 SUPER EASY MEMORY TRICK
Service Models:
IaaS ➔ Infrastructure | PaaS ➔ Platform | SaaS ➔ Software
Think: I ➔ P ➔ S (Infrastructure ➔ Platform ➔ Software)
As you move from IaaS ➔ PaaS ➔ SaaS:
Customer responsibility ↓  |  Provider responsibility ↑
Deployment Models:
Public ➔ Shared | Private ➔ Dedicated | Hybrid ➔ Combination
🚌 Public = Bus  |  🚗 Private = Your/Rented Car  |  🚌+🚗 Hybrid = Both
INTERVIEW CORNER

🎯 Top Interview Questions & Exact Answers

Q1. What is cloud computing?

Ans: On-demand delivery of IT resources such as compute, storage, databases, and networking over the Internet with usage-based or pay-as-you-go pricing.

Q2. What is a Cloud Service Provider?

Ans: A company providing cloud computing services and infrastructure over a network (e.g., AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud).

Q3. What is IaaS?

Ans: Provides fundamental infrastructure like VMs, storage, and networking, while customer manages more of the software environment.

Q4. What is PaaS?

Ans: Provides a managed platform and runtime environment that allows developers to focus primarily on developing and deploying applications.

Q5. What is SaaS?

Ans: Provides a complete software application over the Internet, which users can access without managing underlying infrastructure.

Q6. Difference between Public and Private Cloud?

Ans: Public cloud uses shared provider infrastructure serving multiple customers with logical isolation; Private cloud is dedicated exclusively to one organization.

Q7. What is Hybrid Cloud?

Ans: Combines private and public cloud environments, allowing organizations to use both according to workload and security requirements.

Q8. Why do organizations use cloud computing?

Ans: Scalability, flexibility, faster deployment, reduced upfront infrastructure costs, global availability, and access to managed services.

Q9. Is cloud computing only about Virtual Machines?

Ans: No. Cloud computing provides vast services beyond VMs, including storage, databases, networking, containers, serverless computing, machine learning, IAM, monitoring, and logging.

🔥 FINAL 1-MINUTE REVISION Essential Exam Summary

• Cloud Computing: On-demand IT resources over the Internet + pay-as-you-go pricing.
• Three Service Models: IaaS (Infrastructure ➔ More Control) | PaaS (Platform ➔ Focus on Code) | SaaS (Software ➔ Ready-to-Use).
• Three Deployment Models: Public (Shared) | Private (Dedicated) | Hybrid (Public + Private).
• Much More Than VMs: Compute, Storage, DB, Networking, Containers, Serverless, ML, IAM, Monitoring, Logging, Security.
• ⭐ Core Shift: Traditional IT: Buy ➔ Install ➔ Configure ➔ Maintain ➔ Scale | Cloud: Select ➔ Provision ➔ Use ➔ Pay ➔ Scale. Foundation for understanding AWS EC2, S3, VPC, IAM, RDS, ELB, Lambda & CloudWatch!

💡 8 Bonus Study Tips for Cloud Exams (Explained in Plain English!)

Use these 8 proven study methods to retain cloud architecture forever without memorization stress.

1. Mind Maps 🗺️

In simple terms: Instead of reading pages of text, draw a central cloud icon and branch it out into 3 main branches: Service Models, Deployment Models, and Key Benefits. Your brain remembers pictures 10x faster than paragraphs!

2. Flow Charts ➔

In simple terms: Always draw the linear flow for transitions: Traditional: Buy ➔ Install ➔ Maintain vs Cloud: Select ➔ Use ➔ Pay-per-use. Drawing arrows in your exam answers instantly shows the examiner that you understand how processes work.

3. Formula / Rule Box 📦

In simple terms: Put golden rules in a bordered box. For Cloud: Control ∝ Customer Responsibility (As control increases in IaaS, your responsibility increases; as you shift to SaaS, provider responsibility increases).

4. Revision Section ⏱️

In simple terms: Don't re-read entire textbooks before tests. Dedicate 60 seconds every evening to scan the Final 1-Minute Revision block on Page 6. This activates active recall and cements topics into long-term memory.

In simple terms: Use a consistent 3-pen system: Red pen for headings and definitions, Blue pen for explanations and real-world examples, and Yellow highlighter for memory shortcuts and exam answers.

AWS ESSENTIALS

☁️ AWS — Overview & Introduction Detailed Notes

Comprehensive, Structured, Exam & Interview-Ready Study Guide

CORE DEFINITION

1. What is AWS?

Full Form: AWS = Amazon Web Services

AWS is a Cloud Service Provider (CSP) offered by Amazon.

Simple Definition:
AWS is a cloud computing platform that provides a wide range of IT resources and services over the Internet on a pay-as-you-go basis.

Instead of purchasing and maintaining physical servers, storage, networking equipment, databases, etc., organizations can use AWS services according to their requirements.

CONCEPTUAL SHIFT

2. AWS in Simple Words

Think of AWS as a huge collection of IT infrastructure and services available through the Internet.

Traditional Approach:
Buy Hardware ➔ Install Servers ➔ Configure Networking ➔ Setup Storage ➔ Maintain Infrastructure
Using AWS:
Internet ➔ AWS ➔ [ Compute + Storage + Database + Networking + Security + Monitoring + AI/ML + etc. ]
ORIGINS

3. History of AWS

AWS was officially launched in 2006 as a commercial cloud platform.

It initially became known for foundational services such as:

Amazon S3 (Simple Storage Service):
Used for storing data such as files, images, videos, backups, and application data.
Amazon EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud):
Used to provide scalable computing capacity, commonly through virtual servers/instances.
ECOSYSTEM

4. Evolution of AWS

AWS started with a relatively small set of foundational services. Over time, AWS expanded into a very large cloud ecosystem covering areas such as:

• Compute
• Storage
• Databases
• Networking
• Security
• Containers
• Serverless
• Analytics
• Artificial Intelligence
• Machine Learning
• IoT
• Developer tools
• Monitoring
• Management
Important: The exact number of AWS services changes over time, so don't memorize a specific number such as "200 services." AWS's service catalog continues to evolve.

5. AWS and Modern Technologies

🤖 AI & Machine Learning: Developing and deploying advanced AI/ML workloads.
🌐 Internet of Things (IoT): Connecting and managing fleets of IoT devices.
⚡ Serverless Computing: Run applications without directly managing traditional servers.
📦 Containers: Running and managing containerized microservices apps.
📊 Analytics: Processing and analyzing massive volumes of big data.

6. AWS Real-World Usage

AWS is used by organizations of different sizes, from early-stage startups to multinational enterprises.

Examples of industries and use cases:

• E-commerce
• Financial services
• Healthcare
• Gaming
• Media & entertainment
• Government
• Education
• Software development
• Data analytics

AWS publishes customer stories and case studies showing how organizations solve real-world problems.

7. Why is AWS Popular?

⭐ 4 PILLARS TO REMEMBER

There are several important reasons. The four major concepts to remember are:

📈 1. Scalability
🌍 2. Global Reach
🔄 3. Reliability
🔐 4. Security
PILLAR 1

8. Scalability 📈

Definition: Scalability is the ability to increase or decrease computing resources according to workload requirements.

Initially: 100 Users ➔ Small Resources
Later: 100,000 Users ➔ More Resources Required!

AWS allows you to scale resources according to your application's requirements.

Example: A website may need:
2 GB RAM ➔ 4 GB RAM ➔ 8 GB RAM or additional instances may be added dynamically.

👉 Key Point: AWS makes it easier to scale infrastructure as demand changes.

PILLAR 2

9. Global Reach 🌍

Suppose your application has users spread across continents:

🇮🇳 India 🇺🇸 USA 🇪🇺 Europe 🇦🇺 Australia 🇸🇬 Singapore

You may want your application and supporting infrastructure to be available close to your users.

AWS has infrastructure distributed across many geographic locations worldwide. This helps organizations build high-performance applications for global audiences.

PILLAR 3

10. Reliability 🔄

AWS provides infrastructure designed to support highly available and resilient applications.

Single Location (Risky):
One Location ➔ Single Failure ➔ App Down ❌
Multi-AZ Setup:
AWS Region ➔ AZ-1 | AZ-2 | AZ-3 ✓

Instead of keeping everything in one physical location, you can architect applications across multiple Availability Zones. If one AZ experiences a problem, workloads can potentially continue operating in another zone!

PILLAR 4

11. Security 🔐

Security is one of the most important aspects of cloud computing. AWS provides many security-related capabilities, including:

• Identity & Access (IAM)
• Encryption
• Network security
• Monitoring & Logging
• Security services
• Granular Access control
⚠️ Critical Rule: AWS does not automatically make every application secure. Customers are also responsible for securing the resources and apps they configure.
AWS Shared Responsibility Model (covered in depth later).

12. AWS in the Cloud Market

COMPETITIVE LANDSCAPE

AWS is one of the largest and most widely used cloud platforms globally. Other major cloud providers include:

AWS
Amazon Web Services (Pioneer & Market Leader)
Microsoft Azure
Microsoft's Cloud Computing Platform
Google Cloud (GCP)
Google's Cloud Computing Platform
Hierarchy: AWS ➔ [ Microsoft Azure | Google Cloud ] ⚠️ Market-share rankings change over time, so don't memorize an old percentage from a particular quarter as a permanent fact.

13. Popular AWS Services (The Big 5 for Beginners)

MUST-KNOW SERVICES

AWS has hundreds of services, but as a beginner, you should first focus on the most important ones:

🖥️ Amazon EC2 COMPUTE

Full Form: Elastic Compute Cloud
Used for scalable compute capacity / virtual servers.

Application ➔ EC2 Instance ➔ Compute Resources (vCPU, RAM, OS)

Rent VMs in the cloud without purchasing physical servers.

💾 Amazon S3 OBJECT STORAGE

Full Form: Simple Storage Service
Used for highly durable object storage.

Common uses: Images, videos, documents, backups, logs, static website files.

Application ➔ S3 Bucket ➔ Objects / Files (Unlimited scale)
🗄️ Amazon RDS MANAGED DATABASE

Full Form: Relational Database Service
Used to run and manage relational databases without administrative burdens.

Supported database engines:

MySQL PostgreSQL MariaDB Oracle SQL Server
⚡ AWS Lambda SERVERLESS COMPUTE

A serverless compute service. You can run code without managing traditional servers directly.

Event Occurs ➔ Lambda Triggered ➔ Code Executes ➔ Auto-Shuts Down

Zero server provisioning, auto-scales, pay only for milliseconds executed.

🌐 Amazon CloudFront CDN (GLOBAL DELIVERY)

A Content Delivery Network (CDN) service. It helps deliver content (videos, data, APIs) to users with lower latency by using a globally distributed edge network.

User in India ➔ CloudFront Edge Location (Close to User) ➔ Content Delivered Fast! ⚡

14. AWS Management Console

PORTAL INTERFACE

AWS provides a web-based management interface called the: AWS Management Console. You can use any modern web browser to access AWS services directly.

Typical Console Workflow:
1. Browser ➔ 2. AWS Console ➔ 3. Select Region ➔ 4. Select Service ➔ 5. Configure Resource ➔ 6. Create & Manage

You can manage, monitor, and deploy many AWS resources directly from this intuitive visual console.

Handwritten Lecture Notes Page 3 of 8
📚 Subject: Cloud Computing & AWS Topic: Global Infrastructure (Regions, AZs & Local Zones) Sheet No: 04
CORE CONCEPT

15. AWS Regions 🌍

Geographic Physical Location

Definition: An AWS Region is a separate geographic area where AWS has infrastructure for running cloud workloads.

• India • USA • Europe • Asia Pacific • Australia • Middle East
16. Why Do Regions Matter?

Suppose your customers are primarily in India. You choose an Indian Region to minimize network latency and satisfy regulatory laws.

Indian Users ➔ AWS India Region ➔ Application (Ultra-low latency!)

Choosing a Region affects: Latency, Data residency, Service availability, Pricing, and Disaster recovery architecture.

17. AWS Region Example — Mumbai

AWS has a major Region in Mumbai. Its unique AWS Region identifier code is:

ap-south-1
India ➔ Mumbai Region ➔ ap-south-1

When deploying resources (like EC2 or RDS), you select this Region to provision resources locally.

FAULT ISOLATION

18. Availability Zones (AZs) & 19. Why AWS Uses Them

Isolated Datacenters within Region

Definition: A Region is divided into multiple isolated locations called Availability Zones (AZs). An AZ consists of one or more discrete data centers with independent power, cooling, and physical security, designed to isolate failures.

Region Hierarchy:
AWS Region ➔ [ AZ-1 | AZ-2 | AZ-3 ]

Connected via low-latency redundant fiber optics.

Why Use Multiple AZs?

High Availability & Fault Tolerance: If an app runs in only AZ-1 and AZ-1 fails ➔ App goes down ❌! But across AZ-1, AZ-2, AZ-3 ➔ If one fails, others continue serving traffic smoothly ✓.

20. Region vs Availability Zone (Interview Favorite!)

HIGH YIELD
Feature Region Availability Zone (AZ)
Definition Geographic physical area Isolated location / data center(s) within a Region
Composition Contains multiple AZs (typically 3+) Belongs to a specific Region
Example Mumbai (ap-south-1) ap-south-1a, ap-south-1b
Primary Use Geographic deployment, latency & compliance High availability & fault isolation
Memory Trick 🧠: Region = City/Geographic Area | AZ = Separate infrastructure location / data center within that city.

21. Local Zones & 22. Region + AZ + Local Zone Hierarchy

LOW LATENCY

AWS Local Zones: An extension of an AWS Region that places selected compute, storage, and database services closer to large population and industry centers for workloads requiring single-digit millisecond latency (e.g., real-time gaming, live media production, enterprise apps).

AWS Global Infrastructure ➔ Regions ➔ AZ-1, AZ-2, AZ-3 ➔ Local Zone (Closer to specific cities!)

These concepts help AWS customers design applications for maximum Performance, Availability, Resilience, and Geographic distribution.

Estimate Costs Before Launch

25. AWS Free Tier & 26. EC2 Usage

AWS provides a Free Tier for eligible services and accounts, subject to specific limits and terms. Useful for: Learning, practicing, building small experiments.

⚠️ IMPORTANT WARNING:
Never assume "AWS is completely free." AWS has many paid services and usage beyond free limits results in charges!

Always check eligible instance types (e.g. t2.micro / t3.micro), free hours (750 hrs/month), and storage limits before starting.

CRITICAL ADVICE

27. AWS Cost Awareness ⚠️

Golden rule for beginners: When learning AWS, don't create resources and simply forget about them!

Create EC2 ➔ Instance keeps running ➔ Usage accumulates ➔ Potential charges on your credit card! 💸

Good Practice: After practicing, always Stop or Terminate unused resources! Continuously check AWS Billing & Cost Explorer.

🎯 Top 10 Interview Questions & Exact Answers

Q1. What is AWS?

Ans: A cloud computing platform that provides on-demand IT resources and services over the Internet using pay-as-you-go pricing.

Q2. When was AWS launched?

Ans: AWS was launched as a commercial cloud platform in 2006.

Q3. What are popular AWS services?

Ans: EC2 (compute), S3 (storage), RDS (databases), Lambda (serverless), VPC (networking), IAM (security), and CloudFront (CDN).

Q4. What is an AWS Region?

Ans: A separate geographic area containing infrastructure and multiple isolated Availability Zones.

Q5. What is an Availability Zone (AZ)?

Ans: An isolated location within an AWS Region with discrete data centers, designed for fault isolation and high availability.

Q6. Why are multiple AZs used?

Ans: To design fault-tolerant systems; if one AZ fails, workloads can continue operating in another zone without total downtime.

Q7. Region vs Availability Zone?

Ans: A Region is a geographic area; an AZ is an isolated infrastructure location / data center within that Region.

Q8. What is AWS Local Zone?

Ans: Extensions that place AWS compute and storage closer to large population centers for single-digit millisecond latency.

Q9. What is AWS Pricing Calculator?

Ans: A web tool to estimate expected monthly costs of AWS services based on chosen configurations and usage.

Q10. Is AWS completely free?

Ans: No. Free Tier offers exist for eligible services/limits, but many services are chargeable and usage beyond free limits incurs costs.

📚 Subject: AWS Cloud Computing Topic: Account Setup & AWS Console Sheet No: 01
AWS FOUNDATIONS

☁️ AWS Account Setup & AWS Management Console

Comprehensive, Step-by-Step Hands-on Setup Guide

GETTING STARTED

1. Introduction

Before starting hands-on practice with AWS, the first step is to create and configure an AWS account.

An AWS account allows you to:

• Access AWS services
• Create cloud resources
• Practice services such as EC2, S3, VPC, IAM, etc.
• Monitor resource usage and costs
• Deploy applications
• Learn AWS through the AWS Management Console
⚠️ Important Warning: AWS may require valid payment and identity verification. Never use fake identity or payment information.
PREREQUISITES

2. Requirements for Creating an AWS Account

You generally need the following four items:

1. Working Email Address 📧

Your email address should:

  • Be accessible to you
  • Be a valid email address
  • Be available for verification
  • Be used to receive AWS account notifications

AWS sends verification emails during account creation.

2. Working Mobile Number 📱

A valid mobile number is required for verification.

AWS may send an OTP or use phone verification to confirm your identity.

Enter Mobile ➔ Receive SMS/Call OTP ➔ Verified ✓
3. Valid Identity Document 🪪

AWS may require identity verification. Depending on the verification process and country, an accepted government-issued ID may include:

• Driving License
• Passport
• Other supported government-issued ID

Note: The exact documents accepted can vary depending on AWS's current verification process and your location.

4. Credit/Debit Card 💳

AWS requires valid payment information for account verification and billing. You should provide:

• Valid debit card, or
• Valid credit card
Security Rule: Do not use fake card details.

3. Why Does AWS Ask for Payment Information?

COMMON FAQ

A common beginner question is: "If AWS has a Free Tier, why does it ask for my card?"

Answer: Because AWS is a paid cloud platform. The Free Tier allows eligible customers to use certain services/resources within specified limits, but AWS still needs a valid payment method for account verification and for situations where chargeable usage occurs.

EC2 Example:
Suppose you create an EC2 instance:
• If usage remains within an applicable free allowance ➔ You may not be charged.
• But if you exceed allowance, run longer than allowed, or choose paid features ➔ Charges may occur!
Important Rule to Remember:
Do not assume: "AWS Free Tier = Everything is free."
Instead remember:
Free Tier = Specific services + specific usage limits + specific eligibility conditions.
Always check current AWS pricing/free-tier terms before creating resources.

FULL LIFECYCLE

4. AWS Account Creation — Basic Flow

The Complete Signup Pipeline

The general signup process is structured as follows:

AWS Website ➔ Create AWS Account ➔ Enter Email ➔ Verify Email
➔ Create Password ➔ Account Info ➔ Payment Info ➔ Identity Verification
➔ Phone Verification ➔ Select Support Plan ➔ Complete Signup ➔ Sign in to Console ✓

5. Step 1 — Visit AWS

URL

Go to the official AWS website: aws.amazon.com

Choose the option to create/sign up for an AWS account. Look for the button:

Create an AWS Account / Create a Free Account

AWS may change the wording or signup interface over time.

6. Step 2 — Enter Your Email Address

COMMUNICATION

Enter a valid email address. AWS will use this email for:

• Verification
• Account communication
• Billing notifications
• Security alerts
• Important AWS notifications
Important: Use an email account that you regularly access.

7. Step 3 — Verify Email

SECURITY

AWS sends a verification code/link to your email.

Enter Email ➔ AWS sends code ➔ Open Email ➔ Enter Code ➔ Email Verified ✓

After successful verification, you can continue the signup process.

8. Step 4 — Create AWS Account Password

CREDENTIALS

Create a strong password according to AWS's current password requirements.

Good Practice:
• Uppercase letters
• Lowercase letters
• Numbers
• Special characters
Avoid:
• Your name
• Birthday
• Simple passwords
• Reused passwords

9. Step 5 — Provide Account Information

AWS asks for information required to create the account. You may need to provide details such as:

• Name
• Contact information
• Address
• Country / region
• Phone number
• Account type / purpose

👉 For learning purposes, select the appropriate personal option if that accurately describes your use.

10. Step 6 — Add Payment Information

Enter your valid Debit card, or Credit card. AWS uses this information for billing and account verification.

Temporary Verification Charge:
AWS may place a small temporary authorization/verification charge on the card. The exact amount and whether/how quickly it is reversed can vary by region, bank, card network, and AWS's current verification process.

⚠️ Important: Do not rely on a specific amount such as ₹2 as a universal rule.

📚 Subject: AWS Cloud Computing Topic: Verification, Activation & Console Overview Sheet No: 03

11. Step 7 — Identity Verification

SECURITY

AWS may ask you to verify your identity. You may be asked to provide an accepted government-issued ID.

Process varies by Country, Account type, and AWS requirements.

🚨 Important Security Rule:
Never share your: AWS password, OTP, Card PIN, CVV, or MFA codes with another person!

12. Step 8 — Phone Verification

OTP CHECK

AWS may require phone verification. Make sure the phone number is working and accessible.

Enter Phone Number ➔ Receive OTP / Verification ➔ Enter Code ➔ Phone Verified ✓

13. Step 9 — Choose a Support Plan

COST FREE

During signup, AWS may ask you to choose a support plan. For basic learning and experimentation, the Basic Support option is generally sufficient when available.

Basic Support: Suitable for learning AWS, practicing services, basic experimentation, personal projects, beginner study.

Paid support plans provide additional features and 24/7 technical support response.

14. Step 10 — Account Creation Completed

ACTIVATED

After completing all required verification steps, AWS activates the account.

You will receive an email confirming that your: AWS services are ready to use.

You can then immediately sign in to the AWS Management Console!

PORTAL

15. AWS Management Console

Graphical Web-Based Portal

The AWS Management Console is a web-based graphical interface used to manage AWS resources and services. Instead of using commands, you can perform many AWS operations through the browser.

Using the console, you can:

Launch EC2 instances Create S3 buckets Configure VPCs Create IAM users & roles View CloudWatch metrics Manage databases (RDS) Configure load balancers Monitor billing & costs

16. AWS Console — Dashboard

After signing in, you see the AWS Console. The dashboard provides access to:

• Recently visited services
• AWS services catalog
• Region selection
• Cost and usage info
• Account-related shortcuts & resources

For a new AWS account, dashboard looks empty initially because you haven't used services yet.

17. Recently Visited Services

AWS Console keeps track of services you recently accessed. For example:

EC2 S3 IAM VPC RDS

This makes it fast and easy to return to frequently used services without searching.

19. Searching for Services: Instead of manually browsing, use the Console Search bar. AWS Console ➔ Search "EC2" ➔ Click Elastic Compute Cloud

20. AWS Region Selection

One of the most important concepts in the AWS Console is the Region. The console displays the currently selected AWS Region in the top-right corner:

• Europe (Stockholm)
• ap-northeast-1 (Tokyo)
• Asia Pacific (Mumbai)

The exact selected region depends on your session and what you choose.

21. What is an AWS Region?

Definition: An AWS Region is a geographical area where AWS operates infrastructure (India, US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Middle East, Canada, Australia).

Mumbai Region Identifier:
Asia Pacific (Mumbai) = ap-south-1

Each region has a distinct, standardized alphanumeric identifier code.

VERY IMPORTANT

22. Why Does Region Matter?

When creating AWS resources, you select a region. The resource is created in that selected region!

Created in Mumbai ➔ Switch to Singapore ➔ EC2 Instance disappears from view! 😱
Common Beginner Panic: "I created my EC2 instance, but now I can't find it!"
➔ You didn't lose it! You are simply looking at a different region in the console dropdown.

23. Choosing a Region (5 Factors)

Region selection depends on application requirements:

1. Latency: Choose geographically closer regions to users (Indian Users ➔ Mumbai Region = low latency).
2. Compliance: Strict legal data-residency laws requiring data to remain inside the country.
3. Service Availability: Not every AWS service/feature is available in every region.
4. Cost: Pricing differs slightly across AWS regions.
5. Disaster Recovery: Multi-region strategies for high availability.

📚 Subject: AWS Cloud Computing Topic: Infrastructure Hierarchy, Cost Tracking & Workflow Sheet No: 05
HIERARCHY

24. Region vs Availability Zone (AZ)

Resilience & Isolation

Remember this fundamental architecture hierarchy:

AWS Global Infrastructure ➔ Region ➔ [ Availability Zone 1 | Availability Zone 2 | Availability Zone 3 ]
Example: Mumbai Region (ap-south-1) ➔ [ ap-south-1a | ap-south-1b | ap-south-1c ]
Region:
A geographical area containing multiple Availability Zones. Used for geographic deployment.
Availability Zone (AZ):
A separate, isolated infrastructure location / data center within a Region. Designed for high availability, auto-scaling & disaster recovery.

25. Cost & Usage Monitoring

AWS provides tools and dashboards to help you monitor your spending. You can see:

• Current costs
• Usage metrics
• Billing breakdown
• Cost trends
• Forecasts
• Service-level charges
EC2 ➔ Running Instance ➔ Usage Generated ➔ Possible Charges ➔ Billing Dashboard

A beginner should make cost monitoring an everyday habit!

26. Why Cost Monitoring is Crucial ⚠️

Cloud resources can continue running even when you are not actively using them!

Create EC2 ➔ Finish Practice ➔ Forget to Stop/Delete ➔ Keeps Running ➔ Charges on Card! 💸
Golden Habit: Always clean up (Stop/Terminate) resources after practice!
27. AWS Console Theme: Supports Light Theme and Dark Theme for comfort during long sessions.

28. Practical Beginner Workflow (Make This Your Daily Habit)

DISCIPLINE

Once your AWS account is ready, strictly follow this sequential workflow every single lab session:

1. Login 2. Check Region 3. Check Billing 4. Open Service 5. Create Resource 6. Configure 7. Test 8. Monitor 9. Stop/Delete 10. Check Cost

29. Important Security Practices

CRITICAL

After creating your account, security is top priority:

1. Enable MFA: Multi-Factor Authentication adds an essential second defense layer beyond passwords.
Password + MFA Code ➔ Strong Security
2. Never Share Credentials: Never share Password, Access keys, Secret access keys, MFA codes, or OTPs.
3. Use IAM Properly: Avoid using the root user for everyday administrative or lab tasks.

30. Root User vs IAM User

KEY DISTINCTION
Root User:
The original AWS account identity created with email. Has unrestricted, complete permissions over everything in the account.
IAM User / Role:
Identities created inside IAM with strictly controlled, granular permissions to specific resources.
Industry Best Practice: Use the root user ONLY when root-level setup is required, and use IAM identities for all regular tasks.

31. Common Beginner Mistakes (Avoid These Traps!)

WATCH OUT
Mistake 1 — Assuming Everything Is Free
❌ "AWS is free."
✅ "Some AWS usage may be free within applicable limits & conditions."
Mistake 2 — Forgetting the Region
Create EC2 in Mumbai, then switch to Oregon.
"My EC2 disappeared!" No, it's just in Mumbai!
Mistake 3 — Leaving Resources Running
EC2 launched ➔ practice done ➔ forgot to terminate ➔ bills pile up silently on your credit card.
Mistake 4 — Creating Unnecessary Expensive Resources
Creating multiple EC2 instances, Elastic IPs (charged when unattached!), NAT Gateways, Load Balancers, or RDS without understanding costs. Start small!
Mistake 5 — Ignoring Billing
Never checking AWS Billing & Cost Management dashboard until an invoice notification arrives.

32. Real-World Example — Practicing EC2

Imagine you are learning AWS and want to practice launching an EC2 instance:

Step 1: Login to AWS
Step 2: Select Mumbai Region
Step 3: Open EC2
Step 4: Launch small instance (Free-tier eligible)
Step 5: Connect and practice
Step 6: Finish your exercise
Step 7: Stop or Terminate instance
Step 8: Check cost dashboard

This is the correct, disciplined cloud-learning mindset.

35. Interview Questions & Exact Answers (Part 1)

Q1. What is the AWS Management Console?

Ans: A web-based graphical interface that allows users to access, configure, monitor, and manage AWS services and resources through a browser.

Q2. Why does AWS require payment information?

Ans: For identity verification and billing. Even with Free Tier, charges occur when paid resources or usage beyond free allowances are consumed.

Q3. Is AWS completely free?

Ans: No. AWS is a paid platform. Free Tier offers exist under specified limits/conditions, but usage outside those conditions generates charges.

Q4. What is an AWS Region?

Ans: A geographical area containing AWS infrastructure and multiple isolated Availability Zones (e.g. Mumbai ap-south-1).

Q5. Why is region selection important?

Ans: It determines where resources are created and directly impacts network latency, service availability, compliance laws, and pricing.

Q6. What happens if you switch AWS Regions?

Ans: Region-specific resources won't appear in the new region's console view. An EC2 instance created in Mumbai won't show in Singapore.

Handwritten Lecture Notes Page 7 of 9
📚 Subject: AWS Cloud Computing Topic: Interview Questions (Part 2) & Final Memory Trick Sheet No: 08
INTERVIEW FINALE

35. Interview Questions & Answers (Part 2)

Q7. What is an Availability Zone?

Ans: An isolated infrastructure location containing one or more discrete data centers within an AWS Region, designed to provide resilience and support high availability.

Q8. Why should AWS resources be stopped or deleted after practice?

Ans: AWS resources generate ongoing charges while they remain active or provisioned. Cleaning up unused resources prevents unexpected monthly billing charges.

Q9. What is MFA?

Ans: Multi-Factor Authentication. It adds a crucial second verification factor (such as a time-based TOTP code) beyond the password, dramatically improving account defense.

Q10. What is IAM?

Ans: Identity and Access Management. It controls authentication (who can sign in) and authorization (what permissions and resources they can access) in AWS.

Q11. What is the difference between a Region and an Availability Zone? TOP QUESTION

Composition Contains multiple AZs Belongs to one Region
Example Mumbai (ap-south-1) Individual AZ within Mumbai (ap-south-1a)
Primary Use Geographical deployment, latency & compliance Resilience, high availability & fault isolation

AWS IAM — Identity and Access Management — Handwritten Lecture Notes
📚 Subject: AWS Cloud Computing Topic: AWS IAM (Identity and Access Management) Sheet No: 01
SECURITY CORE

🔐 AWS IAM — Identity and Access Management

Comprehensive, Step-by-Step Security, Authentication & Permissions Guide

FOUNDATION

1. Introduction to IAM

IAM (Identity and Access Management) is one of the most important AWS services for managing authentication and authorization.

IAM helps you control:

• Who can access your AWS account
• Which AWS resources they can access
• What actions they can perform
• How much permission they should have
• How users and groups are managed
• How access is secured
Simple Definition:
AWS IAM is a service used to securely control access to AWS resources by managing identities, permissions, and authentication.
USE CASE

2. Why Do We Need IAM?

Organization Scenario: 50 Employees

Imagine an organization with 50 employees. Everyone cannot have complete access to everything!

Developers
↓
Need EC2 + S3 access
Database Team
↓
Need RDS access
Operations Team
↓
Need EC2 + CloudWatch
Security Team
↓
Need IAM + Security
⚠️ Critical Rule: Giving everyone administrator access would be dangerous! IAM allows us to provide only the access that each user needs.
PILLARS

3. IAM's Main Responsibilities

1. Identity Management 👥

Create and manage:

Users Groups Roles
2. Authentication 🔑

Verify: "Who are you?"

Examples: Username + password, MFA, other supported mechanisms.

3. Authorization 🛡️

Determine: "What are you allowed to do?"

Alex ➔ Allowed to view S3 ➔ Denied delete S3 buckets.
4. Permissions Management 📋

Define what actions users, groups, or roles can perform on AWS resources.

4. IAM Is a Global AWS Service 🌍

GLOBAL

Unlike services such as EC2 (which are tied to a specific AWS Region), IAM identities are not created separately in every region.

User "Alex" created once ➔ Active in Mumbai, Singapore, US East, Europe, etc.

Console Observation: When viewing IAM in the AWS Console, you see "Global" instead of an AWS Region selector.

5. IAM Has No Additional Charge 💰

FREE CORE

IAM itself is available without an additional charge.

⚠️ Remember: IAM being free does NOT mean the resources accessed through IAM are free!
IAM: Free EC2: Paid RDS: Paid S3: Paid
Handwritten Lecture Notes Page 1 of 9
📚 Subject: AWS Cloud Computing Topic: Root User, Users, Groups & Policies Intro Sheet No: 02

6. Root User 👑

HIGHEST ACCESS

When you initially create an AWS account, AWS creates a root user for that account.

AWS Account ➔ Root User ➔ Highest level access over everything!

The root user has unrestricted access to all resources and billing. It must be protected very carefully.

7. Why Avoid Root User Daily?

SECURITY

Using the root user for everyday operations is not recommended.

Root credentials stolen ➔ Attacker gets ultimate control ➔ Complete account compromise!
Root User:
Secure with MFA; use ONLY when required.
IAM Users/Roles:
Use for all regular AWS operations.
IDENTITIES

8. IAM Users

Individual Person / Identity

An IAM User represents an identity that can be given access to AWS resources. Each user can have different permissions:

Alex
Role: Developer
Permissions: EC2 + S3
Paul
Role: Operations
Permissions: EC2 + CloudWatch
Sarah
Role: Security
Permissions: IAM + Security Services

Each user receives permissions strictly appropriate to their job function.

COLLECTIONS

9. IAM Groups

Team Permission Bundling

An IAM Group is a collection of IAM users. Groups are useful when multiple users need similar permissions.

Without Groups (Repetitive & Painful):
• Alex ➔ Operations permissions
• Paul ➔ Operations permissions
• John ➔ Operations permissions
• Sarah ➔ Operations permissions
With IAM Groups (Clean & Scalable):
Operations Group ➔ Attach Operations Policy
➔ Add Alex, Paul, John, Sarah to Group.
All users inherit permissions automatically!

10. Users vs Groups

COMPARISON
IAM UserIAM Group
Represents individual identityCollection of users
Can have direct permissionsPermissions assigned to group
Example: AlexExample: Developers
Used for individual accessUseful for common permissions
🧠 Easy Memory Trick: User = Person | Group = Team

11. IAM Policies

RULES DOC

A policy is a document that defines permissions. It answers the ultimate question:

"Who can perform what action on which resource, under which conditions?"

AWS IAM policies are commonly written in JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) format.

Handwritten Lecture Notes Page 2 of 9
📚 Subject: AWS Cloud Computing Topic: Policy Structure, Wildcards & Least Privilege Sheet No: 03
JSON STRUCTURE

12. Basic IAM Policy Structure

Language: JSON 
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": "s3:GetObject",
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
Effect: Determines whether the operation is Allow or Deny.
Action: Defines what operation is being permitted or rejected. Example: s3:GetObject.
Resource: Specifies which AWS resource the permission applies to. Example: * (wildcard = all applicable resources).

13. IAM Policy — Easy Explanation (The Instruction Sheet)

PLAIN ENGLISH

Think of a policy as a simple 4-question instruction sheet:

WHO?
Which identity?
WHAT?
Which action?
WHERE?
Which resource?
ALLOW / DENY?
What should happen?
Real Example: "Allow Alex to read objects from a specific S3 bucket."

14. Managed Policies

AWS PREBUILT

AWS provides many predefined policies for common use cases, saving admins from creating every permission from scratch:

• AdministratorAccess
• ReadOnlyAccess
• AmazonS3FullAccess
• AmazonEC2FullAccess
• CloudWatchFullAccess

15. AdministratorAccess Policy

DANGER

Provides broad access across all services. Conceptually:

Effect: Allow | Action: * | Resource: *
⚠️ Warning: The * wildcard means ALL actions on ALL resources. Never give this unnecessarily! It violates least privilege.

16. Custom IAM Policies

You can create custom policies via two approaches in the AWS Console:

1. Visual Editor: Point-and-click GUI to select Service ➔ Actions ➔ Resources ➔ Conditions.
2. JSON Editor: Directly write or modify the raw JSON policy document.

Visual Editor ↕ JSON Editor both produce the exact same policy.

GOLDEN RULE

17. Principle of Least Privilege

Definition: Give a user, application, or role only the permissions required to perform its job — nothing more.

❌ Bad Approach:
Developer ➔ AdministratorAccess (when only reading 1 S3 bucket).
✅ Better Approach:
Developer ➔ Specific S3 permissions on that specific bucket only!
Handwritten Lecture Notes Page 3 of 9
📚 Subject: AWS Cloud Computing Topic: IAM Roles, Federation & Multi-Factor Auth (MFA) Sheet No: 04
TEMPORARY ACCESS

18. IAM Roles & 19. Role vs User

No Long-Term Credentials!

An IAM Role is an identity that can be assumed by trusted entities to obtain temporary permissions.

Roles are heavily used by: AWS Services, Applications, EC2 instances, Lambda functions, Users needing temporary access, Federated identities.

FeatureIAM UserIAM Role
NatureRepresents an identityProvides permissions that can be assumed
AssociationOften associated with a specific personUsed by AWS services/apps & temporary access
CredentialsCan have long-term credentials (password/keys)Designed strictly around temporary credentials
ExampleDeveloper user (Alex)EC2 instance assuming role to read S3
🧠 Memory Trick: User = Who you are | Role = What access you can assume

20. Real Example of an IAM Role

Imagine an EC2 web app that needs to read files from S3:

❌ Without a Role (Dangerous):
Hardcode Access Key + Secret Key inside the app code. (Leaking code = leaking account!)
✅ With an IAM Role (Safe):
EC2 Instance ➔ Attach IAM Role ➔ Temporary Credentials ➔ S3 Access. (Zero hardcoded keys!)

21. Federated Access (Enterprise)

Large enterprises already have their own corporate directory identity systems:

Company ➔ Active Directory / Okta IdP ➔ IAM Role ➔ AWS Access

IAM participates in identity federation, allowing companies to centralize logins without creating separate AWS users for every staff member.

SECURITY DEFENSE

22–26. Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)

Essential Extra Layer

22. Definition: MFA adds an essential second verification layer beyond passwords.

Without MFA:
Username + Password ➔ Login (Vulnerable!)
With MFA:
Username + Password + MFA Code ➔ Login ✓
23. Why MFA is Crucial:
If a hacker steals your password, they still cannot sign in without physical possession of the MFA device!
24. Common MFA Methods:
• Authenticator Apps (Google Auth, Authy)
• Hardware Security Keys (YubiKey)
• Other supported token devices
25. MFA Example (TOTP):
Phone app displays rotating 6-digit code (e.g. 123456). Code changes every 30 seconds!
26. Protect the Root User with MFA: One of the most important AWS security mandates. Enable MFA on root immediately!

📚 Subject: AWS Cloud Computing Topic: Password Policies, Access Keys, CLI & SDK Sheet No: 05

27. IAM Password Policy

Administrators configure requirements for user passwords:

• Minimum length (e.g. 12)
• Uppercase letters
• Lowercase letters
• Numbers & symbols
• Password reuse limits
• User password reset

28. Expiration & 29. Access Keys

28. Expiration: E.g., password expires after 90 days, forcing a rotation.

29. Access Keys: Used for programmatic access to AWS. Consists of a pair:
Access Key ID + Secret Access Key
TERMINAL

30–32. AWS CLI (Command Line Interface)

Automation Powerhouse

30. Definition: Interact with AWS from a command-line environment. Example command: aws iam list-users

Terminal ➔ AWS CLI ➔ AWS API ➔ AWS Service
AWS Console (GUI)AWS CLI (Command Line)
Graphical, browser-based interfaceCommand-line terminal tool
Easy for beginners to exploreExtremely powerful for automation & scripting
Manual clicks & operationsScriptable, repeatable operations
Requires browserRuns in terminal / CI/CD pipelines

32. Why Use CLI? Performing an operation 100 times manually = 100 clicks & mistakes. With CLI, write 1 bash script and execute instantly!

33. CloudShell & 34–35. SDKs

33. AWS CloudShell: Built-in browser terminal inside the AWS Console, pre-authenticated with your login session.

34–35. AWS SDK (Software Development Kit): Write code in Python (Boto3), Java, JavaScript, etc., to call AWS APIs directly:

Python App ➔ AWS SDK ➔ AWS API ➔ S3 / EC2
THE BIG 3

36. Three Ways to Access AWS

1. AWS Console (GUI): Browser ➔ Click
2. AWS CLI (Terminal): Shell ➔ Command
3. AWS SDK/APIs (Programmatic): Code ➔ APIs
🧠 Easy Memory Trick:
Console = Click | CLI = Command | SDK = Code

📚 Subject: AWS Cloud Computing Topic: Credential Security, CLI Setup & Auditing Sheet No: 06
CRITICAL WARNING

37–38. Protect Access Keys & Never Commit to Git!

Bot Scanners Alert

37. Access keys are sensitive credentials. Never send them in chats, upload to GitHub, commit to source code, store in public repos, put in screenshots, or share in documents.

Hardcode Keys in Code ➔ Git Commit ➔ Push to GitHub ➔ Attacker Scans Repo ➔ Full Account Compromised! 💸
38. Modern Secure Approach: Use IAM Roles, AWS Secrets Manager, environment variables, or temporary STS credentials. Never bake static keys into files!

39–40. Access Key Creation & Config

39. Critical Rule: The Secret Access Key is shown only once at creation. Download/save it securely immediately!

$ aws configure
AWS Access Key ID: AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE
AWS Secret Access Key: wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCY
Default region name: ap-south-1
Default output format: json

41–43. Listing IAM Users & Flow

$ aws iam list-users

42. Why did it initially fail? If run before aws configure, it throws: "Unable to locate credentials." AWS needs to know WHO you are!

CLI ➔ Credentials ➔ AWS API ➔ IAM Policy Evaluation ➔ Allow / Deny

44. Access Keys vs Password

KEY COMPARISON
PasswordAccess Keys
Commonly used for AWS Console sign-inUsed for programmatic access (CLI / SDK / API)
GUI / browser accessTerminal, script, and code access
Username + PasswordAccess Key ID + Secret Access Key
Can be protected with MFAMust be securely managed and rotated periodically

AUDIT

Downloads a complete audit CSV of all account credentials. Answers:

• Who has passwords? When last used?
• Which access keys exist? Are they active?
• Who has MFA enabled? Who doesn't?

Indispensable when managing 100+ IAM users!

DEFENSE

📚 Subject: AWS Cloud Computing Topic: IAM Best Practices, Architecture & Pitfalls Sheet No: 07
8 RULES

49. IAM Security Best Practices

Industry Gold Standards
1. Avoid Root Daily: Use root only for initial setup.
2. Enable MFA: Mandate MFA on Root & privileged users.
3. Use Groups: Assign permissions to teams, not users.
4. Least Privilege: Grant minimum necessary rights.
5. Protect Keys: Never commit access keys to code/git.
6. Audit Regularly: Run Credential Reports periodically.
7. Clean Unused: Disable/delete inactive credentials.
8. Prefer Roles: Use IAM Roles over hardcoded keys.

50. IAM Architecture — Big Picture

AWS ACCOUNT ➔ Root User (MFA)
↓
[ IAM Users (Alex, Paul) ] ➔ IAM Group ➔ Policies
↓
Permissions ➔ [ EC2 | S3 | RDS ]
↑
IAM Roles (Assumed by EC2 / Lambda)

51 & 54. Complete Access Model

Identity (User/Role) ➔ Policy ➔ Action ➔ Resource ➔ Evaluation
54. IAM Evaluation Rule:
By default, all requests are DENIED. An explicit ALLOW grants access. However, an explicit DENY always overrides any ALLOW!

52–53. Practical Example: Adding & Removing Developers

WORKFLOW
Step 1: Create Users (Alex, Paul)
Step 2: Create Group (Developers)
Step 3: Attach S3 Policy to Group
Step 4: Add Users to Group

53. What happens when Alex is removed from Developers? He instantly loses all S3 permissions inherited through that group! No manual revocation needed per service.

55. Auth vs Auth

Authentication: "Who are you?" (Username, MFA).
Authorization: "What can you do?" (Policies).

58. IAM vs Security Groups

IAM: API identity permissions.
Security Group: Virtual firewall controlling network IP traffic to EC2.

60. Common Mistakes ❌

• Giving AdminAccess to all
• Using Root daily
• Committing keys to GitHub
• Forgetting MFA

VIVA / SCREENING

61. Top 20 Interview Questions & Answers

Q1. What is AWS IAM?

Ans: A service used to securely manage identities and control access to AWS resources through authentication and authorization.

Q2. Is IAM regional or global?

Ans: IAM is a global service. Identities and policies are not created separately for each AWS Region.

Q3. Is IAM free?

Ans: Yes, IAM is offered at no additional charge. However, resources managed via IAM (EC2, S3) incur standard charges.

Q4. What is the AWS root user?

Ans: The original identity created with the AWS account. Has complete access; must be locked with MFA and avoided for daily tasks.

Q5. What is an IAM user?

Ans: An identity representing a person or application that can be granted granular permissions to access AWS resources.

Q6. What is an IAM group?

Ans: A collection of IAM users. Permissions assigned to the group are automatically inherited by all its members.

Q7. Why use IAM groups?

Ans: To simplify permission administration by assigning common policies centrally rather than individually.

Q8. What is an IAM policy?

Ans: A JSON document that formally defines permissions (Effect, Action, Resource, Condition) for identities.

Q9. What is the Principle of Least Privilege?

Ans: Granting only the minimum required permissions necessary for an identity to perform its job — nothing more.

Q10. What is an IAM role?

Ans: An identity with permissions that can be assumed by trusted entities (services, users, apps) using temporary credentials.

Q11. What is MFA?

Ans: Multi-Factor Authentication. Adds an additional verification factor (e.g. 6-digit TOTP code) beyond the password.

Q12. Why enable MFA for root?

Ans: Because the root user has ultimate power. MFA ensures account safety even if the root password is compromised.

Q13. Difference: Authentication vs Authorization?

Ans: Authentication = "Who are you?" (login). Authorization = "What are you allowed to do?" (permissions).

Q14. What are access keys used for?

Ans: Credentials (Key ID + Secret Key) used for programmatic access to AWS via CLI, SDKs, and APIs.

Q15. What is AWS CLI?

Ans: A unified command-line tool to manage and interact with AWS services using terminal commands and scripts.

Q16. Why is AWS CLI useful?

Ans: Enables task automation, repetitive batch operations, scripting, DevOps pipelines, and headless administration.

Q17. What is AWS SDK?

Ans: Software Development Kits enabling software applications (Python, Java, Node.js) to call AWS APIs programmatically.

Q18. 3 Main ways to access AWS?

Ans: 1. AWS Console (Click), 2. AWS CLI (Command), 3. AWS SDK/APIs (Code).

Q19. What is a Credential Report?

Ans: An auditing CSV report showing password status, access key age, and MFA adoption across all account users.

Q20. Why never commit keys to GitHub?

Ans: Automated bots scan public repos within seconds, hijacking credentials to run malicious crypto miners or steal data.
