AWS ELB & ASG - Handwritten Study Notes
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 1
AWS Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) & Auto Scaling Groups (ASG)

1. Overview

This section covers two important AWS concepts:

  • Elastic Load Balancing (ELB)
  • Auto Scaling Groups (ASG)

Before understanding ELB and ASG, three concepts are important:

  • Scalability
  • High Availability
  • Elasticity

2. Scalability

Definition

Scalability is the ability to increase or decrease computing resources to handle changes in workload or traffic.

Example

Suppose a website is running on one EC2 instance. Suddenly, traffic increases significantly.

Normal Traffic
↓
1 EC2
↓
Website

When traffic becomes high, the existing resources may not be sufficient. You can scale the resources to handle the additional load. AWS provides different ways to scale.

3. Types of Scalability

There are two major types:

  • Vertical Scaling
  • Horizontal Scaling

4. Vertical Scaling — Scaling Up

Vertical scaling means increasing the capacity of an existing EC2 instance.

t2.micro → m5.large

You increase resources such as: CPU, RAM, Computing power.

Example

Suppose your website is running on t2.micro and traffic increases. You can move to a more powerful instance type such as m5.large. The same instance now has greater computing capacity.

Memory Trick

Vertical = Make the existing machine bigger.

Small EC2
↓
Bigger EC2

5. Horizontal Scaling — Scaling Out

Horizontal scaling means adding more EC2 instances. Instead of making one server bigger, you add multiple servers.

Before:

EC2 ↓ Website

After:

EC2 #1 ↓ EC2 #2 ↓ EC2 #3 ↓ EC2 #4

All instances can work together to handle incoming traffic.

Memory Trick Horizontal = Add more machines.

6. Vertical vs Horizontal Scaling

Feature Vertical Scaling Horizontal Scaling
Also called Scaling Up Scaling Out
Method Increase capacity of one instance Add more instances
Example t2.micro → m5.large 1 EC2 → 3 EC2
Main resource CPU/RAM/compute power Number of servers
Multiple servers No Yes
Easy Memory Trick

Scale Up = Bigger Server

Scale Out = More Servers

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 2

7. High Availability (HA)

Definition

High Availability means keeping an application/service available with minimal downtime. The goal is: Users should be able to access the application even if a resource or infrastructure component fails.

Example

Suppose your website is running on one EC2 instance. If that EC2 instance fails:

EC2
↓
Website
↓
FAILURE
↓
Website Down

This creates a single point of failure.

8. High Availability Using Multiple Availability Zones

To improve availability, you can run resources across multiple Availability Zones (AZs).

Availability Zone A
↓
EC2 #1
Availability Zone B
↓
EC2 #2

If one Availability Zone experiences a problem, the other can continue serving users.

Key Idea High Availability = Keep the application running despite failures.

9. Scalability vs High Availability

Scalability High Availability
Handles increasing/decreasing workload Handles failures and reduces downtime
Focuses on capacity Focuses on availability
Adds or increases resources Uses redundancy
Example: Add EC2 instances Example: Run EC2 across AZs
Simple Memory Trick

Scalability = Can I handle more traffic?

High Availability = Can I stay online if something fails?

10. Elasticity

Definition

Elasticity is the ability to automatically adjust resources according to demand.

Traffic increases
↓
Add resources automatically
↓
Traffic decreases
↓
Remove unnecessary resources

Example

Suppose normally you need: 2 EC2 instances

During peak traffic: 2 → 5 EC2 instances

When traffic becomes normal: 5 → 2 EC2 instances

This automatic adjustment is the key idea behind elasticity.

11. Elasticity vs Scalability

A useful distinction from this section:

  • Scalability → Ability to increase/decrease capacity.
  • Elasticity → Automatic adjustment of capacity based on demand.

12. What is Elastic Load Balancing?

ELB (Elastic Load Balancing) distributes incoming traffic across multiple resources such as EC2 instances.

Instead of users directly accessing individual EC2 instances, users can access the Load Balancer.

Users ↓ Load Balancer ↓ ┌───────┬───────┬───────┐ EC2 #1 EC2 #2 EC2 #3

13. Why Do We Need a Load Balancer?

Suppose you have three EC2 instances running the same website. The question becomes: Which EC2 instance should receive each request?

The Load Balancer handles this responsibility. It accepts incoming requests and distributes them among the available instances.

User 1 ──┐ User 2 ──┼──→ Load Balancer User 3 ──┘ │ ┌──────┼──────┐ ↓ ↓ ↓ EC2-1 EC2-2 EC2-3
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 3

14. Benefits of Load Balancing

1. Traffic Distribution: Traffic is distributed across multiple EC2 instances.

2. Improved Availability: If one instance fails, traffic can continue to healthy instances.

3. Scalability: More instances can be added behind the Load Balancer.

4. Single Point of Access: Users access the Load Balancer instead of exposing individual EC2 instances directly.

15. Load Balancer + Multiple Availability Zones

For better availability, instances can be distributed across multiple AZs.

Load Balancer │ ┌───────────┼───────────┐ ↓ ↓ ↓ AZ-A AZ-B AZ-C EC2 EC2 EC2

This provides two major benefits: Traffic distribution & Higher availability/fault tolerance.

16. ELB Types

The section introduces these load balancer types:

17. Application Load Balancer (ALB)

Primarily designed for application-level traffic: HTTP, HTTPS

Works at: OSI Layer 7 — Application Layer

Common Use Case: Websites and web applications.

User
↓
HTTP/HTTPS
↓
ALB
↓
EC2

18. Network Load Balancer (NLB)

Designed for high-performance, low-latency network traffic.

Works at: OSI Layer 4 — Transport Layer (TCP, UDP, TLS)

Common Use Cases: High-performance apps, real-time apps, gaming, financial apps.

19. Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB)

Designed to deploy and manage third-party virtual appliances. Examples include: Firewalls, Monitoring solutions, Security appliances.

Client
↓
GWLB
↓
Third-Party Appliance
↓
Server

20. Load Balancer Type Comparison

Load Balancer Layer Main Use
ALB Layer 7 HTTP/HTTPS applications
NLB Layer 4 TCP/UDP/TLS, high performance
GWLB Gateway/network appliance use Third-party virtual appliances
Classic LB Older generation Legacy use
Quick Memory ALB → Application | NLB → Network | GWLB → Gateway / Appliances

21. Practical ELB Architecture  |  22. Creating EC2 Instances

Internet │ ↓ Application LB │ Target Group / \ / \ ↓ ↓ EC2 Web #1 EC2 Web #2

For a basic Load Balancer practical, at least two EC2 instances are useful because the purpose is to distribute traffic.

Configuration: Each EC2 instance has: Amazon Linux, Web server (httpd), Simple website.

23. Using User Data

Instead of manually installing the web server, User Data can automate the setup:

Launch EC2↓User Data executes↓Install httpd↓Start httpd↓Create website

24. Using Hostname to Test

A useful testing technique is to display the hostname of the EC2 instance on the webpage.

Welcome to Web Server
Hostname: server-1

Now, when the Load Balancer distributes requests, you can identify which server responded.

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 4

Components of Load Balancer Setup (25 - 29)

25. Availability Zones

For better High Availability, place instances in different Availability Zones: AZ-A → EC2 #1, AZ-B → EC2 #2. This improves fault tolerance.

26. Security Group

The Load Balancer needs an appropriate Security Group. For an HTTP website: HTTP | Port 80 | Source: Anywhere.

27 & 28. Target Group

A Target Group contains the targets to which the Load Balancer forwards requests.

Config: Target type → EC2 instances | Protocol → HTTP | Port → 80 | Health check → HTTP

29. Listener

The Load Balancer listens for incoming requests on a specified port (e.g., HTTP : 80).

30. Complete Request Flow

User │ ↓ Load Balancer │ HTTP : 80 Listener │ ↓ Target Group / \ / \ ↓ ↓ EC2 #1 EC2 #2 │ │ ↓ ↓ Website Website

31. Health Checks & Fault Tolerance

A Load Balancer checks whether registered targets are healthy. If an instance stops responding (Unhealthy), the Load Balancer can stop sending traffic to it.

Key Benefit Traffic is sent to healthy targets.

33. Testing Distribution: Refreshing the webpage can show different hostnames (Server 1, Server 2), proving load distribution.

34 & 35. When an Instance Stops

If EC2 #2 stops, ELB detects it as Unhealthy and routes all traffic to EC2 #1. This demonstrates fault tolerance.

Important: Health checks take time. Do not expect the health status to change instantly when an instance stops or starts.

36. Auto Scaling Group (ASG)

ASG = Auto Scaling Group

An Auto Scaling Group automatically manages the number of EC2 instances according to defined requirements and policies. It can: Add EC2 instances, Remove EC2 instances, Replace unhealthy instances, Maintain a desired number of instances.

37. Why Do We Need ASG?

Manually managing EC2 instances during high/low traffic is inefficient. ASG automates the process.

38. ASG and Elasticity

ASG provides elasticity. High Traffic → 4 EC2. Low Traffic → 2 EC2. Automatic adjustment.

39. Main Functions of ASG

  • 1. Automatic Scaling: Increase or decrease instances.
  • 2. Health Management: Replace unhealthy instances.
  • 3. Maintain Desired Capacity: Keep a specific number running.
  • 4. Scaling Policies: Rules based on CPU or request count.
  • 5. Scheduled Scaling: Scale at specific predictable times.
  • 6. Multi-AZ Deployment: Distribute across AZs for HA.
  • 7. Load Balancer Integration: Works with ELB to distribute traffic to the scaled instances.
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 5

40. Very Important — ELB vs ASG

A common confusion is: "Does ASG distribute traffic?" No.

ELB

Handles: Traffic distribution

ASG

Handles: Number of EC2 instances

41. ELB + ASG Together

Users │ ↓ Load Balancer │ ↓ Target Group │ ┌───────────┼───────────┐ ↓ ↓ ↓ EC2 #1 EC2 #2 EC2 #3 ↑ ↑ ↑ └──────── Auto Scaling ────────┘

Together they provide: Scalability, Elasticity, High Availability, Fault tolerance.

42. Desired, Minimum and Maximum Capacity

Minimum Capacity: Minimum number of instances (e.g., Min = 1)

Desired Capacity: Normal/target number of instances (e.g., Desired = 2)

Maximum Capacity: Maximum instances ASG can create (e.g., Max = 3)

Normal condition: 2 instances

High demand: 2 → 3 instances

Low demand: 2 → 1 instance

43 & 44. ASG + Launch Templates & AMIs

ASG needs a way to know how new EC2 instances should be launched. This is why a Launch Template is important.

AMI
↓
Launch Template
↓
ASG
↓
Creates EC2

You need an AMI so you don't launch empty instances. The AMI contains the web server, application, and configuration.

45. ASG Creation Flow

1. Create AMI → 2. Create/Use Launch Template → 3. Create Auto Scaling Group ↓ 4. Select AZs/Subnets → 5. Attach Load Balancer → 6. Configure Health Checks ↓ 7. Set Minimum/Desired/Maximum → 8. Configure Scaling Policy → 9. Create ASG

48. Multiple AZs

ASG can distribute instances across AZ-A, AZ-B, AZ-C to ensure if one zone fails, others continue.

49 & 50. LB & Health

ASG uses the ELB Target Group. ASG can use LB health checks to detect and replace unhealthy instances automatically.

Scaling Policies (51 - 54)

  • CPU-Based Scaling: e.g., Target Average CPU Utilization = 50%. ASG attempts to maintain this target.
  • Request-Based Scaling: More Requests → Higher Load → Add Instances.
  • Scheduled Scaling: Useful when traffic patterns are known (e.g., 6 PM → Increase, 12 AM → Reduce).
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 6

55. Maintaining Desired Capacity

If Desired = 2, and one instance is manually terminated, ASG notices the shortage and launches a replacement. ASG tries to maintain the configured capacity. (Sec 56: You can view Activity History to see what happened and why).

57. Practical Example — Complete Architecture

Traffic Flow:

User → Load Balancer → Target Group → Healthy EC2

Scaling Flow:

High Traffic → Scaling Policy → ASG → Launch new EC2 → Target Group → Load Balancer

59 & 60. Cleanup After Practical Work

Important Rule: Delete the ASG First!

If you manually terminate instances while the ASG is active, ASG sees capacity below desired and will just launch replacements. Delete ASG → Delete LB → Terminate EC2.

61. Most Important Differences

Scalability vs HA Scalability = Handle workload. HA = Minimize downtime.
Vertical vs Horizontal Vertical = Bigger instance. Horizontal = More instances.
ELB vs ASG ELB = Distributes traffic. ASG = Manages EC2 capacity.
AMI vs Launch Template AMI = Machine image. Launch Template = EC2 launch config.
AMI → What should the EC2 contain? Launch Template → How should EC2 be launched? ASG → How many EC2 instances should exist? ELB → Where should user traffic go?

62. Interview Questions (Summary)

Q9. Does ASG distribute traffic?
No. ELB distributes traffic. ASG manages capacity.
Q12. What is an ALB?
Application Load Balancer (Layer 7 - HTTP/HTTPS).
Q13. What is an NLB?
Network Load Balancer (Layer 4 - TCP/UDP, high perf).
Q16. What is Min/Desired/Max?
Min allowed, target normal, max allowed capacity.
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 7

63. Quick Revision Sheet

Scalability: Handle changing workload.
Vertical: 1 EC2 → Bigger EC2
Horizontal: 1 EC2 → Multiple EC2

High Availability:
Multiple resources + Multiple AZs = Higher availability.

Elasticity:
High Demand → Add resources
Low Demand → Remove resources

ALB: Layer 7 | HTTP/HTTPS | Web apps
NLB: Layer 4 | TCP/UDP/TLS | High perf
GWLB: Firewalls / monitoring appliances

ELB: Main job → Distribute traffic
ASG: Main job → Manage EC2 capacity

64. Final Memory Map

AWS APPLICATION │ ▼ LOAD BALANCER │ Distributes Traffic │ ▼ TARGET GROUP │ ┌─────────────┼─────────────┐ ↓ ↓ ↓ EC2 EC2 EC2 ↑ ↑ ↑ └─────────────┼─────────────┘ │ ▼ AUTO SCALING GROUP │ Manages Instance Count │ ┌────────────┴────────────┐ ↓ ↓ Scale Out/In Replace Unhealthy

The 5 Things to Remember

  1. Scalability → Handle more workload.
  2. High Availability → Stay available despite failures.
  3. Elasticity → Automatically adjust capacity.
  4. ELB → Distribute traffic.
  5. ASG → Automatically manage EC2 instance count.
⭐ One-Line Architecture

ELB distributes traffic, ASG manages EC2 capacity, AMI provides the machine image, and Launch Template defines how new EC2 instances are launched.

AWS S3 (Simple Storage Service) - Handwritten Study Notes
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 1
AWS S3 (Simple Storage Service)

1. Introduction to Amazon S3

Amazon S3 = Simple Storage Service

Amazon S3 is an AWS cloud-based object storage service used to store, manage, and retrieve large amounts of data.

Common Uses of S3

S3 can store:

  • Images, Videos, Documents
  • Backup files, Logs
  • Application data
  • Static website files
  • Archived data
Main Idea

S3 = Bucket + Objects

Bucket → Container where data is stored

Object → Individual file/data stored inside the bucket

2. What is an S3 Bucket?

An S3 bucket is a container used to store objects.

For example:

S3 └── Bucket ├── index.html ├── style.css ├── image1.jpg └── image2.jpg

Important Properties of a Bucket

1. Globally Unique Bucket Name: An S3 bucket name must be globally unique across AWS. It is not enough for the name to be unique only inside your account. Example: demo-bucket-abc12345

2. Region-Specific: When you create a bucket, you select an AWS Region. Example: Bucket → Stockholm Region. The bucket belongs to that selected AWS Region.

3. Objects are Stored Inside Buckets: Files uploaded to S3 are treated as objects. So remember: Bucket = Container | Object = File/Data inside the container.

3. S3 Object Model  |  4. Maximum Object Size

An S3 object can be understood using a simple Key–Value concept.

Key: The key identifies the object. Example: index.html (Key = index.html).

Value: The actual contents/data of the file are the value. Example: HTML code inside index.html.

Object ├── Key → index.html └── Value → HTML file contents

According to the course material: Maximum size of a single S3 object = 5 TB.

For very large objects, multipart upload is used/recommended. A large file can be divided into smaller parts and uploaded separately.

Large File → Parts 1-4 → S3 combines parts

Why? It makes large-file uploads easier to manage and can improve reliability.

5. S3 Data Durability and Availability

S3 is designed to provide highly reliable object storage. The transcript explains that S3 data is replicated across multiple Availability Zones (AZs) within the selected Region.

AWS Region │ ├── Availability Zone 1 ├── Availability Zone 2 └── Availability Zone 3

This helps protect data against failures affecting an individual Availability Zone.

Important

Do not confuse: Region and Availability Zone. A bucket is created in a Region, not in a specific Availability Zone.

6. Creating an S3 Bucket

Basic process: Open AWS Console → Search for S3 → Select Create bucket → Choose bucket type → Select AWS Region → Enter globally unique bucket name → Configure settings → Create bucket.

After creation, the bucket becomes a container for storing objects.

7. Uploading Files to S3

Bucket ↓ Upload ↓ Select/Review Files ↓ Upload

Inside a bucket, you can upload: Individual files, Multiple files, Folders, or use drag-and-drop. After successful upload, the objects appear inside the bucket.

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 2

8. Working with S3 Objects

After uploading an object, several operations can be performed. Common Operations: Open, Download, Delete, View properties, Change storage class, Manage versions.

For example: index.html, style.css, image.jpg. A text-based object can be opened and inspected, while an image object can be opened to view the image.

9 & 10 & 11. Hosting a Static Website on S3

One important use case of S3 is Static Website Hosting. A static website may contain: index.html, style.css, image1.jpg, image2.jpg. There is no server-side application logic required for a basic static website.

Website Structure │ ├── index.html (Main/Default) ├── style.css ├── image1.jpg └── image2.jpg

Steps to Host:

Step 1: Upload Website Files to the S3 bucket.

Step 2: Enable Static Website Hosting. (Bucket → Properties → Static website hosting).

Specify: Index document → index.html, Error document → error.html

12. Why "Access Denied" Can Occur  |  13. Block Public Access

Simply enabling static website hosting does not automatically make the objects publicly accessible. You need appropriate permissions.

Static Website Hosting
+
Public Access Permission
↓
Website Accessible
Important Warning

S3 provides Block Public Access settings. If public website access is required, the relevant public-access blocking configuration must be adjusted appropriately.

Public access should be enabled only when required. Making an S3 bucket public can expose its contents to the internet. Always understand what data is being made public before changing public-access settings.

14. S3 Bucket Policy  |  15. Important Actions

A Bucket Policy is a JSON-based policy attached to an S3 bucket. It controls: Who can access the bucket, What actions they can perform, Which resources the policy applies to. (It defines: Who can do what on which resource?)

Easy Memory Trick

GetObject → Used to retrieve/read/download an object. (s3:GetObject) | GET → Get/Read object

PutObject → Used to upload/write an object. (s3:PutObject) | PUT → Upload/Write object

16. Bucket Policy Structure

Policy │ ├── Effect → Allow / Deny ├── Principal→ Who? ├── Action → What can they do? └── Resource → Which resource?

Principal: Defines who gets permission. Action: Defines what the user/service can do (e.g. s3:GetObject). Resource: Defines the bucket/object.

17. Policy Generator  |  18. Static Website Access — Overall Flow

If you are not comfortable writing JSON manually, AWS provides a Policy Generator.

Select Type→Effect=Allow→Action→Resource→Generate→Copy JSON

18. The Complete Static Website Access Concept:

Website Files → S3 Bucket
↓
Enable Static Website Hosting
↓
Configure Public Access → Bucket Policy → Allow Required Object Access
↓
Website Endpoint → Website Accessible
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 3

19. S3 Versioning

What is Versioning?

S3 Versioning keeps multiple versions of an object.

Suppose you upload: index.html → Version 1. Then modify it and upload again: index.html → Version 2. S3 can keep both versions.

index.html ├── Version 1 └── Version 2

20. Why Versioning is Useful

Versioning helps with: Accidental overwrites, Accidental deletion, Data recovery, Maintaining previous versions, Backup-like protection.

Example: Version 1 → Old Website | Version 2 → Updated Website. If Version 2 causes a problem, you can recover/use the previous version.

21. Important Point

When versioning is enabled, new versions uploaded after enabling versioning receive version IDs. Objects uploaded before versioning was enabled may appear with: Version ID = null.

22. S3 Versioning Example  |  23. Accidental Deletion

Upload index.html→Version 1→Modify/Upload→Version 2→Modify/Upload→Version 3 (Current)

S3 maintains the different versions. The latest version is normally used as the current object.

Key Concept Versioning = Protection against accidental changes/deletion. If the current version is removed, an earlier version may still be available depending on the deletion operation and versioning state.

24. S3 Replication

S3 supports automatic replication of objects between buckets. Two important scenarios are:

1. Same-Region Replication

Data can be replicated between buckets in the same AWS Region.

Primary Bucket ↓ Replication ↓ Secondary Bucket

2. Cross-Region Replication

Objects can be replicated to a bucket in another AWS Region.

Mumbai Region (Primary) ↓ Cross-Region Replication ↓ Europe Region (Secondary)

25. Why Use S3 Replication?

Common use cases include:

  • Backup: Maintain another copy of important data.
  • Disaster Recovery: If the primary location has problems, another copy exists elsewhere.
  • Geographic Data Access: Data can be replicated closer to users in another geographical region.

26. Requirements  |  27. Practical Flow  |  28. Existing Objects

A destination bucket must already exist before replication can be configured. Replication is generally configured using a replication rule. (Source Bucket → Replication Rule → Destination Bucket). You can configure replication for all objects or specific objects/prefixes.

27. Practical Flow

Create destination bucket → Enable versioning → Open source bucket → Management → Create replication rule → Select source scope → Select destination bucket → Configure IAM role/permissions → Configure options → Save rule.

28. Existing vs New Objects

When configuring replication, there can be an option/process for handling existing objects as well as objects uploaded after the rule is created. Existing Objects + Future Objects. The exact behavior depends on the configuration.

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 4

29. S3 Storage Classes

AWS provides different S3 Storage Classes. Why? Because different types of data have different: Access frequencies, Retention requirements, Performance requirements, Cost requirements. Choose the storage class according to your workload.

30. S3 Standard

Use Case: Frequently accessed data (website files, app data).
Characteristics: High durability, high availability, low latency.

31. S3 Intelligent-Tiering

Automatically moves data between appropriate access tiers based on usage patterns. Frequent Access → suitable tier, Infrequent Access → lower-cost tier. Best when access patterns are unknown.

32. S3 Standard-IA

IA = Infrequent Access. Used for data that must remain readily available but is accessed less frequently (e.g., occasional backups). Lower storage cost, but retrieval charges apply.

33. S3 One Zone-IA

Designed for infrequently accessed data where lower storage cost is important and data can tolerate a single AZ. Use Case: Non-critical or reproducible data (temporary logs, secondary copies). Do not choose blindly for critical data.

34. S3 Glacier

Designed for long-term archival. Good for data that is rarely accessed and needs long-term retention (old records, historical data).

35. S3 Glacier Deep Archive

Designed for very long-term archival with very low storage cost. Example: Compliance records retained for many years.

36. S3 Outposts

S3 Outposts provides S3 storage capabilities using AWS infrastructure deployed through AWS Outposts for workloads that require local/on-premises data residency or processing characteristics.

Memory Trick
Frequent→Standard | Less Frequent→Standard-IA | Rare→Glacier | Very Long-term→Deep Archive

37. Storage Class Selection

A simple decision-making approach:

Requirement Suitable Class
Frequently accessed dataS3 Standard
Unknown/changing access patternS3 Intelligent-Tiering
Infrequently accessed dataS3 Standard-IA
Infrequent, non-critical/re-creatable dataS3 One Zone-IA
Long-term archiveS3 Glacier
Very long-term archive/complianceS3 Glacier Deep Archive
AWS Outposts local storage use caseS3 Outposts

Always check current AWS pricing and storage-class conditions before making a production decision.

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 5

38. S3 Lifecycle Rules

What is a Lifecycle Rule? An S3 Lifecycle rule automatically manages objects as they age or become less relevant. It can: Transition objects between storage classes, Expire/delete objects, Manage old versions in versioned buckets.

39. Example Lifecycle Policy

Suppose website data is frequently accessed for the first month:

Day 0 → S3 Standard ↓ After 30 days → S3 Standard-IA ↓ After 60 days → S3 One Zone-IA / lower-cost tier ↓ After 90 days → Archive storage ↓ After required retention period → Delete

40. Benefits of Lifecycle Rules

  • Reduce Cost: Old data automatically moves to cheaper storage.
  • Automate Data Mgmt: No manual moving needed.
  • Manage Retention: Data automatically expires.
  • Operational Efficiency: Upload → Store → Transition → Archive → Delete (automatic).

41. S3 Glacier — Key Idea  |  42. S3 Storage Cost Concept

Think of Glacier as: Cold/Archive Storage. It is suitable when data is stored mainly for retention rather than frequent access. (Historical records, backup archives, compliance data).

42. S3 Storage Cost Concept: S3 costs depend on factors such as amount of data stored, storage class, requests, data retrieval, data transfer, and lifecycle/replication configs. More data + more operations can mean higher cost. Lifecycle rules and appropriate classes help optimize costs.

AWS Snow Family (43 - 48)

The AWS Snow Family is used for moving large amounts of data and for certain edge-computing use cases. It becomes useful when transferring huge datasets over the internet would be: Too slow, Difficult, Expensive, Operationally challenging.

Concept: Imagine an organization has 10 TB of data. Uploading over internet takes too long. AWS provides physical devices to transfer data.

Your Data Center→AWS Snow Device→Ship Device to AWS→AWS imports data to S3

45. Snowcone

Snowcone is a small and portable device intended for smaller-scale data transfer and edge use cases.
Memory: Snowcone = Small + Portable

46. Snowball

Snowball is a larger device designed for transferring much larger quantities of data. Supports some edge computing.
Memory: Snowball → Larger

47. Snowmobile

Snowmobile is designed for extremely large-scale data transfers. Think of it as a massive data-transfer solution (truck/container-scale) for very large datasets.
Memory: Snowcone (Small) → Snowball (Large) → Snowmobile (Massive)

48. Snow Family — Exam Memory Table

ServiceMain Idea
SnowconeSmall, portable data transfer/edge device
SnowballLarge-scale data transfer and edge computing
SnowmobileExtremely large-scale data migration
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 6

49 & 50 & 51. AWS Storage Gateway

AWS Storage Gateway is a hybrid cloud storage service. Hybrid Cloud Meaning: A hybrid environment combines: On-Premises Infrastructure + AWS Cloud.

Suppose a company has an On-Premises Application in a Local Data Center but wants to use AWS storage services. Storage Gateway can provide a bridge between on-premises environments and AWS storage.

On-Premises Application ↓ Storage Gateway ↓ AWS Storage

51. Storage Gateway Types:

  • File Gateway: File-based access to AWS storage.
  • Volume Gateway: Block-storage-oriented functionality.
  • Tape Gateway: Virtual tape for backup/archive workflows.

52. S3 vs Snow Family vs Storage Gateway

ServiceMain Purpose
S3Cloud object storage
S3 GlacierLong-term archive
Snow FamilyLarge-scale physical data transfer / edge
Storage GatewayHybrid on-premises + AWS storage
Easy Memory Trick S3 → Store data in cloud | Snow → Physically move huge amounts of data | Storage Gateway → Connect on-premises storage with AWS

53 & 54. S3 Encryption & Security Concepts

Data security is an important part of S3. Encryption protects data by making it unreadable without the appropriate decryption mechanism. S3 supports encryption options for protecting data at rest.

Data→Encryption→Protected Storage

54. S3 Security Areas: Block Public Access, Bucket Policies, IAM Permissions, Encryption, Versioning.

55. Important S3 Concepts — One-Page Revision

  • S3: Object storage service.
  • Bucket: Container for objects. Name is globally unique. Tied to an AWS Region.
  • Object: Individual file/data (Max size: 5 TB).
  • Versioning: Maintains multiple versions.
  • Replication: Copies objects between buckets.
  • Bucket Policy: JSON-based access-control.
  • GetObject: Retrieve/read object.
  • PutObject: Upload/write object.
  • Static Website: Host static website files.
  • Lifecycle: Automate transition/expiration.
  • Storage Classes: Options based on access.
  • Snow Family: Large-scale physical transfer.
  • Storage Gateway: Hybrid storage.

56. S3 Practical Workflow — Complete

Creating a Bucket: AWS Console → S3 → Create Bucket → Region → Unique Name → Create Uploading Files: Bucket → Upload → Select Files → Review → Upload Static Website: Upload Website → Enable Hosting → index.html → Access Config → Policy → Endpoint Versioning: Bucket → Enable Versioning → Upload New Version → Previous Versions Maintained Replication: Source Bucket → Replication Rule → Destination Bucket Lifecycle: New Object → Standard → IA → Archive → Expiration/Delete
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 7

57. Important Interview Questions

Q1. What is Amazon S3?
Amazon S3 is an AWS object storage service used to store, manage, and retrieve large amounts of data.
Q2. What is an S3 bucket?
A bucket is a container used to store S3 objects.
Q3. What is an S3 object?
An object is an individual piece of data/file stored inside an S3 bucket.
Q4. Difference between bucket and object?
Bucket → Container | Object → File/Data inside the container
Q5. Must an S3 bucket name be unique?
Yes. The bucket name must be globally unique.
Q6. What is S3 Versioning?
Versioning allows S3 to maintain multiple versions of an object.
Q7. Why is versioning useful?
Protects against accidental overwrites/deletions and allows previous versions to be recovered.
Q8. What is a Bucket Policy?
A JSON-based resource policy used to control access to an S3 bucket and its objects.
Q9. What does GetObject mean?
It allows retrieval/read access to an S3 object.
Q10. What does PutObject mean?
It allows an object to be uploaded/written to S3.
Q11. What is S3 Lifecycle?
A lifecycle config automatically transitions or expires objects based on rules such as age.
Q12. Why are different Storage Classes available?
To optimize storage according to: Access frequency, Retention period, Retrieval requirements, Cost.
Q13. What is S3 Intelligent-Tiering?
A storage class designed to automatically optimize storage costs based on changing access patterns.
Q14. What is S3 Glacier used for?
Long-term archival and rarely accessed data.
Q15. What is Glacier Deep Archive?
A very low-cost storage option intended for long-term archival and retention.
Q16. What is S3 Replication?
It automatically copies eligible objects from a source bucket to a destination bucket.
Q17. What is Cross-Region Replication?
Replication of objects from a bucket in one AWS Region to a bucket in another Region.
Q18. What is the Snow Family?
Provides physical devices/services for large-scale data transfer and edge-computing.
Q19. What is AWS Storage Gateway?
A hybrid cloud storage service that connects on-premises environments with AWS storage.

58. Quick Memory Map

AMAZON S3 │ ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐ │ │ │ Bucket Object Security │ │ │ Container File Policy / IAM Encryption Public Access │ ├── Versioning │ ├── Replication │ ├── Lifecycle │ ├── Static Website │ └── Storage Classes │ ┌─────────┼─────────┐ │ │ │ Standard IA Glacier │ │ Frequent Archive Access

59. Final Exam Revision

Remember these 10 key points:

  • S3 = Simple Storage Service
  • Bucket = Container
  • Object = File/Data
  • Bucket names are globally unique
  • Buckets are created in a selected Region
  • Versioning maintains multiple object versions
  • Bucket Policies control resource access
  • Lifecycle Rules automate transitions and expiration
  • Storage Classes help optimize cost according to access patterns
  • Snow Family + Storage Gateway solve specialized data-transfer and hybrid-storage requirements

AWS RDS - Handwritten Study Notes
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 1
AWS RDS (Relational Database Service)

1. What is AWS RDS?

Amazon RDS (Relational Database Service) is a managed relational database service provided by AWS.

It allows you to create, operate, scale, monitor, back up, and maintain relational databases without managing the underlying database infrastructure manually.

Relational Data

Relational data is generally organized into: Tables, Rows, Columns.

Example:

IDNameEmail
1Rajuraju@email.com
2Shamsham@email.com

Popular relational database systems include:

MySQL PostgreSQL Oracle Microsoft SQL Server MariaDB

AWS RDS supports several popular relational database engines.

2. Why Use RDS?

Normally, if you install MySQL yourself on a server, you are responsible for many administrative tasks. With RDS, AWS manages much of the underlying database infrastructure.

Important RDS Benefits

  • Automated maintenance
  • Monitoring & Backups
  • Scaling options
  • High Availability & Fault tolerance
  • Read replicas & Recovery options
  • Security controls
  • Easier database administration

Simple Example

Without RDS:

EC2→Install MySQL→Configure MySQL→Patch→Monitor→Backup→Maintain

With RDS:

Application→RDS

AWS handles many of the infrastructure-management tasks for you.

Key Concept RDS is a managed database service, not simply a database installed manually on an EC2 instance.

3. RDS Practical Use Case

A common architecture is:

User
↓
Browser
↓
EC2 / Application
↓
RDS (MySQL)
↓
Relational Data

In this example: EC2 hosts the frontend/application. Docker runs the Node.js application. RDS hosts the MySQL database. User data is stored in RDS.

Example Application

A simple contact-management application can allow users to: 1. Enter an email address. 2. Click Add. 3. Store the email in MySQL. 4. Display stored contacts. 5. Delete contacts.

4. Technologies Used in the Practical

AWS Services

  • EC2 – application server
  • RDS – database service

App Technologies

  • Node.js
  • Docker
  • MySQL
Architecture Browser | ↓ EC2 | Docker Container | Node.js Application | ↓ RDS | MySQL | Database

This is a useful real-world example because it demonstrates how different cloud components work together.

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 2

5. Creating an RDS Database

Go to the AWS Console and search for: RDS → Relational Database Service
Then: Databases → Create database

AWS provides different creation approaches.

Easy Create

Designed to make database creation simpler and faster. AWS automatically chooses many configuration options based on the selected use case.

Typical choices include:

  • Production
  • Test
  • Free Tier

Standard Create

Gives you much greater control over database configuration.

For learning and practical purposes, Standard Create is useful because you can understand individual configuration options.

6. Selecting the Database Engine

For the practical, MySQL is selected. RDS supports multiple database engines, such as:

MySQL PostgreSQL MariaDB Oracle Microsoft SQL Server

The database engine should be selected according to the application's requirements.

7. Templates

RDS provides templates based on the intended workload. Typical options include:

  • Free Tier: Useful for learning, practice, testing, small experiments.
  • Production: Designed for production workloads where requirements such as High Availability, Performance, Reliability, Fault tolerance are more important.
  • Test/Development: Useful for development and testing environments.

8. High Availability in RDS

For production environments, RDS can be configured across multiple Availability Zones (AZs).

AWS Region | ----------------------- | | | AZ-1 AZ-2 AZ-3 | | | DB-1 DB-2 DB-3

The exact architecture depends on the selected RDS configuration.

Important Point High Availability helps protect the application from failures affecting a single Availability Zone.

9. RDS Instance vs RDS Cluster

The transcript distinguishes between database instances and clusters.

Instance-based setup

A primary database instance handles database operations while another instance can remain available for failover depending on the configuration.

Primary DB ↓ Replication ↓ Standby DB

If primary fails, AWS performs failover.

Cluster-based setup

A cluster can provide multiple database instances with capabilities designed for higher availability and/or read scalability, depending on the selected RDS database technology.

10. Storage & Auto Scaling

RDS provides storage options such as SSD-based storage. Storage configuration can include: Allocated storage, Storage type, Storage scaling, Performance-related settings.

Storage Auto Scaling

Storage Auto Scaling can automatically increase allocated database storage when the database approaches its storage capacity.

Capacity Limit→Usage Increases→Threshold Reached→Storage Automatically Increases

This helps reduce the risk of the database running out of storage.

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 3

11. Database Credentials

When creating an RDS database, you configure credentials for accessing the database. Common credentials include Master username and Master password.

Username: admin
Password: ********

Security Reminder

  • Do not use simple passwords.
  • Do not expose database credentials publicly.
  • Do not hard-code passwords into application source code.
  • Use secure secret-management practices.

12. Connectivity

One important RDS configuration is deciding how the database will be accessed. The database may need to communicate with: EC2, Application servers, Other AWS resources, External systems (depending on the architecture).

The networking configuration includes: VPC, Subnets, Security Groups, Public/private accessibility.

13. Public Access

The practical demonstrates a database configured for public access so that it can be accessed during testing. However:

Publicly accessible databases are generally not recommended for production unless there is a specific security requirement and the network access is tightly controlled.

A better production architecture is usually:

Internet→Load Balancer→Application / EC2→Private RDS

The database should generally be protected from direct public Internet access.

14. RDS Security Groups

A Security Group acts as a virtual firewall controlling network traffic to the RDS instance. For MySQL, the standard port is: TCP 3306.

Source → Allowed
Port → 3306
Protocol → TCP

Practical Setup vs Production

The transcript opens MySQL port 3306 to a broad source for testing. However, this is not recommended for production. A more secure approach is:

EC2 Security Group
→ TCP 3306 →
RDS Security Group

This allows the database to accept connections specifically from the application server rather than from the entire Internet.

15 - 18. Application Setup (EC2 & Docker)

15. EC2 App Server

After creating RDS, an EC2 instance is prepared for the Node.js application (Example name: Node App). The EC2 instance hosts the application.

16. Installing Docker

Install Docker↓Start Service↓Check Status↓Pull Image↓Run Container

17. Docker Image

The practical uses a pre-built Docker image containing the Node.js application pulled from a registry.

Docker Registry→docker pull→EC2 Image

18. Port Mapping

The Node.js application listens on port 3000. HTTP port exposed to users is 80.

EC2 Port 80→Container Port 3000

Users access via HTTP (80), container listens internally on 3000.

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 4

19. Connecting Node.js to RDS  |  20. Env Variables

The Node.js application needs database connection information. The RDS endpoint acts as the database host. The practical uses environment variables to provide this info.

DB_HOST = RDS Endpoint DB_USER = admin DB_PASSWORD = ******** DB_NAME = myapp DB_PORT = 3306

Why Env Variables?

They help separate configuration from application code. Instead of writing credentials directly into source code (password = "..."), the application can read them from its environment. For production, use secure secret-management.

21. Testing  |  22. Application CRUD Operations

Once the Docker container is running: Get EC2 public IP → Open browser → Enter IP → Access application.

Browser→EC2 IP (Port 80)→Docker→Node.js→RDS MySQL

The practical demonstrates basic database operations (CRUD):

CRUDMeaning
CCreate (Add email)
RRead (Display contacts)
UUpdate
DDelete (Remove contact)

23. Accessing RDS from Terminal  |  24. Useful SQL

RDS can also be accessed using a MySQL client. The practical uses a Docker-based MySQL client from the EC2 server.

EC2 Terminal→MySQL Client→RDS Endpoint→Database

Useful MySQL Queries

SHOW DATABASES; USE myapp; SHOW TABLES; SELECT * FROM contacts;

The transcript demonstrates that when a new email is added through the application, it becomes visible when querying the database directly. This shows the complete data flow.

RDS Operations (25 - 28)

25. Monitoring: RDS provides monitoring capabilities. Important metrics include: CPU utilization, Database connections, Storage usage, Database activity, Performance-related metrics.

26. Current Activity: The RDS dashboard can show information about active database connections (e.g. Connection 1 → App, Connection 2 → Terminal). This helps identify how many clients are connected.

27. Logs and Events: RDS provides info about logs, events, and operational activities (creation, restart, shutdown, maintenance). Useful for troubleshooting.

28. Maintenance: AWS performs maintenance (engine updates, patches). RDS provides a maintenance window. Key Point: Managed service does not mean zero maintenance. AWS handles infrastructure, but DB still has requirements.

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 5

29 - 32. Automated Backups & Snapshots

29. Automated Backups: Supports data recovery, point-in-time recovery, protection against accidental changes, and disaster recovery. Retention depends on config.

30. RDS Snapshots

A DB snapshot is a point-in-time backup of an RDS database. It can later be used to restore a database.

RDS Database↓Snapshot↓Stored State

31. Restoring & 32. Manual

If database is deleted, but snapshot exists:

Snapshot→Restore→New DB

Manual Snapshot: Useful to preserve a specific state before major changes, testing, migration, or risky config changes.

33. Snapshot Copy Across Regions  |  34. Sharing

Mumbai Region→Snapshot→Copy→Another Region

This supports: Disaster recovery, regional migration, business continuity, geographic redundancy. RDS snapshots can also be shared with other AWS accounts for cross-account migration and collaboration.

35. Multi-AZ Deployment  |  36. Read Replicas

35. Multi-AZ: Primarily designed for High Availability and failover.

RDS | ---------------- | | Primary Standby AZ-1 AZ-2 | | Sync replication ↓

If primary fails, AWS performs failover. Multi-AZ is for HA, not read scaling.

36. Read Replica: Designed to improve read scalability.

Primary / \ ↓ ↓ Read Replica Read Replica

Primary handles writes, replicas handle reads. Reduces read workload on the primary database.

37. Multi-Region Read Replica  |  38. Multi-AZ vs Read Replica

A primary instance exists in one Region and a read replica exists in another. Benefits: lower latency for closer users, geographic distribution, DR strategies.

FeatureMulti-AZRead Replica
Main purposeHigh AvailabilityRead scalability
FailoverYesNot primarily the purpose
Read trafficNot the main purposeYes
SetupPrimary + standbyPrimary + replicas
Typical useFault toleranceHeavy read workload
Easy Memory Trick Multi-AZ = Availability  |  Read Replica = Read Performance
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 6

39. RDS Cluster  |  40. Aurora  |  41. Arch Comparison

39. Cluster Architecture: Multiple instances participate in a cluster (Primary = Read/Write, DB-2/DB-3 = Read).

40. Amazon Aurora: Cloud-optimized DB engine compatible with MySQL/PostgreSQL. Designed for high performance, high availability, scalability, automated management, failover.

41. Quick Comparison

  • Basic: App → RDS
  • Multi-AZ: App → Primary → Standby (HA)
  • Read Replica: App → Primary + RR1/RR2 (Read scale)
  • Multi-Region RR: Region A Primary → Region B Replica (DR/Geo read)

42. RDS Use Cases  |  43. Major Benefits

Use Cases:

  • Web Apps: Website → App → RDS
  • E-Commerce: Customers, orders, inventory.
  • Business Apps: Structured data.
  • CRM: Customer info, sales records.
  • Financial: Structured financial workloads.

Benefits:

  • Managed Service (AWS handles infra)
  • High Availability (Multi-AZ)
  • Automated Backups & Recovery (Snapshots)
  • Read Replicas (Scaling)
  • Monitoring, Security, DR, Cost Efficiency.

44. Complete Practical Arch  |  45. Data Flow

USER | ↓ WEB BROWSER | ↓ EC2 PUBLIC IP | ↓ HTTP : 80 | ↓ DOCKER CONTAINER | ↓ NODE.JS APP | ↓ MySQL Connection | ↓ RDS ENDPOINT | ↓ MySQL RDS | ↓ CONTACTS TABLE

45. End-to-End Data Flow

  1. User enters email in browser.
  2. Request reaches EC2 application.
  3. Node.js receives the request.
  4. Node.js sends a SQL query to RDS.
  5. RDS/MySQL stores the data.
  6. App retrieves stored data when requested.
User→Browser→EC2→Node.js→RDS→MySQL→Table

46. Cleanup After Practical

Delete App Resources → Terminate EC2 → Delete RDS → Remove Snapshots → Check Other Resources.

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 7

47. Important Interview Questions

Q1. What is Amazon RDS?
Amazon RDS is a managed AWS service for running relational databases.
Q2. Why use RDS instead of installing MySQL manually on EC2?
RDS reduces database administration work by providing managed capabilities such as backups, monitoring, maintenance, scaling options, and high-availability features.
Q3. Which databases can be used with RDS?
MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle, Microsoft SQL Server.
Q4. What is the default MySQL port?
3306
Q5. What is a DB snapshot?
A point-in-time saved state of an RDS database that can be used for restoration.
Q6. What is Multi-AZ?
A configuration designed primarily for high availability and failover.
Q7. What is a Read Replica?
A replicated database instance designed primarily to handle read workloads.
Q8. Multi-AZ vs Read Replica?
Multi-AZ → High Availability
Read Replica → Read Scalability
Q9. What is the RDS endpoint?
It is the network endpoint used by an application/client to connect to the RDS database.
Q10. What is Aurora?
Aurora is an AWS cloud-optimized relational database engine compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL technologies.

48. Quick Revision  |  49. One-Minute Memory Map

RDS = Managed Relational DB Service

  • Engines: MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle, SQL Server
  • Port: MySQL → 3306
  • Flow: User → EC2 → Node.js → RDS → MySQL → Tables

Remember:

  • Multi-AZ → High Availability
  • Read Replica → Read Scalability
  • Snapshot → Backup/Restore
  • Endpoint → Database Connection
  • Security Group → Network Access Control
AWS RDS | ----------------------------------- | | | Engines Features Architecture | | | MySQL/PostgreSQL Backup Single-AZ MariaDB/Oracle Snapshot Multi-AZ SQL Server Monitoring Read Replica Maintenance Multi-Region Scaling Aurora | ↓ Application | ↓ EC2 | ↓ Docker | ↓ Node.js App | ↓ RDS MySQL | ↓ Relational Data
⭐ Final Takeaway

Amazon RDS makes it easier to run relational databases on AWS without manually managing all of the underlying database infrastructure.

EC2 runs the application → RDS stores relational data → Security Groups control access → Monitoring observes performance → Backups/Snapshots support recovery → Multi-AZ provides high availability → Read Replicas improve read scalability.

AWS DynamoDB - Detailed & Structured Notes
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 1
AWS DynamoDB — Detailed & Structured Notes

1. What is Amazon DynamoDB?

Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL database service provided by AWS.

In the previous section, we studied Amazon RDS, which is mainly used for relational data.
DynamoDB is different because it is a NoSQL database designed for flexible, non-tabular data and highly scalable applications.

RDS vs DynamoDB

RDS DynamoDB
Relational database NoSQL database
Structured/tabular data Flexible, non-tabular data
Uses rows and columns Uses items and attributes
SQL-based NoSQL API-based
Schema is generally more structured Flexible schema
Example: MySQL, PostgreSQL DynamoDB

2. What is NoSQL?

NoSQL = Not Only SQL

NoSQL databases are generally designed for data that does not need to follow a rigid table structure.
A common representation is similar to JSON.

Example

{ "name": "Raju", "email": "raju@example.com", "age": 30 }

Here:
name → key/attribute  |  Raju → value
email → key/attribute  |  raju@... → value
age → key/attribute  |  30 → value
This entire object can be treated as a document/item.

Important Point

Different items in DynamoDB do not necessarily need to contain exactly the same attributes.

For example:

Item 1:
ID = 01
Username = Raju

Item 2:
ID = 02
Username = Shyam
Age = 30

The second item contains Age, while the first item does not. This demonstrates DynamoDB's flexible schema.

3. Basic DynamoDB Terminology

The most important terms are:

Table: A table is a collection where DynamoDB stores items. Example: Contacts

Item: An item is an individual record inside a DynamoDB table. Example: {"id": "01", "username": "Raju"}

Attribute: An attribute is a piece of information inside an item. Example: id, username, age, email

Simple Structure

DynamoDB │ └── Table │ ├── Item 1 │ ├── id │ └── username │ ├── Item 2 │ ├── id │ ├── username │ └── age │ └── Item 3 ├── id └── email

4. Real-World Users of DynamoDB

Large companies use DynamoDB for different workloads. Examples mentioned in the course include: Jam, Dropbox.

DynamoDB is particularly useful when applications need:

  • High scalability
  • Very low latency
  • Flexible data models
  • Large numbers of requests
  • Automatic scaling

5. DynamoDB Free Tier / Pricing Concept

The course demonstrates DynamoDB's free usage options and explains that it can handle a large number of requests. However, AWS Free Tier limits and pricing can change over time, so the exact values shown in the practical should be treated as course/demo values, not permanent limits.

Important Pricing Concept: DynamoDB can use an on-demand pricing model, where you pay based on actual request activity rather than continuously provisioning a fixed amount of database capacity. This can be particularly useful for applications with unpredictable or fluctuating traffic.

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 2

6. Creating a DynamoDB Table

The basic process is:

AWS Console
↓
Search DynamoDB
↓
DynamoDB Dashboard
↓
Create Table

In the practical, the table name is: Contacts

7. Partition Key

When creating the table, a partition key needs to be defined. Example:

Partition Key: id
Type: String

What is a Partition Key?

The partition key is used to uniquely identify items and determine how DynamoDB distributes data internally. For the simple example: id = 01, id = 02, id = 03. Each item can be identified using its key.

SQL Comparison

Conceptually, the partition key can be compared with the role of a primary key in a relational database, although DynamoDB's key design and data distribution work differently.

8. Creating Items Manually

After creating the table:

Contacts↓Explore Table Items↓Create Item

Initially, the table contains no data. Example item:

id = 01
username = Raju

Another item:

id = 02
username = Shyam

You can also add different attributes: id = 02, username = Shyam, age = 30. The important concept is that the items can have different attributes.

9. Flexible Data Model

This is one of DynamoDB's major characteristics. Consider:

Item 1

{ "id": "01", "username": "Raju" }

Item 2

{ "id": "02", "username": "Shyam", "age": 30 }

The two items don't have exactly the same set of attributes. This is different from a traditional relational table where columns are normally defined as part of the table schema.

Key Concept DynamoDB provides a flexible schema at the item/attribute level. However, the key schema still matters and must be designed properly.

10. Why DynamoDB is Serverless

DynamoDB is a fully managed serverless database service.

With a traditional database server, you may need to think about: Server instances, CPU, Memory, Storage, Operating system, Patching, Database infrastructure.

With DynamoDB, AWS manages the underlying infrastructure. You don't need to manually provision a database server in the same way as a traditional database deployment.

Simple Comparison

Traditional Database

Server↓CPU↓Memory↓Storage↓Database

DynamoDB

Application↓DynamoDB↓AWS-managed infrastructure

11. Automatic Scaling  |  12. Zero-Server Management

11. Automatic Scaling: DynamoDB is designed to handle changing workloads. Suppose your application normally receives 100 requests but suddenly receives 10,000 requests. DynamoDB can scale according to the selected capacity mode and workload.

Scaling Concept:

Low Traffic→Lower Capacity
Traffic increases→More Capacity
Traffic decreases→Capacity decreases

This is especially useful for fluctuating workloads.

12. Zero-Server Management: One major advantage is that you don't have to manage database servers yourself. You don't need to manually manage:

  • Database server provisioning
  • Operating system maintenance
  • Hardware
  • Database infrastructure scaling

AWS manages the underlying service infrastructure.

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 3

13. Provisioned Capacity vs 14. On-Demand Capacity

DynamoDB provides different capacity approaches.

A. Provisioned Capacity

You specify the expected capacity. For example:

Read Capacity:
Minimum → X | Maximum → Y

Write Capacity:
Minimum → X | Maximum → Y

You can configure auto scaling so capacity can increase or decrease according to demand. Concept: Low traffic → Lower provisioned capacity. High traffic → Higher provisioned capacity. This can be useful when workload patterns are relatively predictable.

B. On-Demand Capacity

With on-demand capacity, you don't have to manage a fixed provisioned capacity in the same way. The service is designed to handle requests automatically and billing is based on request usage.

Best suited for:

  • Unpredictable traffic
  • New applications
  • Spiky workloads
  • Applications where traffic patterns are difficult to estimate

Example: Normal traffic → Low request activity. Sudden traffic spike → Higher request activity. Traffic falls → Lower activity.

15. Read Capacity and Write Capacity

Two important concepts are:

Read Capacity: Represents capacity for read operations.
Write Capacity: Represents capacity for write operations.

Application │ ├── Read Request │ ↓ │ Read Capacity │ └── Write Request ↓ Write Capacity

These concepts are particularly relevant when using provisioned capacity.

16. Auto Scaling

DynamoDB can use auto scaling with provisioned capacity. You can configure: Minimum capacity, Maximum capacity, Target utilization.

For example: Minimum Capacity → 1  |  Maximum Capacity → 10  |  Target Utilization → 70%

These values are only examples from the practical concept; actual settings should be chosen according to the application's workload.

Auto Scaling Flow:

Traffic decreases→Capacity decreases→Lower resource usage
Traffic increases→Capacity increases→More requests can be handled

17. Maximum Table Throughput

The course also demonstrates configuring maximum read/write throughput. The exact limits depend on the DynamoDB configuration and current AWS service limits.

Concept You can control and monitor the capacity available to your DynamoDB workload.

18. Monitoring Auto Scaling

DynamoDB provides monitoring information about capacity and scaling activity. You can inspect:

  • Current capacity
  • Read activity
  • Write activity
  • Scaling changes
  • Table metrics

This allows you to understand how the database is responding to application traffic.

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 4

19. DynamoDB Indexes

Indexes are used to improve the efficiency of queries based on attributes other than the primary key. Suppose your application frequently searches using: username. You can create an appropriate index so that queries based on that attribute can be handled efficiently.

Concept

Without suitable indexing:

Query→Find matching data

With an appropriate index:

Query→Index→Matching items
Important

DynamoDB has concepts such as:

  • Primary key
  • Local Secondary Index (LSI)
  • Global Secondary Index (GSI)

Index design should be based on the application's access patterns.

20. Backup and Point-in-Time Recovery

Backup is extremely important for databases. DynamoDB supports backup and recovery capabilities.

Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR)

Point-in-Time Recovery allows you to restore table data to a point in time within the supported recovery window.

Example: Suppose:

  • 10:00 → Database is correct
  • 10:30 → Data accidentally changed
  • 11:00 → Problem discovered

With appropriate point-in-time recovery configuration, you can recover the table to an earlier point in time.

Concept

Past │ ├── 10:00 ├── 10:15 ├── 10:30 ├── 10:45 └── 11:00 ↓ Choose recovery point

This is useful for accidental changes or deletions.

21. On-Demand Backups

You can also create an on-demand backup. This can be useful when you want to explicitly preserve a table's data before performing an important operation.

DynamoDB Table │ ├── Point-in-Time Recovery │ └── On-Demand Backup

22. Delete Protection

DynamoDB provides deletion protection. When enabled, it helps protect a table from accidental deletion.

Without protection: Accidental delete → Table deleted → Data loss
With protection: Delete attempt → Protection enabled → Additional protection against deletion

Useful for important production tables.

23. Time to Live (TTL)

DynamoDB supports Time to Live (TTL). TTL allows expired items to be automatically removed after a specified expiration time.

Example

Suppose you store temporary data:

{ "id": "101", "session": "ABC", "expiresAt": 1750000000 }

Once the item reaches its expiration condition, DynamoDB can automatically remove it.

Useful for:

  • Temporary data / Sessions
  • Cache-like information
  • Expiring records / Temp state

24. Encryption

DynamoDB supports encryption of data at rest. Encryption helps protect stored database data. For production systems, encryption should be part of the overall security design.

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 5

25. Practical Architecture — Node.js + DynamoDB

The course demonstrates a practical application using: Amazon EC2, Docker, Node.js application, DynamoDB.

User │ ▼ Web Browser │ ▼ ┌─────────────────┐ │ EC2 │ │ │ │ Docker │ │ Node.js App │ └────────┬────────┘ │ ▼ DynamoDB Table Contacts

The Node.js application communicates with DynamoDB using the AWS SDK.

26. AWS SDK  |  27. Node.js

Applications can interact with AWS services programmatically using the AWS SDK. For Node.js applications, AWS provides an SDK that can be installed through the Node package ecosystem (npm).

Node.js App→AWS SDK→DynamoDB

The SDK provides APIs that allow the application to: Create/read/update/delete data, Access AWS services, Send requests to DynamoDB, Work with DynamoDB tables and items.

28 - 30. Practical Setup (EC2 & Docker)

28. Creating EC2

The practical creates an EC2 instance. Example name: My Web Server. Process: AWS Console → EC2 → Launch Instance → Configure instance → Allow HTTP traffic → Launch.

For a web application, HTTP access needs to be allowed through the appropriate security configuration.

29. Docker & 30. Running Node.js

After connecting to the EC2 instance, Docker is installed. Conceptually: sudo yum install docker -y. Then start service: sudo systemctl start docker, and check status.

The course uses a pre-built Docker image for the Node.js DynamoDB demo application. Workflow:

Registry→docker pull→EC2→Container→Node.js→DynamoDB

31. Env Variables  |  32. IAM Role for EC2  |  33. Creating Role

The container needs AWS configuration to communicate with DynamoDB. The course demonstrates environment variables such as AWS_REGION, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.

Important Security Note

Do not hard-code or expose access keys in application commands, source code, screenshots, or public repositories. For an EC2 application, the preferred approach is usually: EC2 → IAM Role → DynamoDB permissions. This avoids manually managing long-lived access keys.

Instead of giving an EC2 instance permanent access keys, attach an IAM role.

EC2 │ ▼ IAM Role │ ▼ DynamoDB Permissions │ ▼ DynamoDB

33. Creating an IAM Role: IAM → Roles → Create Role → AWS Service → EC2. Then permissions are assigned. Principle of Least Privilege: Instead of "DynamoDB Full Access", prefer only what's needed (GetItem, PutItem, UpdateItem, DeleteItem, Query).

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 6

Docker Operations (34 - 38)

34. Docker Secrets: The course mentions Docker secrets as another way of handling sensitive info. The main idea is: Sensitive configuration should be managed securely rather than exposed directly. For AWS, IAM roles are often preferable.

35. Running the Container: The Docker container maps: EC2 Port 80 → Container Port 3000 because the Node.js application is listening on port 3000. Conceptually: Browser → EC2 :80 → Docker Container :3000 → Node.js → DynamoDB.

36. Checking Container: Use docker ps. Shows Container ID, Image, Status, Port mapping, Name.

37. Accessing App & 38. Testing

After the container is running: EC2 Public IP → Web Browser → Node.js App. The app can add contacts, view contacts, display data.

Testing Integration: Suppose the application adds baburao@example.com. The app sends the data to DynamoDB. Open DynamoDB console → Tables → Contacts → Explore Items. The newly inserted item should appear.

Data Flow proving connection:

User → Browser → Node.js → AWS SDK → DynamoDB → Contacts Table

39. DynamoDB Global Tables  |  40. DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)

39. Global Tables

DynamoDB Global Tables allow a table to be replicated across multiple AWS Regions. This is useful for globally distributed applications (e.g. users in USA, Europe, Asia).

Global Application │ ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐ ↓ ↓ ↓ USA Region Europe Region Asia Region │ │ │ └───────────────┼───────────────┘ Global Table

Helps provide: Multi-Region availability, Lower latency, Disaster recovery, Global app support.

40. DAX & 41. Caching

DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is a fully managed, in-memory cache designed specifically for DynamoDB. It is used when applications require extremely fast access to frequently requested data.

Normal vs DAX Flow:

App→DynamoDB
App→DAX→DynamoDB

41. Caching: If app repeatedly requests "Product A", DAX returns cached result instead of hitting DynamoDB every time, reducing latency and DB reads.

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 7

42. DAX vs ElastiCache  |  43 & 44. Performance & Use Cases

Both involve caching, but they are designed for different use cases.

DAXElastiCache
Designed specifically for DynamoDBGeneral-purpose managed cache
Integrates directly with DynamoDB workloadsSupports caching technologies such as Redis
In-memory cachingIn-memory caching
Useful for DynamoDB-heavy applicationsUseful across many application architectures

43. Performance: DynamoDB provides single-digit millisecond latency. DAX provides microsecond-level latency for cached workloads. DynamoDB → Very low latency | DAX → Even lower latency.

44. When is DAX Useful? Financial apps, High-traffic apps, Gaming, Mobile apps, Apps requiring very fast reads, Read-heavy DynamoDB workloads.

45. DAX Architecture

Users │ ▼ Application │ ▼ DAX ┌────┴────┐ │ │ Cache Hit Cache Miss │ │ ▼ ▼ Response DynamoDB │ ▼ Data Store

46. DynamoDB vs RDS  |  47. High-Level Architecture

This is one of the most important interview concepts.

FeatureRDSDynamoDB
Database typeRelationalNoSQL
Data modelTables/rows/columnsTables/items/attributes
SchemaStructuredFlexible item attributes
Query styleSQLDynamoDB APIs/expressions
ScalingInstance/storage-based + replicasManaged/serverless capacity
Best forRelational workloadsHigh-scale NoSQL workloads
JoinsSupported by relational enginesNot relational joins
Typical useBusiness apps, ERP, relational systemsWeb, mobile, gaming, IoT, high-scale apps
Users │ ▼ Load Balancer │ ▼ Application / EC2 │ ▼ AWS SDK/API │ ▼ ┌──────────────┐ │ DynamoDB │ │ Table │ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌──────────┴──────────┐ ▼ ▼ DAX Cache Global Tables
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 8

48. DynamoDB Use Cases  |  49. Key Advantages

48. Use Cases

DynamoDB is particularly useful for workloads such as:

  1. Web Applications: High-traffic web apps requiring scalable data storage.
  2. Mobile Applications: Large numbers of users and requests.
  3. Gaming: Fast reads/writes, high scalability, large concurrent users.
  4. IoT: Generating huge numbers of events and records.
  5. Advertising Technology: Extremely high request rates and low latency.
  6. Real-Time Applications: Where fast data access is important.

49. Key Advantages

  • Fully Managed & Serverless: AWS manages infra; no servers to manage directly.
  • Automatic Scaling: Designed to handle changing traffic.
  • Flexible Data Model: Items can contain different attributes.
  • High Performance: Designed for low-latency DB operations.
  • High Availability: Managed infra for HA.
  • Backup & Recovery: Backup and PITR capabilities.
  • Global Tables: Multi-Region architectures.
  • DAX: In-memory caching option.

50. Important Security Best Practices  |  51. Cleanup

When implementing DynamoDB:

  • 1. Prefer IAM Roles: For EC2: EC2 → IAM Role → DynamoDB. Avoid long-lived access keys in code.
  • 2. Use Least Privilege: Give only needed permissions.
  • 3. Protect Credentials: Never expose AWS Access Key or Secret Access Key in GitHub, Docker images, code, or screenshots.
  • 4. Enable Encryption: Use appropriate AWS encryption.
  • 5. Enable Recovery Features: Backup and PITR for prod.
  • 6. Enable Delete Protection: Protect critical tables.

51. Practical Cleanup

After completing the lab, remove resources to avoid charges:

DynamoDB Table → Delete EC2 Instance → Terminate IAM Access Keys → Deactivate/Delete

Always check AWS Billing / Cost Management after practicals.

52. Important Concepts to Remember

  • DynamoDB: Managed NoSQL database
  • Table: Collection of items.
  • Item: Individual record/document.
  • Attribute: Property inside an item.
  • Partition Key: Key used to identify/distribute items.
  • Provisioned Capacity: Capacity configured in advance.
  • On-Demand Capacity: Pay based on actual request usage.
  • Auto Scaling: Automatically adjusts provisioned capacity.
  • GSI: Global Secondary Index.
  • LSI: Local Secondary Index.
  • PITR: Point-in-Time Recovery.
  • TTL: Automatically expires/removes items.
  • DAX: DynamoDB Accelerator — in-memory cache.
  • Global Tables: Multi-Region DynamoDB replication.
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 9

53. Interview Questions

Q1. What is DynamoDB?
A fully managed, serverless NoSQL database service provided by AWS, designed for highly scalable and low-latency applications.
Q2. Difference between RDS and DynamoDB?
RDS is a managed relational database service, while DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL database service.
Q3. What is an item?
An individual record stored inside a DynamoDB table.
Q4. What is an attribute?
A property or piece of data belonging to an item.
Q5. What is a partition key?
A key attribute used to identify items and determine how DynamoDB distributes data.
Q6. Is DynamoDB serverless?
Yes. Fully managed serverless database service; users don't provision or manage servers directly.
Q7. What is auto scaling?
Adjusts provisioned read/write capacity according to workload demand.
Q8. What is on-demand capacity?
Handles request traffic without requiring a fixed provisioned capacity, billing based on request usage.
Q9. What is DAX?
DynamoDB Accelerator, a fully managed in-memory caching service specifically for DynamoDB.
Q10. What are Global Tables?
Allow DynamoDB data to be replicated across multiple AWS Regions for globally distributed apps.
Q11. What is Point-in-Time Recovery?
PITR allows a table to be restored to a selected point in time within the supported recovery period.
Q12. What is TTL?
Time to Live automatically expires items based on an expiration attribute.

“Serverless + NoSQL + Fast + Flexible + Scalable”

Major components: T → P → C → I → B → D → G

Amazon DynamoDB is a serverless, fully managed NoSQL database designed for flexible data models, very low latency, automatic scalability, and high availability.
