AWS Lambda - Handwritten Study Notes
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 1
AWS Lambda — Detailed & Structured Notes

1. What is AWS Lambda?

AWS Lambda is a managed serverless compute service provided by AWS.

It allows you to run your code in the cloud without managing the underlying servers yourself.

Normally

If you want to execute some code, you need a machine/server.

Laptop / EC2 Instance↓Run Code

With Lambda

Your Code↓AWS Lambda↓AWS manages infra

You mainly provide the code, while AWS handles the underlying compute infrastructure.

2. What Does "Serverless" Mean?

A common misunderstanding is: "Serverless means there are no servers." That is not literally true.

Servers are still required to execute your code. Serverless means that AWS manages the servers and infrastructure for you.

You don't have to manually manage: Server provisioning, Operating system, Hardware, Server maintenance, Infrastructure scaling.

Simple Definition Serverless = You focus on code; AWS manages the underlying infrastructure.

3. Why Use AWS Lambda?  |  4. Main Features

With traditional servers (like EC2), you manage CPU, Memory, Storage, OS, Scaling, and Maintenance.

This makes Lambda particularly useful for small, event-driven tasks.

Main Features of AWS Lambda

  • 1. No Server Management: AWS manages the infrastructure required to execute your functions.
  • 2. Upload Your Code: You can deploy your function code directly to Lambda.
  • 3. Automatic Scaling: Lambda can create multiple concurrent function executions when many events arrive.
  • 4. Event-Driven Execution: A Lambda function normally runs when it is invoked by an event or request.
  • 5. Pay for Usage: Usage-based pricing model. You generally pay according to execution/request usage.
  • 6. Suitable for Short Tasks: Designed for relatively short-lived workloads rather than continuously running applications.

5. Supported Programming Languages

Lambda supports multiple programming languages/runtimes. Common examples include:

Python Java JavaScript / Node.js C# Go Ruby

AWS also provides mechanisms for using other languages through custom runtimes.

6. Creating a Lambda Function

Workflow: AWS Console → Search "Lambda" → Create Function.

Option 1 — Scratch: Create completely new function.
Option 2 — Blueprint: Use AWS templates.

Example: Function Name: DemoFunction | Runtime: Python

7. What is a Lambda Function?

A unit of code that AWS can execute.

def hello():
print("Hello")
Lambda Function │ └── Code │ └── Executes when invoked
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 2

8. Lambda Handler  |  9. Testing a Function

8. Lambda Handler

The main entry point for execution. The handler receives information about the event and executes the required logic.

Event↓Lambda Handler↓Your Code↓Response

9. Testing a Lambda Function

A Lambda function does not simply execute continuously. You can manually invoke it using the Test feature.

Function→Create Test Event→Invoke→View Response

10. What is an Event?  |  11. Example Function

An event contains information that is passed to a Lambda function when it is invoked. { "message": "Hello" }

Important Concept Creating a function does not automatically mean that the code is constantly running. It executes when invoked.

11. Example Python Function

import json def lambda_handler(event, context): print("Hello from Lambda") return { "statusCode": 200, "body": json.dumps("Hello") }
  • event → information about the invocation
  • context → information about the Lambda execution environment
  • lambda_handler → handler function
  • return → response returned by the function

12. Deploying Code Changes  |  13. Event-Driven Execution

If you change code, it needs to be deployed so the updated version is used for subsequent invocations.

Edit Code→Deploy→Test New Code

Editing and deploying are separate concepts.

13. Event-Driven Architecture

The function executes in response to an event.

Event→Lambda Trigger→Lambda→Task

The event can originate from another AWS service.

14 - 16. Architectural Examples

15. S3 + Lambda

User │ ▼ S3 Bucket │ File Upload │ ▼ S3 Event │ ▼ Lambda │ ┌───┼───┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Resize Process

16. DynamoDB + Lambda

Lambda can perform tasks based on DB changes.

User Signup ↓ Application ↓ DynamoDB ↓ New Data ↓ Lambda ↓ Send Welcome Email
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 3

17. Integrations  |  18. Adding an S3 Trigger

Lambda can work with many AWS services: S3, DynamoDB, API Gateway, CloudWatch, EventBridge, SQS, SNS.

18. Adding an S3 Trigger

Basic flow to configure a trigger:

Lambda → Add Trigger ↓ Select S3 & Bucket ↓ Select Event Type (e.g. All Object Create)

19 & 20. S3 Event Notification

Behind the scenes, the event notification connects the S3 event to the Lambda function. If you upload image.jpg to the bucket, an Object Created Event fires, invoking the function.

Monitoring and Logs (21 - 24)

21. Monitoring: Provides metrics about function executions: Number of invocations, Duration, Errors, Performance.

22. CloudWatch Logs: Lambda integrates with Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Output like print("Hello") goes here.

Execution→Logs→CloudWatch

24. Monitoring vs Logs

Monitoring → Metrics
(Invocation count, duration, errors)

Logs → Detailed Information
(Detailed execution output/print statements)

Lambda Permissions & IAM Roles (25 - 29)

Permissions are very important when Lambda interacts with other AWS services.

26. Execution Role

An IAM role that determines what AWS resources the function is allowed to access.

What can the Lambda access?

Lambda → Execution Role → S3 Read Perm → S3 Bucket

28. Resource-Based Policies

Controls which AWS services or principals are allowed to invoke the Lambda function.

Who can invoke the Lambda?

S3 → Invoke Permission → Lambda Function
29. S3 to Lambda Permission Flow

S3 needs permission to invoke Lambda (Resource-based).

Lambda needs permission to access other resources (Execution Role).

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 4

30. AWS Lambda Limitations

Lambda is powerful, but not suitable for every workload.

30.1 Execution Time Limit

Lambda functions are designed for short-lived tasks. The maximum execution time is 15 minutes.

Short Task → Lambda
Long-Running App → EC2 / ECS

31. Hosting  |  32. Stateless Nature

31. Not an always-running server: Lambda is not designed to host an entire traditional website (24/7 continuous server). Combine with API Gateway + DB for a serverless backend.

32. Stateless Nature

Functions are treated as stateless. Do not depend on in-memory info from a previous invocation.

Use external services for persistent state: DynamoDB, S3, RDS.

33. Cold Start  |  34. Warm vs Cold Execution

If a function hasn't been invoked recently, an initialization delay can occur. This is a Cold Start.

Cold Start

Request ↓ Initialize environment ↓ Run function

Warm Execution

Request ↓ Existing environment ↓ Run function

Use Cases (35 - 39)

Lambda is excellent for short, event-driven, automatically scalable tasks.

  • 1. Image Processing: User uploads image to S3 → Lambda resizes, compresses, generates thumbnails.
  • 2. Data Processing: Data enters DB → Lambda validates, cleans, transforms.
  • 3. Real-Time Notifications: User signs up → Event fires → Lambda sends welcome email.
  • 4. API Backend: Combined with API Gateway to create serverless backends connecting to databases.
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 5

40. Automatic Scaling

Lambda can automatically scale the number of concurrent executions according to incoming demand.

Requests │ ┌─────────────┼─────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Lambda Lambda Lambda Execution Execution Execution #1 #2 #3

41. Why it's useful: If 100 users sign up simultaneously, instead of manually creating 100 servers, Lambda creates concurrent execution environments as needed.

42. Pay-As-You-Go  |  43. Lambda vs EC2

42. Pricing: Usage-based model. You pay for executions, not continuous server uptime.

44. Vs Containers: Containers host long-running processes. Lambda executes a function and completes.

EC2Lambda
Virtual serverServerless compute
You manage instanceAWS manages infra
Runs continuouslyEvent/request driven
Requires config for scaleAutomatic scaling
Pay for running resourceUsage-based pay
Long-running workloadsShort/event workloads

Deployment (45 - 48)

45. ZIP Deployment

If code exists locally, package it into a ZIP file and upload. The ZIP can contain application code, dependencies, and supporting files.

47. Dependencies: Required because external libraries aren't automatically in the runtime.

48. Lambda Layers

Allows libraries/reusable components to be packaged separately from function code.

Lambda Function + Lambda Layer ↓ Execution Environment

49 & 50. Architecture  |  51. Lifecycle

User │ ▼ S3 Bucket │ Object Created │ ▼ AWS Lambda │ ┌────┴────┐ ▼ ▼ Execute Log Output │ ▼ CloudWatch

51. Execution Lifecycle

  1. Event/request arrives
  2. Lambda invocation
  3. Environment available/created (Cold start possible here)
  4. Function code runs
  5. Function returns
  6. Logs/metrics recorded
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 6

52. Important Concepts

  • Serverless: AWS manages servers.
  • Function: Unit of code executed.
  • Event: Input that causes execution.
  • Trigger: Mechanism invoking Lambda.
  • Handler: Function entry point.
  • Execution Role: IAM permissions.
  • CloudWatch: Monitoring & logs.
  • Cold Start: Init delay.
  • Stateless: No persistent local memory.

53. Advantages

  • No server management
  • Automatic scaling
  • Event-driven workflow
  • Usage-based pricing
  • Fast development & Integration

54 & 55. Limitations

  • 15-minute max duration
  • Stateless design
  • Cold starts
  • Not for continuous workloads

56. Lambda Interview Questions

Q1. What is AWS Lambda?
Fully managed serverless compute service executing code in response to events.
Q2. What does serverless mean?
AWS manages the underlying infrastructure.
Q6. Can S3 trigger Lambda?
Yes, via S3 object creation events.
Q7. What is an Execution Role?
IAM role defining what AWS resources the function can access.
Q8. Max execution duration?
15 minutes per invocation.
Q9. What is a cold start?
Initialization overhead when a new execution environment is created.
Q10. Is Lambda stateful?
No, generally designed as stateless.
Q12. How does Lambda scale?
Automatically creates concurrent executions in response to events.

57. Quick Revision

AWS LAMBDA │ ├── Serverless Compute ├── Fully Managed ├── Function-Based ├── Event-Driven ├── Automatic Scaling ├── Usage-Based Pricing ├── Triggers (S3, DynamoDB, API GW) ├── IAM Execution Role ├── Monitoring (CloudWatch) └── Limitations ├── 15-Minute Max ├── Stateless └── Cold Starts

58. Memory Trick

CODE → EVENT → FUNCTION → SCALE → PAY

59. Top Architectures

S3 + Lambda S3 → Event → Lambda → Process → Logs DynamoDB + Lambda DynamoDB → Event → Lambda → Notify API Gateway + Lambda Client → API GW → Lambda → DB
⭐ Final Takeaway

Lambda is a serverless, event-driven compute service best for short tasks.

  1. Serverless → AWS manages servers
  2. Event-driven → Runs when invoked
  3. Auto-scaling → Handles concurrency
AWS ECS - Handwritten Study Notes
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 1
AWS ECS (Elastic Container Service)

1. What is Amazon ECS?

Amazon ECS (Elastic Container Service) is a cloud-based container management service provided by AWS.

It allows you to run and manage containerized applications, especially Docker containers, on AWS infrastructure.

Simple Definition Amazon ECS is a managed AWS service used to deploy, run, manage, and scale container-based applications.

ECS can work with: Docker containers, Container images stored in registries such as Amazon ECR, and other supported/private container registries.

2. Why Use Amazon ECS?

Suppose you have developed an application and:

  • Created the application
  • Containerized it using Docker
  • Built a Docker image
  • Uploaded the image to a container registry
  • Now want to deploy it

Without ECS, manual work:

  • Set up servers & Install Docker
  • Configure the application
  • Run & Monitor containers
  • Restart failed containers
  • Handle scaling & Manage instances

ECS simplifies this process.

You provide ECS with information such as: Which container image to use, How much CPU/memory is required, Which ports to expose, Environment variables, and How many copies of the application should run.

ECS then manages much of the container deployment and operation for you.

3. Basic ECS Architecture

The three most important ECS terms are: Cluster, Service, Task.

And another important concept is: Task Definition.

ECS │ └── Cluster │ ├── Service │ ├── Task │ ├── Task │ └── Task │ └── Task Definition

4. ECS Cluster

What is a Cluster? An ECS Cluster is a logical grouping that contains the resources and infrastructure used to run your ECS workloads.

Easy way to remember:

Cluster = Place/group where your ECS workloads run.

My Cluster │ ├── Service │ ├── Task 1 │ └── Task 2 │ └── Other Services

A cluster can contain multiple services and tasks.

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 2

5. ECS Service

An ECS Service is responsible for maintaining and managing the desired number of running tasks.

It helps with: Maintaining the desired number of tasks, Scaling, Deployments, Replacing failed tasks, Integration with load balancing.

Example

Suppose you want 2 copies of your app running. You configure: Desired Tasks = 2

Before:

Task 1 → Running Task 2 → Running

Task 2 fails...

After:

Task 1 → Running Task 2 → New replacement task

The ECS service can maintain the desired number of tasks.

Remember Service = Manages how many tasks should be running and how they are deployed/scaled.

6. ECS Task

A Task represents a running instance of your containerized application.

Task └── Container └── Nginx

If you run two copies:

  • Task 1 → Nginx Container
  • Task 2 → Nginx Container

Therefore: Task = A running workload/container execution in ECS.

7. Task Definition

A Task Definition is a blueprint/configuration that tells ECS how your container should run.

It can specify things such as:

  • Container image & name
  • CPU & Memory
  • Port mappings
  • Environment variables
  • Logging configuration
  • Storage & Health checks

Docker comparison

With Docker, you might run:

docker run -p 80:80 -e ENV=production nginx

In ECS, many of these configuration details are defined in the Task Definition.

Easy memory trick Task Definition = Blueprint | Task = Running instance created from that blueprint

8. Cluster → Service → Task → Container

This is one of the most important concepts.

ECS │ └── Cluster │ └── Service │ ├── Task 1 │ └── Container │ └── Task 2 └── Container

The Task Definition tells ECS how those tasks should be configured.

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 3

9. ECS Infrastructure Options

When creating an ECS cluster, you need to decide where/how your containers will run. The transcript demonstrates two important options:

1. AWS Fargate

Fargate is a serverless compute option for containers. You don't have to manually manage the underlying EC2 servers.

Your Application ↓ Container ↓ ECS + Fargate ↓ AWS-managed infra

2. EC2

With the EC2 option, you use EC2 instances as the compute infrastructure for your containers.

You have more control over the underlying instances, but also more infrastructure management responsibilities.

10. Fargate vs EC2

Feature Fargate EC2
Server management AWS manages underlying infra You manage EC2 instances
Infrastructure control Lower Higher
Operational effort Lower Higher
Good for Simpler container deployments Workloads requiring more instance-level control
Scaling ECS/Fargate handles capacity You manage instance capacity + ECS
Serverless experience Yes No
Simple rule Want less infrastructure management → Fargate | Want more control over servers → EC2

Practical ECS Deployment (11 - 14)

The transcript demonstrates deploying an Nginx container using ECS Fargate.

Step 1: Open ECS

AWS Console→ECS

Step 2: Create an ECS Cluster

Name: my-cluster | Infra: AWS Fargate

Step 3: Create a Task Definition

Name: my-task | Infra: AWS Fargate

14. Container Configuration

The task definition needs to know which container image should be executed.

Container Name: nginx
Image: nginx
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 4

Task Definition Details (15 - 20)

15. Port Mapping

Nginx is a web server, so HTTP traffic needs to reach the container. Container Port: 80

Internet↓HTTP :80↓ECS Task↓Nginx :80

16. CPU and Memory

You can configure the resources allocated. Resource limits help prevent one workload from consuming unlimited resources, control costs, and improve resource planning.

17. Env Variables & 18. Logging

Env Vars: Allows configuration to be separated from app code. (e.g., ENV=prod).

Logging: Enable container logging (commonly to CloudWatch Logs) for troubleshooting.

19. Health Checks & 20. Create

Health Checks: Determine if app is functioning. Unhealthy tasks can be replaced.

20. Create: After configuring Image, Port, CPU, Memory, Env vars, Logs, Health checks, you create the Task Definition.

Creating an ECS Service (21 - 24)

Cluster→Create Service→Select Task Definition→Name: my-service

22. Desired Tasks & 23. Why?

Desired Tasks = 2

Running multiple tasks improves availability. If Task 1 fails, the service attempts to start a replacement to maintain the desired count of 2.

24. Networking Config

Configure VPC, Subnets, SG, Public IP. For HTTP app, allow HTTP Port 80. Best Practice: Don't blindly allow 0.0.0.0/0 for every port. Only expose what's needed.

Running and Updating (25 - 29)

25. Public IP: If task needs internet access, enable Public IP. Internet → Public IP → ECS Task

26. Auto Start: Service automatically starts tasks to meet desired count. PENDING → RUNNING

27. Checking: Service → Tasks tab shows status, IP, logs, etc.

28. Accessing & 29. Updating

If HTTP 80 is allowed, http://<PUBLIC-IP> shows the Nginx page.

29. Updating: You can change service config. Update Desired Count 2 → 1, and ECS will reduce running tasks to match.

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 5

30. Scaling  |  31. ECS + Load Balancer

ECS services can be configured for scaling according to workload requirements.

Internet ↓ Load Balancer ↓ ┌─────────┴─────────┐ ↓ ↓ Task 1 Task 2 ↓ ↓ Container Container

Why a Load Balancer?

If many users access your application, the load balancer can distribute requests across healthy tasks.

This improves: Availability, Scalability, Traffic distribution.

32. ECS Logging

Container→ECS→CloudWatch Logs

Logs are useful for debugging, error analysis, monitoring, and troubleshooting.

33. Important ECS Concepts — Quick Table

TermMeaning
ECSAWS container orchestration service
ClusterLogical grouping for ECS workloads
ServiceMaintains and manages running tasks
TaskRunning workload/container execution
Task DefinitionBlueprint describing how a task should run
FargateServerless container compute option
EC2Customer-managed compute infrastructure
Desired CountNumber of tasks the service should maintain

34. ECS Architecture Memory Diagram

AWS ECS │ ┌──────┴──────┐ │ Cluster │ └──────┬──────┘ │ Service │ ┌─────────┴─────────┐ │ │ Task 1 Task 2 │ │ Container Container

35. ECS vs EC2

EC2 = Virtual Machine. ECS = Container Management.

36. ECS vs Docker

Docker builds/runs containers. ECS orchestrates/scales them on AWS.

Docker Image→Registry→ECS→Running Tasks
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 6

37. ECS Fargate Arch  |  38. Practical Workflow

Docker Image ↓ Container Registry ↓ ECS Task Definition ↓ ECS Service ↓ Fargate (Serverless) ↓ Running Container

38. Complete Workflow

  1. Create & Dockerize App
  2. Build & Push Image to Registry
  3. Create ECS Cluster
  4. Create Task Definition
  5. Create ECS Service
  6. Set Desired Task Count
  7. Configure Networking
  8. Run Container
  9. Monitor Logs/Metrics
  10. Scale/Update as Required

39. Cleanup  |  ⭐ Best Practices

39. Cleanup

Don't create resources and forget them. Flow:

Delete/scale down Service Stop running Tasks Deregister Task Defs Delete Cluster
  • 1. Prefer Fargate when you don't need server-level control.
  • 2. Least-privilege IAM permissions.
  • 3. Restrict Ports: Only allow required traffic via SGs.
  • 4. Use CloudWatch for proper logging.
  • 5. Multiple tasks for important apps (HA).
  • 6. Load Balancer for production web apps.

🧠 Quick Revision & 🎯 Interview Questions

Quick ECS summary

  • Managed container orchestration service.
  • Cluster groups workloads.
  • Service manages running tasks & capacity.
  • Task = running workload.
  • Task Definition = blueprint.
  • Fargate = Serverless containers.
  • EC2 = More server control.
Q1. Fargate vs EC2?
Fargate: Serverless, AWS manages infra. EC2: You manage instances.
Q2. Task vs Task Definition?
Task Definition is the blueprint. Task is the running instance based on it.
Q3. Why run multiple tasks?
To improve availability and handle more traffic. Service maintains desired count.
⭐ The Easiest Formula to Remember

ECS → Cluster → Service → Tasks → Containers

Task Definition = Instructions/Blueprint for those Tasks.

AWS VPC & Networking - Handwritten Study Notes
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 1
AWS VPC & Networking
Detailed & Structured Study Notes

1. What is Amazon VPC?

VPC = Virtual Private Cloud

Amazon VPC is a logically isolated private network inside AWS where you can launch and control your AWS resources.

Why do we need a VPC?

To create a secure, isolated, and controlled network environment for your resources.

You control:

  • IP address ranges
  • Subnets & Routing
  • Internet connectivity
  • Network security
  • Access between resources

Major Benefits

  • Security — Isolate resources from unwanted access.
  • Control — You dictate routes and network rules.
  • Customization — Design network to fit app needs.
  • Isolation — Resources operate purely in your environment.
Important Note VPC is not unique to AWS. Other cloud providers have similar concepts (e.g., Azure calls it Virtual Network / VNet).

2. AWS Global Infrastructure

Before diving into VPC networking, understand these three terms: Region → Availability Zone → Resources

2.1 Region

A Region is a geographical area where AWS has infrastructure/data centers (e.g., Mumbai, London, Singapore, US East).

Why choose a nearby Region?
Generally, a geographically closer Region can help reduce network latency for your users. If your app serves Indian users, choose Mumbai.

3. Availability Zone (AZ)

An Availability Zone is an isolated location within an AWS Region. A Region contains multiple AZs.

AWS Region / | \ AZ-A AZ-B AZ-C | | | Server Server Server

Why multiple AZs?

To improve Availability, Fault tolerance, Resilience, and Disaster recovery.

If one AZ has a problem, resources in another AZ can continue operating.

⭐ Remember Region = Geographical area
AZ = Isolated location within a Region
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 2

4. VPC CIDR Block

When creating a VPC, you specify an IPv4 CIDR block.

CIDR = Classless Inter-Domain Routing. It is a notation used to define a range of IP addresses.

Example 1

10.0.0.0/16

10.0.0.0 → network address
/16 → prefix length

Total IPv4 addresses = 65,536

Math Formula

Total IPv4 = 2^(32 - prefix)

Example for /28:

2^(32-28) = 2^4 = 16 addresses

Important AWS Rule AWS reserves some IP addresses within each subnet for networking purposes (usually 5), so the number of addresses available for resources is lower than the mathematical total.

5. VPC Architecture

A basic AWS network visualization:

AWS Region │ └── VPC │ ├── Public Subnet │ └── EC2 / Application Server │ └── Private Subnet └── Database / Internal Resource

6. What is a Subnet?

A subnet is a smaller network segment created inside a VPC.

Suppose your VPC has a large IP range (10.0.0.0/16). You can divide it:

VPC: 10.0.0.0/16 ├── Public Subnet: 10.0.1.0/24 └── Private Subnet: 10.0.2.0/24

7. Resources Run Inside Subnets

Common Beginner Mistake:

"I'll create an EC2 instance directly inside the VPC."

Correct Flow:

VPC→Subnet→EC2 Instance
⭐ Remember

VPC = Large network

Subnet = Smaller network inside VPC

Resource = Runs inside a subnet

8. Public vs Private Subnet

Public SubnetPrivate Subnet
Designed for resources requiring internet connectivity Designed for resources that should not be directly internet-accessible
Usually has a route to an Internet Gateway Does not have a direct route to an Internet Gateway for inbound access
Example: public-facing web component Example: database, backend services
More exposed More isolated
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 3

9. Subnets and Availability Zones

A subnet is tied to exactly one Availability Zone. However, you can create multiple subnets across different AZs.

Region: Mumbai │ ├── AZ-A │ └── Public Subnet ├── AZ-B │ └── Public Subnet └── AZ-C └── Private Subnet

Why? To improve availability and distribute workloads.

10. Route Table  |  11. Default Route

A Route Table contains rules that determine where network traffic should be sent.

It answers: "If traffic is going to this destination, where should it go?"

Public Subnet→Route Table→Internet Gateway

11. Default Route

0.0.0.0/0

Matches any IPv4 destination not matched by a more specific route.

Destination: 0.0.0.0/0 | Target: igw-xxx

12. Internet Gateway (IGW)

An IGW provides a path between a VPC and the internet.

Basic requirements for internet connectivity:

  • VPC & Subnet
  • Internet Gateway attached to the VPC
  • Route table with internet route pointing to IGW
  • Appropriate public IP addressing on the instance
  • Security rules allowing required traffic

13. Security Group  |  14. Characteristics

A Security Group is a virtual firewall that controls inbound and outbound traffic for supported resources like EC2.

Inbound vs Outbound

Inbound: What traffic can enter (e.g., HTTP : 80, SSH : 22).

Outbound: What traffic can leave.

14. Characteristics

  • Stateful: Allowed incoming traffic automatically allows the return response.
  • Allow Rules: They only support allow rules (no explicit deny).
  • Resource Level: Attached to instances/ENIs, not the whole subnet.
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 4

15. Network ACL (NACL)

NACL = Network Access Control List

A network-level firewall that controls traffic entering and leaving a subnet.

16. Security Group vs NACL

This is a highly tested interview/exam topic.

Feature Security Group (SG) Network ACL (NACL)
Level Resource / Network Interface Subnet level
Rules Allow only Allow + Deny
Stateful Yes (Return traffic auto-allowed) No (Stateless)
Applies to Explicitly associated resources Entire associated subnet
Common Use Protect individual resources Additional subnet-level filtering
Memory Trick SG → Security of the resource | NACL → Network/subnet access control

17. NACL Example

Subnet [ Protected by NACL ] │ ├── EC2-A ├── EC2-B └── EC2-C

If a NACL is attached to the subnet, its rules apply to all traffic entering or leaving the subnet, affecting all instances inside.

18. NAT Gateway

NAT = Network Address Translation

Allows resources in a private subnet to initiate connections to the internet, while preventing unsolicited inbound connections from the internet.

Example Use Case: Database in a private subnet needs to download patches or access external APIs.

19. NAT Gateway Architecture

Internet ▲ │ Internet Gateway ▲ │ NAT Gateway (in Public Subnet) ▲ │ Private Subnet (EC2)

Important: The private EC2 initiates outbound traffic via the NAT Gateway, but the internet cannot initiate an inbound connection to the private EC2.

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 5

20. VPC Peering

VPC Peering creates private network connectivity between two VPCs.

VPC-A (Mumbai)
← VPC Peering →
VPC-B (London)

Resources communicate using private IPs. Not a full mesh automatically (use Transit Gateway for many-to-many).

21. VPC Endpoint

Provides private connectivity from a VPC to supported AWS services (like S3) without using the public internet.

EC2→VPC Endpoint→AWS S3

Improves security and reduces internet dependency.

22. Bastion Host

A specially controlled server in a public subnet used as an entry point for accessing resources in private networks.

Internet → Bastion Host (Public) → Private EC2

Modern Alternative: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager often replaces bastions.

23. Elastic IP Address (EIP)

A static public IPv4 address. Normal EC2 public IPs can change on stop/start. Elastic IPs remain stable.

Best Practice Avoid allocating EIPs unnecessarily as they incur charges.

24. VPC Flow Logs

Captures information about IP traffic going to and from network interfaces in your VPC.

Use Cases: Troubleshooting connectivity, security investigation, network monitoring.

25. Direct Connect  |  26. Client VPN

25. Direct Connect

Dedicated, physical network connection from an on-premises data center directly to AWS (bypassing public internet).

Office/DC ↔ Dedicated Line ↔ AWS

26. Client VPN

Managed VPN service allowing users to securely connect to AWS networks remotely.

Remote User ↔ VPN ↔ AWS VPC

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 6

27. Complete VPC Architecture

INTERNET │ ▼ ┌─────────────────┐ │ Internet Gateway│ └────────┬────────┘ │ Public Route Table │ ▼ ┌──────────────────────┐ │ Public Subnet │ │ Load Balancer/EC2 │ └──────────┬───────────┘ │ Application │ ▼ ┌──────────────────────┐ │ Private Subnet │ │ Backend/Database │ └──────────┬───────────┘ │ NAT Gateway │ ▼ Internet

28. Complete VPC Hierarchy

AWS │ └── Region │ ├── Availability Zone A │ ├── Public Subnet │ └── Private Subnet │ └── Availability Zone B ├── Public Subnet └── Private Subnet

29. Networking Components — One-Line Definitions

ComponentSimple Definition
VPCYour isolated virtual network in AWS
CIDRDefines an IP address range
RegionGeographic AWS location
AZIsolated infrastructure location within a Region
SubnetSmaller network segment inside a VPC
Route TableDecides where network traffic should go
IGWProvides a path between VPC resources and the internet
Security GroupStateful firewall associated with resources
NACLStateless firewall operating at subnet level
NAT GatewayAllows private resources to initiate outbound internet
VPC PeeringPrivate connectivity between two VPCs
VPC EndpointPrivate connectivity from VPC to supported AWS services
Bastion HostControlled entry point for accessing private resources
Elastic IPStatic public IPv4 address
Flow LogsRecords information about IP traffic
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 7

30 & 31. Public vs Private Concepts

What Makes it Public?

A subnet is public when its route table has a route (0.0.0.0/0) pointing to an Internet Gateway.

What Makes it Private?

It lacks a direct route to an Internet Gateway. It uses a NAT Gateway for outbound internet access.

32. Important: IGW vs NAT Gateway

Internet Gateway (IGW)NAT Gateway
Connects VPC to internetProvides outbound internet for private resources
Commonly used by public subnetsCommonly used by private subnets
Supports full bi-directional internetPrevents unsolicited inbound connections
Attached to VPCDeployed into a subnet

33 & 34. Route Table vs Security Group vs NACL

Route Table

Answers: "Where should traffic go?"

Security Group

Answers: "Is this traffic allowed for this resource?"

Architectural Examples (35 & 36)

35. Hosting a Website

Web server in Public Subnet (Security Group: allow HTTP 80 / HTTPS 443). Database in Private Subnet (Security Group: allow DB traffic ONLY from the Web server SG). This follows the principle of least exposure.

36. Private Server Needs Updates

Private EC2→NAT Gateway→Internet Gateway→Internet

Initiates outbound connection securely without allowing inbound internet access.

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 8

37. ⭐ Interview Questions

Q1. What is a VPC?
A logically isolated virtual network within AWS where you can launch and control resources.
Q2. What is a subnet?
A smaller IP/network segment mapped to an Availability Zone inside a VPC.
Q3. Difference between public and private subnet?
Public has a route to an IGW. Private does not provide direct inbound internet connectivity via an IGW.
Q4. What is an Internet Gateway?
It provides a path between a VPC and the internet for public-facing resources.
Q5. What is a Route Table?
Contains routing rules determining where network traffic should be forwarded.
Q6. What is a Security Group?
A stateful virtual firewall controlling inbound/outbound traffic at the resource/instance level.
Q7. What is a Network ACL?
A stateless firewall operating at the subnet level, supporting both allow and deny rules.
Q8. Security Group vs NACL?
SG: Resource level, stateful, allow rules only. NACL: Subnet level, stateless, allow & deny rules.
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 9
Q9. Why do we use a NAT Gateway?
To allow resources in private subnets to initiate outbound connections without exposing them to inbound internet traffic.
Q10. What is VPC Peering?
Private network connectivity between two specific VPCs.
Q11. What is a VPC Endpoint?
Private connectivity from a VPC to AWS services (like S3) without the internet.
Q12. What is a Bastion Host?
A controlled public server used as an entry point for administrative access to private resources.
Q14. What are VPC Flow Logs?
Logs that capture information about IP traffic to/from network interfaces in a VPC.
Q15. What is AWS Direct Connect?
Dedicated physical network connectivity between an on-premises data center and AWS.

38. 🧠 Quick Revision — VPC in 60 Seconds

REGION ↓ AVAILABILITY ZONE ↓ VPC ↓ SUBNET ↓ RESOURCE

Security:

SG → Resource Level | NACL → Subnet Level

Connectivity:

  • Internet → IGW
  • Private outbound → NAT Gateway
  • VPC ↔ VPC → VPC Peering
  • VPC → AWS Service → VPC Endpoint
⭐ Final Memory Map
  • VPC = Network
  • CIDR = IP Range
  • Subnet = Smaller Network
  • Route Table = Traffic Direction
  • IGW = Internet Connection
  • SG = Resource Firewall
  • NACL = Subnet Firewall
  • NAT Gateway = Private → Internet
  • VPC Peering = VPC ↔ VPC
  • VPC Endpoint = VPC → AWS Privately
  • Bastion = Gateway to Private
  • Elastic IP = Static Public IPv4
  • Flow Logs = Network Traffic Records
  • Direct Connect = DC ↔ AWS
AWS VPC Practical Setup & Networking Notes
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 1
AWS VPC — Practical Setup & Networking Notes

1. Creating a VPC

What is a VPC?

A Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) is an isolated virtual network in AWS where you can launch resources such as EC2 instances.

When creating a VPC, the important configuration is the CIDR block.

Example

VPC Name: my-vpc

IPv4 CIDR: 10.0.0.0/16

IPv6: Not required for this example

A /16 IPv4 CIDR represents 65,536 total IPv4 addresses before AWS subnet reservations.

⭐ Key Point

The VPC CIDR defines the overall IP address range available inside your VPC.

2. CIDR Block

CIDR = Classless Inter-Domain Routing

It defines an IP address range. For example: 10.0.0.0/16

The VPC can then be divided into smaller ranges called subnets.

Example structure VPC 10.0.0.0/16 │ ├── Public Subnet │ └── 10.0.1.0/24 │ └── Private Subnet └── 10.0.2.0/24

A /24 contains 256 total IPv4 addresses, although AWS reserves 5 addresses in every subnet, so fewer are available for resources.

3. Creating Subnets

After creating the VPC, the next step is to create subnets.

A subnet is a smaller IP range inside the VPC.

Example

VPC: 10.0.0.0/16

Public subnet: 10.0.1.0/24

Private subnet: 10.0.2.0/24

These ranges are different and do not overlap.

4. Availability Zone

When creating a subnet, AWS asks you to select an Availability Zone (AZ).

Region └── Availability Zone A └── Public Subnet

You can also create another subnet in another AZ.

Recommended production architecture

Region │ ├── AZ-A │ ├── Public Subnet │ └── Private Subnet │ └── AZ-B ├── Public Subnet └── Private Subnet

This improves availability because your application does not depend on only one AZ.

⭐ Important A subnet belongs to exactly one Availability Zone.
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 2

5. Public and Private Subnets

Public Subnet

A public subnet is a subnet whose route table has a route to an Internet Gateway.

Typical resources:

  • Application Load Balancer
  • Public-facing EC2 instance
  • Bastion host

Private Subnet

A private subnet does not have a direct route to the Internet Gateway for internet access.

Typical resources:

  • Databases
  • Backend application servers
  • Private ECS tasks

Simple architecture

INTERNET │ ▼ Internet Gateway │ ▼ Public Subnet │ ┌──────┴──────┐ │ │ ALB EC2 │ ▼ Private Subnet │ Application/DB

6. Route Table

A Route Table contains rules that determine where network traffic should go.

Example

Destination Target
0.0.0.0/0 Internet Gateway

Meaning:

0.0.0.0/0 means: Any IPv4 destination that does not have a more specific route.

So: 0.0.0.0/0 → Internet Gateway provides a path from the associated subnet toward the internet.

7. Main / Default Route Table

When you create a VPC, AWS automatically creates some default networking components, including a main route table.

A subnet that isn't explicitly associated with another route table uses the VPC's main route table.

Important correction

A default/main route table does not automatically make a subnet public.

For a subnet to function as a public subnet, you generally need:

Subnet ↓ Route Table ↓ 0.0.0.0/0 → Internet Gateway

And the resource itself must have appropriate public addressing and security configuration.

8. Internet Gateway (IGW)

An Internet Gateway provides the VPC with a path for internet communication.

VPC │ └── Internet Gateway

After creating the Internet Gateway, you attach it to the VPC. Example: my-vpc → my-internet-gateway

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 3

9. Connecting a Public Subnet to the Internet

Creating an Internet Gateway alone isn't enough. You need to connect the pieces.

Step 1 — Create Internet Gateway (Internet Gateway)

Step 2 — Attach it to VPC (my-vpc → Internet Gateway)

Step 3 — Create a route table (my-route-table)

Step 4 — Associate the public subnet (my-route-table → Public Subnet)

Step 5 — Add internet route (Destination: 0.0.0.0/0 | Target: Internet Gateway)

Now the flow becomes:

Internet↕Internet Gateway↕Route Table↕Public Subnet

10. VPC Resource Map

AWS provides a Resource Map that makes the relationships easier to understand. Conceptually:

VPC │ ├── Public Subnet │ │ │ └── Route Table │ │ │ └── Internet Gateway │ └── Private Subnet │ └── Main/Private Route Table

This is extremely useful when learning AWS networking because you can visually understand how the components are connected.

11. Launching an EC2 Instance Inside Your VPC

After creating the VPC and subnets, you can launch an EC2 instance.

During EC2 creation: Network Settings → VPC

Instead of Default VPC, select my-vpc. Then select the required subnet.

For example:

  • VPC: my-vpc
  • Subnet: Private Subnet
  • Auto-assign Public IP: Disabled

12. Private EC2 Instance Example

Suppose your private subnet has: 10.0.2.0/24

You launch an EC2 instance into this subnet. AWS may assign it an address such as: 10.0.2.15

Private Subnet │ └── EC2 (10.0.2.15)

The important point is: The instance receives an IP from the subnet's CIDR range.

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 4

13. Complete VPC Architecture

The practical setup from this demonstration can be visualized as:

AWS REGION │ ▼ VPC 10.0.0.0/16 │ ┌──────────────┴──────────────┐ │ │ ▼ ▼ PUBLIC SUBNET PRIVATE SUBNET 10.0.1.0/24 10.0.2.0/24 │ │ ▼ ▼ Route Table Route Table │ │ ▼ │ Internet Gateway EC2 │ 10.0.2.x ▼ INTERNET

14. Public Subnet Traffic Flow

For a properly configured public resource:

User↓Internet↓Internet Gateway↓Route Table↓Public Subnet↓EC2 / ALB

The important configuration is: Public Subnet → Route Table → 0.0.0.0/0 → Internet Gateway

15. Private Subnet Traffic Flow

A private subnet normally does not have 0.0.0.0/0 → Internet Gateway directly.

If a private resource needs outbound internet access, a common architecture is:

Private EC2↓Route Table↓NAT Gateway↓Internet Gateway↓Internet

This allows the private resource to initiate outbound connections without making it directly reachable from the internet.

16. Important Difference: Public vs Private

Feature Public Subnet Private Subnet
Route to IGW Yes No direct internet route
Direct internet exposure Possible Not directly
Typical resources ALB, public web servers DB, backend servers
Public IP Can be used Usually not required
Outbound internet IGW NAT Gateway, if required
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 5
⚠️ Remember

A subnet is not public merely because it is called public-subnet. Its route table configuration determines whether it has a public route.

17. Important Concepts to Remember

  • VPC: Overall virtual network
  • Subnet: Smaller IP range inside VPC
  • Route Table: Decides where traffic goes
  • Internet Gateway: VPC ↔ Internet connectivity
  • NAT Gateway: Private Outbound Internet
  • EC2: Compute resource inside a subnet

🧠 Easy Memory Map

Hierarchy:

AWS Region↓Availability Zone↓VPC↓Subnet↓Resource

Paths:

Public: Internet → IGW → Route Table → Public Subnet → Resource

Private Outbound: Private Resource → Route Table → NAT Gateway → IGW → Internet

⭐ Interview / Exam Questions

Q1. What is a VPC?
A VPC is an isolated virtual network in AWS where cloud resources can be deployed and networked.
Q2. What is CIDR?
CIDR defines the IP address range of a VPC or subnet. Example: 10.0.0.0/16
Q3. What is a subnet?
A subnet is a smaller IP range created inside a VPC.
Q4. What is a public subnet?
A subnet whose route table provides a route to an Internet Gateway.
Q5. What is a private subnet?
A subnet without a direct route to the Internet Gateway for internet access.
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 6
Q6. What does a route table do?
It determines where network traffic should be forwarded.
Q7. What is an Internet Gateway?
It provides a path between a VPC and the internet for appropriately configured public resources.
Q8. Why do we need an Internet Gateway?
To enable internet connectivity for resources that are configured for public access.
Q9. Can a private subnet access the internet?
Yes, for outbound access it can commonly use a NAT Gateway.
Q10. Where is an EC2 instance launched?
An EC2 instance is launched into a subnet, which is part of a VPC.

⚠️ Most Important Corrections

  • VPC is logically isolated, not necessarily a physically separate network.
  • An Availability Zone is not simply one physical server; it represents an isolated infrastructure location within a region.
  • Every subnet belongs to exactly one AZ.
  • EC2 is launched into a subnet, not directly into a VPC.
  • A default route table doesn't automatically make a subnet public.
  • Internet Gateway + route table + appropriate public addressing/security are needed for public connectivity.
  • NAT Gateway is for outbound connections initiated from private resources; it does not provide unsolicited inbound internet access.
  • A Security Group and NACL provide additional traffic controls around these networking components.
🔥 One-Line Revision

VPC = Network → Subnet = IP Segment → Route Table = Traffic Direction → IGW = Internet Path → NAT = Private Outbound Internet → EC2 = Compute Resource

AWS Route 53 - Handwritten Study Notes
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 1
AWS Route 53 — Detailed English Notes

1. What is Amazon Route 53?

Amazon Route 53 is AWS's scalable DNS (Domain Name System) web service.

Its main purpose is to translate a domain name into the destination required to reach your application.

Simple example

Instead of accessing your website using: http://54.123.45.67

You can use: http://www.example.com

The user enters the domain name, and DNS helps direct the request to the appropriate server or AWS resource.

⭐ Key Point

Route 53 is mainly used for DNS, domain registration, health checks, and traffic routing.

2. What is DNS?

DNS = Domain Name System

DNS translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses or other DNS destinations.

Without DNS

Browser ↓ IP Address (54.x.x.x) ↓ EC2 Server

The user needs to remember the IP address.

With DNS

Browser ↓ example.com ↓ DNS ↓ IP / AWS Resource

This makes accessing applications much easier.

3. Why is it called Route 53?

The number 53 refers to the standard DNS port: DNS → Port 53

Hence: Route + 53 = Route 53

🧠 Remember DNS commonly uses port 53.

4. Basic Route 53 Architecture

A simple Route 53 setup can look like this:

User │ ▼ Browser │ ▼ example.com │ ▼ Route 53 DNS │ ▼ IP Address / AWS Resource │ ▼ EC2 / S3 / ALB / Other Endpoint

Route 53 determines where the DNS request should resolve based on the records and routing policies you configure.

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 2

5. Route 53 — Important Components

The major concepts covered here are:

  • Domain Registration
  • Hosted Zones
  • DNS Records
  • Routing Policies
  • Health Checks
  • Traffic Routing
  • Multi-Region Routing
  • Failover
  • Alias Records
  • DNS Queries

6. Domain Name Registration

Before using a custom domain, you need to have a domain. There are two common approaches:

Option 1 — Register through AWS

You can register a domain using Route 53.

AWS Route 53 ↓ Register Domain ↓ example.com

Domain registration generally involves a fee, usually based on the domain extension and registration period.

Option 2 — Register somewhere else

You can purchase/register the domain from another registrar, such as a third-party domain provider. Then you can configure that domain to use Route 53 for DNS management.

⭐ Important Domain registration and DNS hosting are related but separate concepts.

7. Hosted Zone

A Hosted Zone is a container in Route 53 that stores DNS records for a domain.

example.com │ └── Hosted Zone │ ├── A Record ├── AAAA Record ├── CNAME Record └── Other Records

You can think of a hosted zone as: The DNS configuration area for your domain.

8 & 9. Hosted Zone for External Domains & Name Servers

Suppose your domain is registered with another provider.

Domain Registrar→example.com

You create a hosted zone in Route 53. Route 53 provides name servers for the hosted zone. You then configure the domain registrar to use those Route 53 name servers.

Domain Registrar │ ▼ Route 53 Name Servers │ ▼ Hosted Zone │ ▼ DNS Records

DNS propagation

After changing name-server information, the change may not become visible everywhere immediately. Propagation/caching can take time.

⚠️ Note The exact time is not guaranteed to be exactly 24 hours. It depends on DNS caching and TTLs.
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 3

10. DNS Records

A DNS record tells Route 53 how to handle a particular name.

www.example.com→Record→IP / AWS endpoint

Common record types include: A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, NS, and Alias records.

11. A Record

An A record maps a domain name to an IPv4 address.

Name: www
Type: A
Value: 54.123.45.67
www.example.com→54.123.45.67

12. AAAA Record

An AAAA record maps a domain name to an IPv6 address.

Domain→IPv6 Address

13. CNAME Record

A CNAME (Canonical Name) record maps one domain name to another domain name.

www.example.com→app.example.com

14. Alias Records

Route 53 supports Alias records for supported AWS resources (like S3 websites, ALB, CloudFront). Instead of an IP, you point to the AWS resource directly.

example.com→AWS Resource
⭐ Quick Summary
  • A record: Domain → IPv4
  • AAAA record: Domain → IPv6
  • CNAME: Domain → Domain
  • Alias: Domain → Supported AWS Resource
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 4

15. Simple Routing Policy

The simplest routing policy is Simple Routing.

User ↓ example.com ↓ Route 53 ↓ One destination (e.g. EC2 Instance)

This is suitable when you have a simple setup with one primary destination.

16. Why Routing Policies Are Important

Suppose you have multiple servers: Server 1 → Europe and Server 2 → Mumbai.

You may want Route 53 to decide:

  • Which server should receive the request?
  • Which region is closest?
  • Which server is healthy?
  • How much traffic should each server receive?
  • What should happen if one server fails?

Route 53 provides different routing policies for these requirements.

17 & 18. Latency-Based Routing

Goal: Send users to the AWS region that provides the lowest network latency among your configured destinations.

Route 53 / \ / \ Europe Mumbai EC2 EC2

Concept

European User → Route 53 → Europe EC2

Indian User → Route 53 → Mumbai EC2

This can improve user experience when the regional endpoint is healthy and offers lower latency.

⭐ Important Latency-based routing is based on measured network latency, not simply "nearest on the map."

19. Weighted Routing

It allows you to distribute traffic according to assigned weights.

Route 53 / \ 50% 50% / \ Mumbai Delhi

This can be useful for: Traffic distribution, Testing, Gradual deployments, Blue/green deployment strategies.

⚠️ Note Weighted routing does not mean that every small batch of requests will be split with mathematically exact percentages. It represents the intended distribution over time.
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 5

20. Failover Routing

Failover Routing is used when you have a primary and backup destination.

Primary Server │ ▼ Health Check │ ├── Healthy → Continue using Primary │ └── Unhealthy ↓ Backup Server

Example:

Primary: Europe EC2 | Secondary: Mumbai EC2

User→Route 53→Primary ❌→Secondary ✅

21 & 22. Health Checks & Failover

A Route 53 Health Check monitors the health of an endpoint. It can check whether the endpoint is responding according to the health-check configuration.

Health Check Success

Europe Server→Health Check→Healthy ✅

Route traffic to Europe.

Health Check Failure

Europe Server→Health Check→Unhealthy ❌

Route traffic to Mumbai.

23. Health Checks ≠ Zero Downtime

Health checks can improve resilience, but there can still be:

  • Detection time
  • DNS caching
  • TTL effects
  • Application-level failures that aren't detected by the chosen check

Therefore, don't interpret Route 53 failover as an absolute guarantee of zero downtime.

24. Multi-Region Architecture

A common global architecture for globally distributed applications:

Route 53 / \ / \ Europe Region Mumbai Region │ │ EC2 EC2 │ │ Application Application
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 6

25. Complete Practical Flow

The complete setup demonstrated can be remembered as:

STEP 1: Register Domain ↓ STEP 2: Create Hosted Zone ↓ STEP 3: Configure Name Servers ↓ STEP 4: Create DNS Record ↓ STEP 5: Point Record to Destination ↓ STEP 6: Configure Routing Policy ↓ STEP 7: Configure Health Check ↓ STEP 8: Test the Domain

Concrete Examples (26 & 27)

26. EC2 + Route 53

Without Route 53:

Browser→54.x.x.x→EC2

With Route 53:

Browser www.example.com Route 53 (A Record) 54.x.x.x EC2

27. Two Regions + Latency

Europe EC2 → 1.1.1.1
Mumbai EC2 → 2.2.2.2

Records:

  • example.com → 1.1.1.1
  • example.com → 2.2.2.2

Policy: Latency-Based

European User → Route 53 → Europe EC2
Indian User → Route 53 → Mumbai EC2

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 7

28. Route 53 Routing Policies — Quick Comparison

Routing Policy Main Purpose
Simple Basic routing to a destination
Weighted Distribute traffic using weights
Latency-based Route based on lowest latency
Failover Primary/secondary disaster recovery
Geolocation Route based on user's geographic location
Geoproximity Route based on geographic proximity, with optional bias
Multivalue answer Return multiple healthy records
IP-based Route based on client IP ranges

29 & 30 & 31. Use Cases & Billing

29. Disaster Recovery

Primary Server → Mumbai
Backup Server → Singapore

Mumbai ❌→Health Check→Route 53→Singapore ✅

This provides a useful DNS-based failover mechanism.

30. Route 53 + S3

Route 53 can be used with supported S3 website endpoints through an Alias configuration.

example.com→Route 53→S3 Website

31. Route 53 Billing

Route 53 is a billable AWS service. Potential charges can include: Hosted zones, DNS queries, Health checks, Domain registration.

⚠️ Note Don't assume Route 53 has a general always-free tier covering all features. Pricing depends on usage/configuration.
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 8

32. Cleanup After Practice

When doing AWS practicals, always clean up resources you no longer need. Check EC2 instances in every region used.

Delete unnecessary records ↓ Delete health checks ↓ Delete hosted zone ↓ Terminate test EC2 instances

⭐ Important: A domain registered through an external registrar remains registered there even after you delete its Route 53 hosted zone.

🧠 Super-Important Revision

Route 53AWS DNS Service
DNSDomain → Destination
Hosted ZoneContainer for DNS records
A RecordDomain → IPv4
AAAA RecordDomain → IPv6
CNAMEDomain → Another Domain
AliasDomain → Supported AWS Resource
Latency RoutingUser → Lowest-latency configured region
Weighted RoutingTraffic → Distributed according to weights
FailoverPrimary ❌ → Secondary ✅
Health CheckMonitor endpoint health
🔥 Final Architecture to Memorize
USER │ ▼ www.example.com │ ▼ ROUTE 53 │ ┌────────────┼────────────┐ │ │ │ Simple Latency Failover │ │ │ ▼ ▼ ▼ EC2 Best Region Primary/Backup │ ▼ APPLICATION

One-line formula:
Domain → Route 53 → DNS Record → Routing Policy → Healthy/Best Endpoint → Application

AWS CloudFormation - Handwritten Study Notes
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 1
AWS CloudFormation — Structured English Notes

1. What is AWS CloudFormation?

AWS CloudFormation is an Infrastructure as Code (IaC) service provided by AWS.

Infrastructure as Code (IaC)

IaC means: Creating and managing cloud infrastructure using code instead of doing everything manually through the AWS Console.

For example, instead of manually creating an EC2 instance by selecting:

  • AMI
  • Instance type
  • Storage
  • Security Group
  • Other settings

you can define all of these in a CloudFormation template. CloudFormation then creates the required resources automatically.

2. Manual Infrastructure vs CloudFormation

Traditional/manual approach

AWS Console↓Create EC2↓Select AMI↓Select Instance Type↓Configure Storage↓Configure Security Group↓Review↓Create Instance

This involves a lot of manual work.

CloudFormation approach

CloudFormation Template↓Create Stack↓CloudFormation reads template↓AWS Resources↓Resources created

The main benefit is automation and repeatability.

3. CloudFormation Template

A template is a file that describes the infrastructure you want CloudFormation to create.

CloudFormation templates can be written in: YAML or JSON

Example:

Resources: MyInstance: Type: AWS::EC2::Instance Properties: InstanceType: t3.micro ImageId: ami-xxxxxxxx Tags: - Key: Name Value: MySimpleInstance

This template says: "Create an EC2 instance with this AMI, this instance type, and this name."

4. Declarative Approach

CloudFormation follows a declarative approach.

What does declarative mean?

You specify: WHAT you want

rather than explaining every individual step of: HOW to create it.

For example, you just declare:

Type: AWS::EC2::Instance Properties: InstanceType: t3.micro ImageId: ami-xxxxxxxx

You don't manually write: Open EC2 → Click Launch Instance → Select AMI → Configure settings → Launch. Instead, you declare the desired infrastructure state.

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 2

5. Important CloudFormation Terms

A. Template

The file containing your infrastructure definition. Formats: YAML or JSON

B. Stack

A Stack is a collection of AWS resources created and managed together from a CloudFormation template.

CloudFormation Stack │ ├── EC2 Instance ├── Security Group └── Elastic IP

Instead of managing every resource separately, you can manage them as one logical unit.

C. Resources

Resources are the AWS services/components defined in the template. Examples: EC2, S3, VPC, Security Group, Elastic IP, RDS, Lambda, IAM resources, Load Balancer.

6. Creating a Stack

Create Stack→Choose Template→Upload Template→Specify Stack Name→Configure Options→Review→Create Stack

You can use: Existing templates, Sample templates, Templates stored locally, Templates stored in Amazon S3, or Infrastructure Composer.

7. AWS Infrastructure Composer

CloudFormation provides Infrastructure Composer for visualizing infrastructure. Instead of seeing only code, you can visualize resources and their relationships.

Security Group │ ↓ EC2 Instance ↑ │ Elastic IP

Benefits:

  • Visual understanding of architecture
  • See resource relationships
  • Review infrastructure
  • Edit & Validate templates

This is particularly useful when a template contains many interconnected resources.

8. CloudFormation Stack Lifecycle

A basic stack can go through three important operations:

Create

Template→Create Stack→Resources Created

Update

Existing Stack→Modify Template→Preview Changes→Update Stack

Delete

Delete Stack→CloudFormation Deletes Resources
Create → Update → Delete are fundamental CloudFormation operations.
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 3

9. Updating a Stack  |  10. Change Sets

Suppose the original template contains: InstanceType: t3.micro. Later you change it to: InstanceType: t2.micro. You can update the existing stack instead of manually modifying the infrastructure.

10. Change Sets

A Change Set allows you to preview proposed infrastructure changes before applying them.

Current Template↓Modified Template↓Change Set↓Review Changes↓Execute Update
Important Note on Changes

The change preview can indicate whether a resource will be: Modified, Replaced, Deleted, or Created.

A resource replacement can mean the existing resource is removed and a new resource is created.

Therefore, always review changes carefully before executing an update.

11. Example: Simple Name Update

Suppose the instance initially has: MySimpleInstance. You change it to: MyDemoInstance.

CloudFormation can identify the change and update the stack. If the change does not require replacing the underlying resource, the existing resource can remain while its applicable property is updated.

12. Rollback and Failure Handling

One of CloudFormation's important capabilities is rollback. Suppose you attempt an invalid update: t3.micro → Invalid configuration → Update fails.

CloudFormation can roll back the stack to the previous successful state, depending on the operation and configuration.

Previous State→Update→ERROR→ROLLBACK→Previous Successful State

Example from the transcript

An update attempted to change the instance type to t2.micro, but the configuration was not valid in that environment/region. The update failed and CloudFormation rolled the stack back. The EC2 instance therefore remained in its previous working state.

13. Why Rollback is Important

Without proper state management, a failed infrastructure update could leave resources partially modified. CloudFormation helps maintain the intended stack state and provides mechanisms for handling failed operations.

Key Idea If an update fails, CloudFormation can attempt to restore the previous successful state.
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 4

14. Multiple Resources  |  15. Resource References

One of the biggest advantages of CloudFormation is that one template can create multiple related resources.

CloudFormation Stack │ ├──────── EC2 Instance │ ├──────── Security Group │ └──────── Elastic IP

15. Resource References

Resources can reference one another. The EC2 instance can reference the Security Group created in the same template. Similarly, the Elastic IP can reference the EC2 instance. This allows CloudFormation to understand relationships between resources.

16. Example: Web Server Stack

A more advanced template can automatically create a complete basic web server environment.

Internet │ ↓ Elastic IP │ ↓ EC2 Instance │ Security Group │ ↓ Web Server │ ↓ HTML Web Page

17. Security Group in Template

For a web server, the Security Group can allow HTTP traffic (Port 80) from the Internet. Note: In production, security rules should be restricted appropriately rather than unnecessarily exposing services to the entire internet.

18. Elastic IP

An Elastic IP is a static public IPv4 address. Without a persistent public address, the public IPv4 address associated with an instance can change in certain lifecycle situations. Using an Elastic IP provides a stable address for the application.

19. CloudFormation & Automation  |  20. Major Use Cases

CloudFormation becomes especially useful when infrastructure needs to be created repeatedly.

Create Template Once→Reuse Template→Create Infrastructure→Reuse Again→Create Infrastructure

20. Major Use Cases

1. Consistency: Same Template → Same Configuration → Consistent Infrastructure. Reduces manual configuration differences.

2. Automation: Can be incorporated into automated workflows (e.g., Scheduled Job → AWS CLI → CloudFormation → Create Stack).

3. Repeatable Environments: You can create similar environments for Development, Testing, Staging, and Production using the same base infrastructure definition with different parameters.

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 5

21. Infrastructure as Code — Key Benefits

BenefitMeaning
AutomationReduce manual infrastructure work
ConsistencySame infrastructure definition can be reused
RepeatabilityEasily reproduce environments
Version ControlTemplates can be stored with application code
Faster DeploymentInfrastructure can be created systematically
Easy CleanupStack deletion can remove managed resources
State ManagementCloudFormation tracks stack resources and operations
Change PreviewChange Sets show proposed modifications

22. Stack Deletion  |  23. Cost Management Benefit

Instead of manually deleting each resource (EC2, SG, EIP), you can delete the stack: Delete Stack → CloudFormation → Delete Stack Resources. This is especially useful for temporary environments.

⚠️ Important Always understand a resource's deletion behavior before deleting a production stack. Some resources may have retention policies.

23. Cost Management

CloudFormation itself does not generally charge simply for the existence of a template or stack. However, the AWS resources created by CloudFormation (EC2, RDS, NAT, etc.) can incur charges. Deleting unused stacks helps prevent unnecessary resource charges.

24. StackSets

A normal CloudFormation stack is generally deployed in a particular AWS account and region. For larger organizations, CloudFormation StackSets allow you to deploy CloudFormation stacks across Multiple AWS accounts and Multiple AWS Regions.

StackSet │ ┌─────────┼─────────┐ ↓ ↓ ↓ Account A Account B Account C │ │ │ Region 1 Region 1 Region 2

Use case: Organizations can use StackSets to deploy standardized infrastructure across many accounts and regions.

25. CloudFormation and AWS CLI

CloudFormation can also be operated through the AWS CLI.

Local Template→AWS CLI→CloudFormation→Create Stack
aws cloudformation create-stack \ --stack-name demo-stack \ --template-body file://template.yaml

The AWS CLI must be configured with appropriate credentials and region settings.

AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 6

26. Documentation  |  27. Resource Types

When creating templates, you use the CloudFormation Template Reference to find Resource types, Supported properties, Required properties, and Allowed values.

Choose AWS Service↓Find CFN Resource Type↓Check Properties↓Write Template

27. Resource Type

A resource declaration typically contains: Type: AWS::EC2::Instance. This tells CloudFormation which AWS resource should be created.

Examples: AWS::S3::Bucket, AWS::RDS::DBInstance, AWS::Lambda::Function

28. Common CloudFormation Use Cases

  • EC2: EC2 Instance + Security Group + Elastic IP
  • S3: S3 Bucket
  • Networking: VPC, Subnets, Route Tables, Internet Gateway, Security Components
  • Database: RDS Database + Backup Configuration
  • Serverless: Lambda + API Gateway
  • Web App: Load Balancer → Auto Scaling → EC2 Instances

29. Drift Detection

Drift Detection identifies changes made to resources outside CloudFormation.

Example: Your template says: EC2 configuration = A. But someone manually changes the resource through the AWS Console to configuration = B. Now there is a difference between Template State vs Actual Resource State. This difference is called drift.

CloudFormation Template │ │ expected state ↓ Resource ↑ │ actual state │ Manual Console Change

30. Architecture  |  31. Practical Workflow

CloudFormation │ Template ┌────────┴────────┐ ↓ ↓ Stack Change Set │ ↓ AWS Resources ┌──────┼───────┐ ↓ ↓ ↓ EC2 SG EIP
  1. Write Template (YAML/JSON)
  2. Validate Template
  3. Create Stack
  4. CloudFormation Creates Resources
  5. Monitor Stack Events
  6. Update Template When Required
  7. Create/Review Change Set
  8. Apply Update
  9. Rollback if Update Fails
  10. Delete Stack When Done
AWS CERTIFIED CLOUD PRACTITIONER & SAA // STUDY NOTES PAGE 7

33. CloudFormation vs Manual AWS Console

Manual configurationCode-based configuration
Time-consuming for repeated workReusable
Higher chance of human errorMore consistent

Terraform - Handwritten Study Notes
INFRASTRUCTURE AUTOMATION // STUDY NOTES PAGE 1
Terraform — Infrastructure as Code (IaC)

1. Introduction to Terraform

Terraform is an open-source Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tool developed by HashiCorp.

What is Infrastructure as Code?

Infrastructure as Code means using code and configuration files to create, manage, modify, and delete cloud infrastructure.

Instead of manually creating resources through a cloud provider's console, you define the desired infrastructure in a configuration file and let Terraform handle the infrastructure creation process.

Manual Example

AWS Console↓EC2 Dashboard↓Launch Instance↓Select AMI↓Select Instance Type↓Configure Settings↓Launch

Terraform Example

Terraform Configuration↓Terraform Commands↓Cloud Provider↓EC2 Instance Created

Terraform allows you to define the desired EC2 infrastructure in code.

2. Multi-Cloud Support

One of Terraform's major advantages is that it supports multiple cloud providers and infrastructure providers.

Examples mentioned in the course include:

AWS Google Cloud Platform (GCP) Microsoft Azure

Therefore, Terraform can act as a common IaC tool across different cloud platforms.

Key Point Terraform is not limited to a single cloud provider. This makes it useful when organizations work with multiple cloud environments.

3. Configuration Files  |  4. HCL

3. Configuration Files

Terraform configuration files generally use the .tf file extension.

Provider ↓ Region / Location ↓ Resource Type ↓ Resource Configuration

4. HCL (HashiCorp Configuration Language)

Terraform configurations are written using HCL. It is designed to make infrastructure configuration relatively easy to read and write.

Terraform↓HCL↓.tf files
INFRASTRUCTURE AUTOMATION // STUDY NOTES PAGE 2

5. Declarative Approach

Terraform follows a declarative approach.

What does declarative mean?

You specify the desired result, rather than manually specifying every step required to achieve that result.

For example:

"I want an AWS EC2 instance using this AMI and this instance type."

Terraform determines the necessary actions to create that infrastructure.

Imperative Approach

Step 1 → Do this Step 2 → Do this Step 3 → Do this Step 4 → Do this

Declarative Approach

Desired State↓Terraform determines required actions↓Infrastructure
Key Point You describe WHAT you want; Terraform handles HOW to achieve it.

6. Basic Terraform Workflow

Terraform's basic workflow can be remembered using three main stages:

Configuration→init→plan→apply→Infrastructure Ready

For cleanup: terraform destroy

7 - 9. Core Commands

7. terraform init

The first command generally used in a Terraform project. It initializes the Terraform working directory and prepares the project for Terraform operations.

8. terraform plan

Shows the changes Terraform intends to make. It allows you to review the proposed infrastructure changes before actually applying them. Helps you understand what will be created, modified, or removed.

9. terraform apply

Applies the Terraform configuration and creates or modifies the required infrastructure.

terraform apply→Review→Confirm (yes)→Resources Created/Modified

10. Example — Creating an EC2 Instance

Suppose the Terraform configuration defines an AWS EC2 instance. The workflow is:

.tf Configuration File ↓ terraform init ↓ terraform plan ↓ Review Changes ↓ terraform apply ↓ EC2 Instance Created
INFRASTRUCTURE AUTOMATION // STUDY NOTES PAGE 3

11. Modifying Infrastructure

Terraform is not only used to create resources. It can also modify existing infrastructure.

Example

Suppose your EC2 instance initially has the tag: Name = My Server. You change it in your Terraform configuration to: Name = My Web Server.

Modify .tf File→terraform apply→Terraform Detects Change→Resource Modified

Terraform identifies the required modification and updates the resource. The EC2 instance can remain running while the applicable property is changed.

12. terraform destroy

After testing or when the infrastructure is no longer required, you can remove resources using: terraform destroy

Terraform shows what it intends to destroy and asks for confirmation.

terraform destroy ↓ Review Resources ↓ Confirm ↓ Resources Destroyed

Important Use Case

This is particularly useful for temporary environments such as:

  • Testing
  • Development
  • Experiments
  • Training environments

Terraform's Major Benefits (13 - 16)

13. Consistency

Terraform allows infrastructure to be defined in configuration files. The same configuration can be reused multiple times.

Same Configuration ↓ Environment 1 Environment 2 Environment 3

14. Automation

Terraform is command-based, which makes it suitable for automation and scripting.

Script→Terraform→Cloud Provider

15. Cost Saving

Terraform can help with cost control when infrastructure is temporary.

Create Infra→Use→Destroy Infra

Note: Terraform itself does not automatically guarantee cost savings. It depends on your automation.

16. Repeatable Infrastructure

Terraform makes it easier to reproduce an environment.

Testing Configuration ↓ Reusable Terraform Code ↓ Production-like Environment

Reduces the need to manually recreate infrastructure.

INFRASTRUCTURE AUTOMATION // STUDY NOTES PAGE 4

17. Terraform State Management

One of Terraform's important concepts is state management. Terraform maintains information about the infrastructure it manages in a state file.

A commonly used local state file is: terraform.tfstate

Why is state important?

Terraform uses state information to understand the relationship between Terraform Configuration and Managed Resources.

18. Example of State Management

Suppose Terraform created an EC2 Instance with Name = My Server. Later you change the configuration to Name = My Web Server.

Terraform Configuration ↓ State ↓ Actual Infrastructure ↓ Determine Difference ↓ Apply Required Change

19. Local and Remote State

State can initially be maintained locally. However, Terraform also supports remote state storage.

This becomes particularly useful when Terraform is used by teams or in shared environments.

Local State OR Remote State

Terraform Features (20 - 22)

20. Variables

Variables allow configurations to become more flexible and reusable. Instead of hard-coding every value, you can define values separately.

Variable→Configuration→Different Values

21. Functions

Terraform provides functions that can be used to process and manipulate values within configurations. Functions help make configurations more dynamic.

22. Loops in Terraform

Terraform supports concepts that allow you to work with multiple similar resources. For example, if you need to create multiple user accounts, iteration features reduce repetitive configuration.

Input List ↓ Terraform Iteration ↓ Resource 1 Resource 2 Resource 3
INFRASTRUCTURE AUTOMATION // STUDY NOTES PAGE 5

23. Terraform Modules  |  24. Benefits

A Terraform module is a reusable collection of Terraform configuration.

Why use modules?

Suppose you create a complete configuration for a particular infrastructure component. Instead of copying the same code into multiple projects, you can package it as a module and reuse it.

Terraform Code ↓ Module ↓ Reuse in Multiple Projects

24. Benefits of Modules

  • Reusability
  • Better organization
  • Less code duplication
  • Easier maintenance
  • Standardized infrastructure
Key Idea: Write once → Package as a module → Reuse wherever required.

25. Terraform Workspaces

Workspaces can be used when you want to work with separate Terraform states for different environments while using the same basic configuration.

Terraform Configuration │ ├── Dev Workspace ├── Test Workspace └── Production Workspace

26. Terraform Cloud

Terraform Cloud is a managed service from HashiCorp that can make Terraform workflows easier to manage.

Local Setup

Developer↓Local Terraform↓Local Configuration↓Local State

Terraform Cloud

Developer / Team↓Terraform Cloud↓Terraform Operations↓Cloud Infrastructure

27. Terraform and Version Control

Terraform configuration files can be stored in version-control systems such as Git repositories.

.tf Files→Git Repository→Team Collaboration

This provides benefits such as: Version history, Collaboration, Change tracking, Review of infrastructure changes.

INFRASTRUCTURE AUTOMATION // STUDY NOTES PAGE 6

28. Terraform vs Manual Cloud Management

Manual Cloud Console Terraform
Resources created manuallyResources defined as code
RepetitiveReusable
More manual workAutomated workflow
Harder to reproduce exactlyEasier to reproduce
Configuration can varyConfiguration can be standardized
Manual cleanupterraform destroy
Difficult to automateEasy to script/automate

29. Terraform vs AWS CloudFormation

Terraform AWS CloudFormation
Open-source IaC toolAWS-native IaC service
Developed by HashiCorpDeveloped by AWS
Supports multiple providersPrimarily designed for AWS
Uses HCLUses YAML/JSON
Uses .tf filesUses CloudFormation templates
Uses Terraform stateUses CloudFormation stack management
Simple Memory Trick Terraform → Multi-provider IaC | CloudFormation → AWS-native IaC

30. Resource Lifecycle  |  31. Complete Workflow

Terraform │ ┌────────┼────────┐ ↓ ↓ ↓ Create Modify Destroy │ │ │ ↓ ↓ ↓ apply apply destroy
Write Config (.tf) ↓ terraform init ↓ terraform plan (Review) ↓ terraform apply (Create/Modify) ↓ Cloud Infrastructure ↓ Testing / Usage ↓ terraform destroy

32. Commands  |  33. Important Concepts

  • init Initialize project
  • plan Preview changes
  • apply Apply config
  • destroy Destroy infra

INIT → PLAN → APPLY → DESTROY

  • IaC: Infrastructure as Code.
  • HCL: HashiCorp Configuration Language.
  • Declarative: Define desired state.
  • Provider: Connects to cloud platform.
  • State: Information tracking resources.
  • Module: Reusable configuration.
